loc.INS_industrial_events.6.desc: The Cinchona Bureau has accepted our terms. With malaria ravaging half the tropics and no substitute for quinine in sight, they had little choice. The new agreement guarantees us a substantially larger share of the profits from every gram of quinine that leaves our shores. The question now is where to direct this windfall.
loc.INS_industrial_events.28.desc: The convoys have loaded the last of the rubber and put to sea. Our buyers will have what they paid for, and our books will reflect the agreed compensation in due course. For the next two years the cost of this transaction will sit on our balance sheets, a reminder of what the Depression demands of us.
loc.INS_industrial_events.36.desc: The tankers have departed our refineries, their holds bound for the buyer's ports. The compensation has been agreed and will be received in full, though the burden of the sale will weigh on our economy for two years to come. Such are the terms the world offers us in these lean years.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.2.desc: While the petition was approved by [INS.GetLeader], it was vetoed after being reviewed by [HOL.GetLeader], and we will therefore be unable to continue implementation at this time.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.2.a: Perhaps we can try again in the future with a ratified petition.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.10.t: Motion in the Volksraad to allow the Indonesian language in Schools
loc.INS_volksraad_events.10.desc: [INS.GetLeader] has approved a Volksraad petition to foster the creation of Indonesian-language schools and universities in [INS.GetNameDef], and it has been sent to [HOL.GetLeader] for final approval.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.10.a: The Volksraad is serving its purpose.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.11.desc: The petition has been signed by [HOL.GetLeader], and is now officially mandated. Implementation of the petition will begin shortly once final details are decided.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.11.a: The Volksraad is serving its purpose.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.20.t: Motion in the Volksraad to allow the Indonesian language in Government
loc.INS_volksraad_events.20.desc: Governmental roles in the Indies, including the Volksraad all require fluency in the Dutch language, which has led to many members of the Volksraad, especially representatives of native communities, to question the validity of its democracy. They have put together a motion which insists that government positions should be able to be filled by Indonesian speakers when possible.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.21.t: The Indonesian Language is now permitted in Government!
loc.INS_volksraad_events.21.desc: The petition has been signed by [HOL.GetLeader], and is now officially mandated. Implementation of the petition will begin shortly once final details are decided.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.30.t: Motion in the Volksraad to abolish the Education-Quota System
loc.INS_volksraad_events.30.desc: [INS.GetLeader] has approved a Volksraad petition to abolish the education-quota system in [INS.GetNameDef], in order to end the long-lasting arguments within the Volksraad over its implementation and fairness. It has been sent to [HOL.GetLeader] for final approval.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.31.t: The Education-Quota System has been abolished.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.31.desc: The petition has been signed by [HOL.GetLeader], and is now officially mandated. Implementation of the petition will begin shortly once final details are decided.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.40.t: Motion in the Volksraad to reduce export tax on Rubber
loc.INS_volksraad_events.40.desc: [INS.GetLeader] has signed and approved a Volksraad petition to reduce the high taxes imposed on privately owned rubber plantations. These taxes have historically allowed for a very lucrative government monopoly on rubber, however, international protectionism has made this a much less lucrative system. [INS.GetLeader] has stated he no longer believes the taxes make up for the economic consequences they cause.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.41.t: The private tax on Rubber Exports has been reduced.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.41.desc: The petition has been signed by [HOL.GetLeader], and is now officially mandated. Implementation of the petition will begin shortly once final details are decided.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.60.t: Motion in the Volksraad to lift the unwritten rank-limit on Indonesian officers
loc.INS_volksraad_events.60.desc: [INS.GetLeader] has approved a Volksraad petition to lift the unwritten rule that limits the rank non-Dutch KNIL officers can hold, and to promote Indonesian officers who are deemed underranked for their accomplishments. The petition has been sent to [HOL.GetLeader] for final approval.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.61.t: The invisible rank-ceiling on [INS.GetAdjective] Generals is lifted.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.61.desc: The petition has been signed by [HOL.GetLeader], and is now officially mandated. Implementation of the petition will begin shortly once final details are decided.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.70.t: Motion in the Volksraad to legalize public display of nationalist flags and imagery
loc.INS_volksraad_events.70.desc: [INS.GetLeader] has approved a Volksraad petition to lift the restrictions of displaying nationalist flags and imagery in public spaces in [INS.GetNameDef], largely in order to reduce the radicalization of many young nationalists. [INS.GetLeader] insists we should take a defensive stance on the issue, cooperating with peaceful nationalist leaders while rooting out revolutionary movements, however the decision ultimately rests with us.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.71.t: The Red/White Flag is no longer illegal to display!
loc.INS_volksraad_events.71.desc: The petition has been signed by [HOL.GetLeader], and is now officially mandated. Implementation of the petition will begin shortly once final details are decided.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.100.t: Motion in the Volksraad to allow education subsidies for non-Dutch residents
loc.INS_volksraad_events.100.desc: [INS.GetLeader] has approved a Volksraad petition to allow non-Dutch residents of [INS.GetNameDef] to apply for education subsidies. The petition has been sent to [HOL.GetLeader] for final approval.
loc.INS_volksraad_events.101.t: [INS.GetAdjective]'s are now able to apply for Education Subsidies
loc.INS_volksraad_events.101.desc: The petition has been signed by [HOL.GetLeader], and is now officially mandated. Implementation of the petition will begin shortly once final details are decided.
loc.INS_dutch_events.1.desc: Following the fall of our homeland, [INS.GetNameDef] has petitioned us to transfer command of our naval forces to [INS.GetNameDef]. They argue that a unified command will allow for better coordination during this unprecedented time.
loc.INS_dutch_events.1.a: If it strengthens the cause, we must concede.
loc.INS_dutch_events.1.b: Our ships will answer only to The Hague.
loc.INS_dutch_events.2.desc: [HOL.GetNameDefCap] has accepted our proposal to let us assume command of the combined naval forces. The transition is proceeding smoothly, and both [HOL.GetAdjective] and [INS.GetAdjective] officers are working side by side to strengthen our position in the Pacific.
loc.INS_dutch_events.2.a: Together, we will hold the Pacific.
loc.INS_dutch_events.3.desc: [HOL.GetNameDefCap] has declined our offer for a unified naval command, citing logistical and administrative concerns. While disappointing, our cooperation continues through other channels of the war effort.
loc.INS_dutch_events.3.a: We will find another way to strengthen our Naval influence.
loc.INS_dutch_events.4.desc: [HOL.GetNameDefCap] has announced the creation of the [HOL.GetName]-[INS.GetName] Naval Program, a joint initiative to reorganize and expand our maritime forces. [HOL.GetAdjective] expertise and [INS.GetAdjective] manpower will together form the backbone of a new Pacific defense network.
loc.INS_dutch_events.4.a: A firm step toward mutual survival.
loc.INS_union_events.1.desc: With the homeland lost, [HOL.GetNameDef] has informed us that their government and royal household will relocate to [1058.GetName]. They write of necessity, continuity, and the need to keep the Kingdom alive where the flag still flies.
loc.INS_union_events.1.b: Who do they think they are! This is nothing but an attempt at reasserting colonial dominance!
loc.INS_union_events.2.desc: [INS.GetNameDefCap] has agreed to host our government-in-exile in [1058.GetName]. Preparations for relocation are underway, and both administrations are coordinating the integration of offices and personnel. Together, we will carry the torch of the Kingdom forward from the East.
loc.INS_union_events.2.a: A united front against our common foes.
loc.INS_union_events.3.desc: [INS.GetNameDefCap] has outright refused our request to relocate to [1058.GetName]. [INS.GetLeader] stated we have no right to demand this level of aid when they are already spread thin enough as it is.
loc.INS_union_events.3.a: It seems they have forgotten whose banner still binds us.
loc.INS_union_events.4.desc: The first transports have arrived from the homeland. Ships crowded with officers, soldiers, and the remnants of our arsenals. As expected, some convoys did not reach port. What survives will form the spine of our forces in [1058.GetName].
loc.INS_union_events.4.a: Enough to keep the flag flying.
loc.INS_union_events.5.desc: It is clear to the world that the war is not looking in our favor. Our country has fallen and our base of operations has moved to the east. Ministers in [INS.GetName] have sent us a proposal to form a joint union state led by Queen Wilhelmina in order to guarantee as much cooperation as possible. While it seems nobody is particularly happy with the proposal, it may be our key for survival.
loc.INS_union_events.5.a: It is a risk we must undertake. Long live the Queen!
loc.INS_union_events.6.desc: After urgent debate within the cabinet, [HOL.GetLeader] has approved the [INS.GetAdjective] proposal. The decree is brief and without ceremony. Our governments shall act henceforth as one under the Crown until the war’s end.
loc.INS_union_events.6.a: A historic accord for both nations.
loc.INS_union_events.7.desc: The council in [HOL.GetNameDef] has turned down the proposal for a joint union. Their message is firm, cooperation will continue, but sovereignty will not be shared.
loc.INS_union_events.7.a: It is unlikely to have worked out regardless.
loc.INS_union_events.8.desc: It is clear to the world that the war is not looking in our favor. [HOL.GetNameDef] has fallen and their base of operations has moved to the east. [HOL.GetAdjective] leaders have sent us a proposal to form a joint union state led by Queen Wilhelmina in order to guarantee as much cooperation as possible. While it seems nobody is particularly happy with the proposal, it may be our key for survival.
loc.INS_union_events.8.b: This is all but an attempt at reasserting colonial dominance.
loc.INS_union_events.9.desc: [INS.GetNameDefCap] has agreed to our proposal. It is unclear how this will turn out, but we must keep our focus on the war effort.
loc.INS_union_events.9.a: If we are to endure, we must endure together.
loc.INS_union_events.10.desc: [INS.GetNameDefCap] has declined the proposal for union. The [INS.GetAdjective] people and leaders do not see this working out long term, and oppose any proposal of giving up power.
loc.INS_union_events.10.a: It is unlikely to have worked out regardless.
loc.INS_hey_btw_you_are_gonna_die_just_know_: §RThis will end the game for you.§!
loc.INS_revolution_events.1.desc: As expected, the Dutch government has reacted to our demand for independence by sending soldiers to [1058.GetName] and distributing anti-republican propaganda through the media.
loc.INS_revolution_events.2.desc: [HOL.GetLeader] has called an emergency meeting with our leaders, requesting that we provide further help in the reconquest of the Indies, to the extent of directly joining the conflict. [HOL.GetLeader] stated that the situation is dire, and Dutch forces are unable to push back the revolutionary militias. [HOL.GetLeader] promises that if we help them, we will be given Borneo as payment.
loc.INS_revolution_events.3.desc: [ENG.GetNameDefCap] has agreed to directly join the conflict, sending several divisions to fight in Batavia. While we will have to give up Borneo, this moves the odds heavily in our favor.
loc.INS_revolution_events.3.a: Borneo will be a necessary sacrifice.
loc.INS_revolution_events.4.desc: [ENG.GetNameDefCap] has refused any further help in the conflict, despite the urgency and reward offered. [ENG.GetLeader] stated that while it is in their best interest that we preserve our colonial empire, the risk of global escalation following their involvement is too high, and that we will need to handle this ourselves.
loc.INS_revolution_events.5.desc: Revolutionaries in the Dutch East Indies have declared independence from [HOL.GetNameDef] and occupied major cities. [HOL.GetLeader] has reached out to us with urgency, requesting that we help them militarily while they prepare an invasion.
loc.INS_revolution_events.5.a: If the revolutionaries succeed, citizens in our colonies may be inspired to do the same.
loc.INS_revolution_events.6.desc: [ENG.GetNameDefCap] has agreed to send volunteer troops and equipment to [1058.GetName] to help us take back control over the Indies.
loc.INS_revolution_events.7.desc: [ENG.GetNameDefCap] has refused to help us reassert control over the Indies, insisting that the Indies is not their concern, despite their proximity to the conflict. We will have to rearm the KNIL on our own.
loc.INS_revolution_events.8.t: Revolutionary militias plotting in the Indies
loc.INS_revolution_events.8.desc: Our Colonial Police in the East Indies have arrested and questioned several members of a rising revolutionary movement in Indonesia. It appears they are trying to establish a military presence in order to prepare for launching a national independence campaign. We do not know for sure yet, but they may be plotting an armed revolution.
loc.INS_revolution_events.9.desc: A Speech was given today in Java by [INS.GetLeader], declaring independence of the newly founded Republic of Indonesia. While we do not recognize this new republic, their militias have occupied territory and our police are failing to govern these areas. If we do not take this situation seriously, it may turn into all-out warfare.
loc.INS_revolution_events.9.b: This isn't worth the energy, if they want independence so bad, then so be it.
loc.INS_revolution_events.11.t: Indies Military Forces successfully stop Militia Campaign
loc.INS_revolution_events.11.desc: A team of Republican militias have launched a military operation to occupy [?event_target:INS_temp_occupied_state.GetName]. Our brave soldiers in the Indies successfully managed to push the militia forces out, and we maintain full control over the region.
loc.INS_revolution_events.12.desc: A team of Republican militias have launched a military operation to occupy [?event_target:INS_temp_occupied_state.GetName]. Our police and soldiers eventually managed to contain the situation, but the situation has sparked dissent within [?event_target:INS_temp_occupied_state.GetName], with many civilians supporting the militias and publicly speaking against the [HOL.GetAdjective] government.
loc.INS_revolution_events.14.desc: Despite the best efforts of our Colonial Police and Soldiers, Republican militias have successfully launched a military operation to occupy [?event_target:INS_temp_occupied_state.GetName]. Our police and soldiers have had to evacuate and have declared a state of failure to govern the region due to Militia resistance. If we let the militias continue to push us around, we risk losing our great Colony forever.
loc.INS_revolution_events.19.desc: [HOL.GetLeader] has been called to a meeting with [INS.GetLeader] in order to discuss a potential peace agreement. [INS.GetLeader] has stated that far too many lives have been lost, and has proposed a two-state-solution where borders will be kept as they are now, with slight adjustments, and for fighting to stop permanently.
loc.INS_revolution_events.19.a: We must agree. Too many lives have already been lost.
loc.INS_revolution_events.19.b: If you want peace so badly then you can surrender!
loc.INS_revolution_events.20.t: [HOL.GetNameDefCap] agrees to the two state solution!
loc.INS_revolution_events.20.desc: [INS.GetLeader] has returned from his meeting with [HOL.GetLeader] with good news. A two state solution has been agreed on by both sides, and we will begin moving our troops in accordance with the new borders immediately. While nobody is happy that we had to leave our fellow Indonesians behind, the decision to end the fighting is ultimately for the best.
loc.INS_revolution_events.21.desc: [INS.GetLeader]’s meeting with [HOL.GetLeader] did not go to plan, with both parties getting visibly angry and refusing to compromise, causing the meeting to be cut short.
loc.INS_revolution_events.21.a: How many more lives must be lost?
loc.INS_revolution_events.22.desc: [HOL.GetLeader] has called for a meeting with [FRA.GetLeader] in Amsterdam to discuss the ongoing situation in the Indies. During the meeting, [HOL.GetLeader] explained how the revolutionaries have begun arming militias at a pace the Dutch army cannot match, and that [HOL.GetNameDef] is at risk of losing their colonial hegemony. [HOL.GetLeader.GetHeShe] has requested that we formally join the conflict on the Dutch side, and send divisions to Batavia to help reconquer the Indies. In exchange, we will be entitled to northeastern Sumatra once order is restored.
loc.INS_revolution_events.22.a: While helping will be expensive, Sumatra might just make it worth it.
loc.INS_revolution_events.22.b: This is asking too much of us.
loc.INS_revolution_events.23.desc: [FRA.GetNameDefCap] has agreed to our call for help, and has sent many French divisions to Batavia to help us immediately.
loc.INS_revolution_events.23.a: The odds are now in our favor.
loc.INS_revolution_events.24.desc: [FRA.GetNameDefCap] has refused to help us with the revolution, despite the urgency. We must begin to rearm rapidly, or else we will soon be outnumbered.
loc.INS_revolution_events.25.t: The end of the war in Indonesia
loc.INS_revolution_events.25.desc: [HOL.GetAdjective] forces have destroyed the major militia bases and toppled the Republican government. Republican elite and commanders have been arrested, and the Indies government is reestablishing their operations in former-republic territory. As promised for our contributions, the agreed upon territory has been given to us.
loc.INS_revolution_events.26.t: The end of the war in Indonesia
loc.INS_revolution_events.26.desc: [HOL.GetAdjective] forces and Republican militias have been fighting for much longer than either side anticipated, and [HOL.GetLeader] has agreed to sign a peace agreement which imposes a two-state-solution. However, as we still held up our end of the agreement, [HOL.GetLeader] has confirmed we will still be given the territory which we were promised.
loc.INS_revolution_events.27.t: The end of the war in Indonesia
loc.INS_revolution_events.27.desc: [HOL.GetAdjective] forces and Republican militias have been fighting for much longer than either side anticipated, and despite the efforts of [HOL.GetNameDef] and our own military involvement, the sheer number of militia forces and the guerilla nature of their army has made the conflict reach a stalemate heavily in the Republican favor. Thus, [HOL.GetLeader] announced today that [HOL.GetLeader.GetHeShe] has signed a peace-agreement with the Republic imposing a two state solution in the Republican favor. What is left of the Indies is a shell of its former glory. [HOL.GetLeader] stated that as the conflict ended in a loss, he will be unable to give us the promised territory for our military contributions.
loc.INS_revolution_events.28.desc: Despite the heavy military spending done by [HOL.GetNameDef], and our own direct contributions to the conflict, the sheer number of militias in the Indies have managed to overwhelm our forces, and have occupied all major cities, toppling the Dutch administration and forcing a surrender.
loc.INS_revolution_events.29.desc: Despite our best efforts, the revolutionaries in the Indies have taken control of our major cities and have destroyed the colonial government from within. Our generals have been captured and our communications lines have been cut. We have no choice but to accept our defeat.
loc.INS_revolution_events.30.desc: [INS.GetLeader] has proposed a local ceasefire in [FROM.GetName], promising to withdraw his troops from [FROM.GetName] if we agree, allowing our troops to reassert control over the region. However, this is on the condition that we delay our major military operations temporarily, giving the revolutionaries time to plan.
loc.INS_revolution_events.30.b: We refuse, we will take [FROM.GetName] back by force!
loc.INS_revolution_events.31.desc: The ceasefire negotiations have gone well, with [HOL.GetLeader] agreeing to our terms. We have ordered the militia commanders in [FROM.GetName] to withdraw their forces immediately.
loc.INS_revolution_events.31.a: Hopefully they hold up their end of the agreement.
loc.INS_revolution_events.32.desc: The ceasefire negotiations did not go as planned, and [HOL.GetLeader] refused to sign the agreement and cut negotiations short before a compromise could be found.
loc.INS_revolution_events.33.desc: The Indonesian republicans have formally requested our assistance in brokering a settlement with the Dutch. Our advisors in the region report that the situation is deteriorating rapidly, and that continued Dutch military operations risk driving the nationalists into the arms of the Soviets. The Netherlands is a valued ally in Europe, but we cannot ignore the political realities in Southeast Asia. If Indonesia falls to communism because we stood idle, it will be our failure.
loc.INS_revolution_events.33.b: We cannot risk our relationship with the Dutch.
loc.INS_revolution_events.34.desc: Washington has agreed to mediate between our government and the Dutch. American envoys are en route, and a formal ceasefire will be proposed. This is an enormous opportunity. With the world's foremost power backing negotiations, the Dutch will find it far more difficult to stall or resort to force. We must hold firm at the table and let the Americans do what they do best.
loc.INS_revolution_events.34.a: Let us hope the Dutch see reason.
loc.INS_revolution_events.35.desc: The Americans have inserted themselves into the Indonesian question. Washington claims to be acting as a neutral mediator, but the implications are clear. If we cannot resolve this conflict to their satisfaction, they will use their considerable leverage against us. Our negotiators must tread carefully. American goodwill is not something we can afford to squander.
loc.INS_revolution_events.35.a: We will settle this on our own terms.
loc.INS_revolution_events.36.desc: The Americans have refused our request for mediation. Washington has chosen to stand with their European allies rather than support our struggle for self-determination. We are on our own. This is a bitter blow, but the revolution did not begin because we expected foreign powers to hand us our freedom.
loc.INS_revolution_events.36.a: We will win this war without them.
loc.INS_revolution_events.37.desc: The Americans have lost patience. Washington has delivered an ultimatum demanding the immediate cessation of all military operations in Indonesia and the recognition of Indonesian sovereignty. The threat is barely veiled. Our standing in the international community will not survive a public break with the Americans, and our economy cannot absorb the consequences. Our generals insist the campaign can still be won, but at what cost?
loc.INS_revolution_events.37.a: We have no choice but to comply.
loc.INS_revolution_events.37.b: Indonesia is ours. We will not yield.
loc.INS_revolution_events.38.desc: It is over. The Dutch government has accepted the American ultimatum and recognized our sovereignty. Three hundred and fifty years of colonial rule, ended not on the battlefield alone, but at the negotiating table with the weight of the world's greatest power behind our cause. The republic is ours, truly and completely, at last.
loc.INS_revolution_events.39.desc: Against all expectations, the Dutch have rejected the American ultimatum. Their generals must believe they can win this war before Washington acts. They are wrong. With the Americans now openly committed to our cause, the balance of power has shifted decisively. Let them come. We are no longer fighting alone.
loc.INS_revolution_events.40.desc: The Hague has accepted our ultimatum. Dutch forces in Indonesia will stand down, and sovereignty will be transferred to the Indonesian republic. It is a satisfactory conclusion to an unfortunate episode. Our interests in the region are now far better served by a stable, independent Indonesia than by propping up a colonial enterprise the Dutch could no longer sustain.
loc.INS_revolution_events.41.desc: The Hague has rejected our ultimatum outright. Dutch forces in Indonesia continue their operations in open defiance of American demands. This is an extraordinary miscalculation. The Netherlands cannot prosecute a colonial war in Asia and depend on American aid in Europe at the same time. They have forced our hand.
loc.INS_revolution_events.42.t: A Final Throw of the Dice
loc.INS_revolution_events.42.desc: Reports from our intelligence services in Batavia describe an enemy preperation unlike anything we have ever seen from the Republicans. It appears they are preparing a destabilization operation to storm Java and destroy all of our communications infrastructure, effectively guaranteeing their victory. However, this operation is extremely risky, and requires them moving nearly all of their resources toward it. Our generals estimate they are only able to hold this position for around two years, and cannot easily back out of it. If we hold them back for long enough, we will be able to crush their government and revolution like an overripe tomato.
loc.INS_revolution_events.43.t: Militia Base in [FROM.GetName] has been established
loc.INS_revolution_events.43.desc: Our efforts in [FROM.GetName] have been successful, and our local militia leaders have confirmed they are prepared to act when it is time.
loc.INS_chaos_events.1.desc: After the declaration of Independence, power in Surabaya has become unstable. Today, a group of Dutch loyalists raised the old colonial flag atop the former Hotel Yamato. Local pemuda youths stormed the building and removed the flags, raising the red-and-white Indonesian flag instead. The incident has escalated into violent, unorganized combat.
loc.INS_chaos_events.1.b: Order a ceasefire, we cannot risk escalation.
loc.INS_chaos_events.2.desc: The two largest Socialist parties in Indonesia, led by Amir Sjarifuddin and Sutan Sjahrir announced a merger today, forming a unified Socialist Party of Indonesia. This significantly increases the political influence of the party, potentially putting our administration at risk.
loc.INS_chaos_events.2.b: There is no time for politics, declare martial law!
loc.INS_chaos_events.3.desc: An attempt was made on Sukarno's life today by a Dutch soldier, who fired at Sukarno's car. Thankfully Sukarno was not in the vehicle, however his chauffeur was wounded severely. While this attempt was unsuccessful, it is clear this will not be the last attempt, both from Dutch soldiers and Indonesian opposition.
loc.INS_chaos_events.4.desc: A tragic day has befallen Indonesia today. Sukarno has faced another assassination attempt, this time successfully. We mustn't let a succession crisis come out of this, order must be restored quickly or the republic will collapse.
loc.INS_chaos_events.4.a: Vice President Hatta will take over.
loc.INS_chaos_events.4.b: The Socialist Party will take over.
loc.INS_chaos_events.4.c: Abolish the Republic, Tan Malaka will lead us to victory!
loc.INS_loyalist_events.1.t: [INS.GetLeader] requests a transfer of Henri Winkelman
loc.INS_loyalist_events.1.desc: [INS.GetLeader] has contacted us concerning the ongoing conflicts around the world and the dangerous position [INS.GetNameDef] finds itself in. [INS.GetLeader] has proposed that Henri Winkelman, former Commander of the Royal Netherlands East Indies Army be formally transferred back to [INS.GetNameDef], in order to ensure the security of the colony.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.1.a: We will arrange for his immediate transfer.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.1.b: Henri Winkelman is needed in the homeland.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.2.desc: [INS.GetLeader] has returned from [HOL.GetNameDef] where he met with [HOL.GetLeader]. The meeting went well, with [HOL.GetLeader] acknowledging the situation and agreeing to Winkelman's immediate transfer. Henri Winkelman is on his way to [1058.GetName] where he will await our orders.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.3.desc: [INS.GetLeader] has returned from [HOL.GetNameDef] where he met with [HOL.GetLeader]. Unfortunately, Henri Winkelman will not be sent to the Indies, and we will have to defend ourselves without him.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.3.a: We must figure out a new plan at haste.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.4.desc: An [FROM.GetAdjective] delegation has arrived in [ROOT.Capital.GetCapitalVictoryPointName] with a proposal for unification. They point to the shared Malay heritage of our peoples and note that the boundaries between our nations were established by European colonial administrators, not by the peoples who inhabit these lands. The proposal would see both governments dissolved and reformed as a single state.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.5.desc: Our diplomats have returned from [FROM.Capital.GetCapitalVictoryPointName] with excellent news. The [FROM.GetAdjective] government has accepted our proposal, and their officials are already making arrangements for the integration of their territories into our administration.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.6.desc: Our diplomats have returned from [FROM.Capital.GetCapitalVictoryPointName] empty-handed. The [FROM.GetAdjective] government was unwilling to entertain the proposal. Few reasons were given, and our delegation was sent home with little more than polite formalities.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.7.desc: [FROM.GetNameDefCap] has formally requested that we permit a referendum in [MAL.GetName] on the question of unification with their state. Their ambassador was forthright about the likely outcome, stating that the Malay people on both sides of the border consider themselves one nation. Permitting the vote would almost certainly mean losing [MAL.GetName].
loc.INS_loyalist_events.8.desc: Our overlord has granted [FROM.FROM.GetNameDef] permission to hold a referendum in our country. [FROM.FROM.GetAdjective] campaigners have arrived in force, and balloting is to begin within the month. The question put to our people is a simple one. Do we wish to join [FROM.FROM.GetNameDef], or do we wish to remain as we are?
loc.INS_loyalist_events.9.desc: The referendum in [FROM.GetName] has concluded. The [FROM.GetAdjective] people have voted to remain under our administration. The [FROM.FROM.GetAdjective] campaigners have departed.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.10.desc: The referendum in [FROM.GetName] has concluded with a decisive vote in favour of unification with [FROM.FROM.GetNameDef]. Our administrators in the region report that the result was expected. We are obligated to honour it.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.11.desc: The people of [MAL.GetName] have voted to join our nation. [MAL.GetAdjective] officials are cooperating with our administration to begin the transfer of authority. There will be one fewer border on the map of the Malay world.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.12.desc: Our proposal for unification with [MAL.GetName] has been turned down. The [MAL.GetAdjective] government, or those above them, have decided against it. We shall have to revisit the matter at a more opportune time.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.13.desc: The [FROM.GetAdjective] government has approached us with a proposal regarding Singapore. They request sovereignty over the island, citing its place within the Malay world. In return, they are prepared to guarantee our continued access to the port, its military installations, and all resource extraction rights currently in effect.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.14.desc: The deal has been accepted. Singapore will be transferred to our control, while the former controllers retain their commercial and military access to the port. Our flag now flies over one of the most important harbours in Asia.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.15.desc: Our proposal has been refused. The controllers of Singapore are unwilling to part with the island under any terms. We offered them everything short of continued sovereignty, and it was not enough.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.16.desc: The [FROM.GetAdjective] government has made a formal request for the transfer of Ceylon. Their diplomats cite long-standing trade and ethnic connections between the island and the Malay world. The claim is tenuous, to be frank, but [FROM.GetNameDef] has grown powerful enough that such requests must be given serious consideration.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.16.a: Very well, let them have it.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.16.b: Ceylon will remain under our control.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.17.desc: The transfer of Ceylon is complete. Our administration has begun moving officials to the island, and the handover has proceeded without incident. We now hold a position on both sides of the strait.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.18.desc: Our request for the transfer of Ceylon has been denied. The current controllers have no intention of parting with the island, and our diplomats report that further discussion on the matter would be fruitless.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.19.desc: [FROM.GetNameDefCap] has demanded that we permit a referendum in eastern Papua. On the [FROM.GetAdjective] side of the border, there are new roads running through the jungle, clinics staffed with government doctors, and schools teaching in the local languages. On ours, the last governor visited Port Moresby twice in three years. The [FROM.GetAdjective] ambassador did not need to say much more than that.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.20.desc: The Australians agreed to hold the referendum. Every district in eastern Papua returned the same result. Our investment in the western half of the island spoke louder than any campaign poster could have.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.20.a: The island is whole at last.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.21.desc: The Australians refused. Their governor in Port Moresby issued a statement calling the request an affront to Australian sovereignty. The Papuan people themselves were not consulted.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.22.desc: The [FROM.GetAdjective] government has issued a formal demand for the surrender of Eastern Timor. Their ambassador noted that our garrison there numbers fewer than two hundred men and that Lisbon has allocated almost nothing to the territory in years. He then asked what exactly we think we are holding onto.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.22.a: It is not worth fighting over.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.22.b: Timor is ours and will remain so.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.23.desc: The controllers of Eastern Timor have begun withdrawing their garrison and packing up the colonial administration. The entire island will soon be under [INS.GetAdjective] authority.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.24.desc: The colonial governor in Dili has personally written to reject our demand, insisting that Eastern Timor remains sovereign territory of his government. Our general staff has drawn up contingency plans should the cabinet wish to pursue the matter further.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.25.desc: An [FROM.GetAdjective] delegation has arrived with a proposal for the unification of our two republics. They argue that our peoples share common Austronesian roots far older than the colonial boundaries that separate us, and that a single state spanning the archipelago would be the foremost power in Southeast Asia. Accepting would mean dissolving our government and integrating into theirs.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.25.b: We fought too hard for this republic.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.26.desc: The [FROM.GetAdjective] government has accepted our proposal. Their officials are already coordinating with ours to begin the process of integration. From Aceh to Luzon, from Borneo to Mindanao, our nation now spans the full breadth of the Malay archipelago.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.27.desc: The [FROM.GetAdjective] government has declined. Their own struggle for independence is too recent, and too costly, for them to surrender their sovereignty to another state. The proposal has been shelved.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.28.desc: [FROM.GetNameDefCap] has formally requested that we permit a referendum in [PHI.GetName] on the question of unification. Their diplomats stress the shared Austronesian ancestry of both peoples and the artificial nature of the colonial borders separating them. If the vote goes ahead, the result is likely to favour [FROM.GetNameDef].
loc.INS_loyalist_events.28.a: The people should have their say.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.29.desc: [FROM.FROM.GetNameDefCap] has proposed the unification of our two nations on the basis of shared Austronesian heritage. Our overlord has granted them permission to hold a referendum on the matter, and [FROM.FROM.GetAdjective] campaigners have already begun arriving. The result will determine whether our republic joins [FROM.FROM.GetNameDef] or continues under its current arrangements.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.30.desc: The ballot boxes have been counted and the [FROM.FROM.GetAdjective] campaigners sent packing. The [FROM.GetAdjective] people voted to stay. Independence, it seems, still means something in [FROM.Capital.GetCapitalVictoryPointName].
loc.INS_loyalist_events.30.a: That is the end of it.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.31.desc: The ballot boxes have been counted. The [FROM.GetAdjective] people have chosen [FROM.FROM.GetNameDef] over us, and the margin was not close. Our administrators are already receiving instructions to begin the handover.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.32.desc: The [PHI.GetAdjective] referendum has concluded in our favour. Their government has accepted the result and initiated contact with our foreign ministry to arrange the transfer of authority.
loc.INS_loyalist_events.33.desc: The [PHI.GetAdjective] government has declined our proposal for unification. Their parliament voted it down without so much as a second reading. We offered them a place in the greatest nation in Southeast Asia, and they spat on it.
loc.INS_communist_events.6.desc: Our intelligence services have confirmed what we long suspected. [FROM.GetNameDefCap] has been conducting a sustained campaign of subversion within our borders, funding radical cells, distributing seditious pamphlets, and organizing strikes among the workers. Their agents have embedded themselves in the trade unions and rural cooperatives, and are now openly calling for the overthrow of our government. The situation has reached a critical point, and we must act decisively before it spirals beyond our control.
loc.INS_communist_events.7.desc: Troubling reports have reached us from [FROM.FROM.GetName]. Agents operating on behalf of [FROM.GetNameDef] have been stirring up revolutionary sentiment among the local population, exploiting grievances against our administration to build support for a communist takeover. If left unchecked, [FROM.FROM.GetNameDef] could be lost entirely to the radicals, and the rot may well spread further into our other holdings.
loc.INS_communist_events.7.a: We must stamp this out before it spreads!
loc.INS_communist_events.8.desc: Pamphlets and leaflets of [FROM.GetAdjective] origin have been appearing in our factories, markets, and universities with increasing frequency. They preach the gospel of class warfare and promise liberation through revolution, and our police report that they are finding a receptive audience among the discontented. The material is crude but effective, and its spread shows no signs of slowing.
loc.INS_communist_events.8.a: Find out who is distributing this filth!
loc.INS_communist_events.1.desc: The situation has deteriorated beyond recovery. Months of [FROM.GetAdjective] agitation have done their work, and the communist movement in [ROOT.GetName] can no longer be contained through ordinary measures. General strikes have paralyzed the cities, armed partisans hold sway over whole provinces, and the [FROM.GetAdjective] government has thrown its full weight behind the revolutionaries. Our security forces are stretched thin and their loyalty is no longer certain. We must decide now whether to fight for the survival of the state or accept the inevitable before more blood is spilled.
loc.INS_communist_events.1.a: Rally the army. We will not go quietly.
loc.INS_communist_events.1.b: Further resistance will only bring ruin upon our people.
loc.INS_communist_events.1.c: Perhaps if we grant them a seat at the table, we can still control this.
loc.INS_communist_events.2.desc: The government in [FROM.GetName] has refused to yield, and has ordered its armed forces to suppress the revolutionary movement by force. Our comrades there are already taking up positions and seizing key strongholds. The struggle will not be a short one, but the people of [FROM.GetName] have made their choice, and we shall see to it that they do not stand alone.
loc.INS_communist_events.3.desc: The old government in [FROM.GetName] has capitulated. Faced with the full scale of the revolutionary movement and the certain knowledge that [ROOT.GetNameDef] stood behind it, they saw no path forward but submission. Power has been transferred to the local communist party, and the new government has already begun reaching out to us for guidance. Another nation has been freed from the grip of the old order.
loc.INS_communist_events.3.a: A great victory for the working peoples of the world.
loc.INS_communist_events.4.desc: Communist revolutionaries, armed and organized with the backing of [FROM.FROM.GetNameDef], have launched an open insurrection in [FROM.GetName]. The colonial administration has lost control of large swathes of the territory, and the governor reports that the local garrison cannot restore order without reinforcement.
loc.INS_communist_events.4.a: Send in the troops. [FROM.GetName] is ours!
loc.INS_communist_events.5.desc: The administration in [FROM.GetName] has surrendered to the communist insurgents without a fight. The governor and his staff have been placed under arrest, our flag hauled down, and a revolutionary government proclaimed in its place. All of this orchestrated by [FROM.FROM.GetNameDef] and their agents, who have been working to undermine our authority there for months. This is nothing short of theft, and it will not go unanswered.
loc.INS_communist_events.9.desc: [FROM.GetAdjective] operatives have been spotted in the company of known agitators and militant leaders throughout the country. Student organizers who once handed out leaflets on street corners are now holding meetings behind closed doors with men carrying [FROM.GetAdjective] diplomatic papers. Banned publications are being printed faster than the police can confiscate them, and protests that once fizzled out in an afternoon now shut down entire districts for days. These communists are learning how to organize in larger groups every day, if we do not act fast we may lose control of them.
loc.INS_communist_events.9.a: Root out these foreign agents at once!
loc.INS_communist_events.10.desc: [FROM.GetAdjective] pamphlets have been circulating in the barracks and the civil service, and confiscation efforts have done little to stem the tide. They speak of nations unshackled, of peoples who threw off their colonial governors and built something of their own. It would be easier to suppress if the sentiment did not ring true. Even loyal officials have begun to ask, quietly, whether our present arrangement serves our people or merely our masters.
loc.taog_news.1.t: The Dawn of the Netherlands-Indonesia Union
loc.taog_news.1.desc: Queen Wilhelmina held an announcement in [1058.GetName] yesterday, announcing the unexpected creation of a Netherlands–Indonesia Union state. With the homeland under occupation, the [HOL.GetAdjective] government-in-exile and the [INS.GetAdjective] administration have agreed to govern as one body under the Crown. Officials of both countries describe the move as a measure of necessity rather than choice, a desperate effort to preserve the unity and authority of the Kingdom across two continents.
loc.taog_news.2.desc: [INS.GetAdjective] revolutionary [INS.GetLeader] held a speech in Java today declaring the independence of the newly formed Republic of Indonesia. [HOL.GetNameDef] does not recognize the sovereignty of this newfound republic, but Republican militias already hold de-facto control over certain territory.
loc.taog_news.2.a: This could set off a large shift globally.
loc.siam.1.desc: [SIA_phraya_phahon.GetName] stands accused of selling crown real estate to officials at below-market prices, a scandal that has significantly reduced his legitimacy in the People's Assembly. It seems that [SIA_phraya_phahon.GetName]'s influence is coming to an end.
loc.siam.1.a: Maybe this clears the way for someone else?
loc.siam.2.desc: A message from the Bangkok correspondent of Reuters reveals a third attempt in four years to poison the Prime Minister of Siam (Mr, Phibul Songgram)\nLast Week, it is stated, poison was mixed with food and temporarily affected Mr. Songgram and his wife and daughter.\nThe British Foreign Secretary (Lord Halifax) in a message to Mr. Songgram, expresses alarm at the cowardly attempt on the Prime Ministers life and pleasure at his escape.
loc.siam.3.desc: Phraya Songsuradet stands accused of being the mastermind behind one or more assassination attempts against [SIA_plaek_phibunsongkhram.GetName], as well as planning a coup against his government. It is the will of the government that Phraya Songsuradet is to be relinquished of his command,  his ranks and titles stripped, forced to retire from the military without pension and expulsion from the country.\nCritics claim that this is a thinly veiled purge, instigated by [SIA_plaek_phibunsongkhram.GetName] to remove his main rival, but that is clearly slander.
loc.siam.4.desc: In the early hours of the morning, with the help of the Royal Thai Police, the government has arrested 51 additional suspects and sympathizers, including Prince Rangsit, Phraya Thepahatsadin and Phraya Udom Pongphensawad. They stand accused of conspiring with Phraya Songsuradet against the state, with particular note that Rangsit, a member of the royal family is to stand trial. Some commentators wonder if the prince was specifically targeted to send a message to the royals left in [THIS.GetName], stay in line or fall.
loc.siam.5.desc: A special tribunal was created by Phibul to try the 51 people involved in the rebellion, out of which 25 are to be imprisoned for life, and 21 to be executed by firing squad. Out of the 21, three are to be pardoned due to their honorable records, namely Prince Rangsit and Phraya Thepahatsadin.
loc.siam.6.desc: Phraya Songsuradet stands accused of being the mastermind in one or more assassination attempts against [SIA_plaek_phibunsongkhram.GetName], as well as planning a coup against his government. It is the will of the government that Songsuradet is to be relinquished of his command and exiled.\nHowever, his arrest was prevented by military personnel loyal to Songsuradet, decrying the arrest as politically motivated. The government and Songsuradet's military clique are now at an impasse, both refusing to budge.
loc.siam.6.b: This has backfired. Let us back off.
loc.siam.7.desc: As the tense standoff between government forces and Songsuradet's military clique continues government investigators has started hearing rumors that an alliance between the Royal Navy and Songsuradet has formed with the explicit intent of countering Phibuns increasing authoritarianism.\nThat is not all, some aides of the Royal Household has reported representatives from Songsuradet meeting with high-ranking Princes, increasing fears that the Royals will also align with the opposition.
loc.siam.7.a: We are the government, we will not be blackmailed!
loc.siam.7.b: This is getting out of hand. Let's back off.
loc.siam.8.desc: Having secured enough support, both politically and militarily, the Songsuradet military clique in conjunction with the Navy has effectively taken over large areas of [THIS.GetName]. In the early hours gunfire rang out in the suburbs of Bangkok and the entire country seems poised for a full-scale civil war between the government and Songsuradet.
loc.siam.9.t: The End of the Songsuradet Rebellion
loc.siam.9.desc: The rebellion lies in tatters and with Songsuradet having been captured the trial is all that is left, although at this point it is merely a formality. Not only has the conspiracy been found in the army and navy, but in the Royalty as well, with Prince Rangsit having been found openly supporting the rebels. A deep purge of the dissidents has become a necessity, not an alternative.
loc.siam.10.desc: The enemy is routing, and our victory seems assured. With the territory firmly in control the old imperialist forces must be shaking in their boots. How could they lose? It is a sign of our divine providence.
loc.siam.10.b: Actually this is going quite well
loc.siam.11.desc: Against expectations, the [FROM.GetAdjective] military has outmaneuvered our forces and seized control of the contested region. Their occupation has weakened our authority and cast doubt on our claim to the area. Continuing the conflict risks further erosion of discipline and confidence, yet surrendering the territory would be a public admission of failure.
loc.siam.11.a: We must cut our losses and withdraw.
loc.siam.11.b: We will not abandon our claim!
loc.siam.12.desc: Our campaign has succeeded. Enemy resistance has collapsed, and [FROM.GetName] has formally relinquished control of the disputed lands to avoid further devastation. This victory elevates our standing and secures our borders—for now.
loc.siam.13.desc: [FROM.GetName] has dismissed all proposals involving territorial concessions, branding them unacceptable. Their leadership has declared that only the destruction of our state will end this conflict.
loc.siam.14.desc: [FROM.GetNameDefCap] has abandoned any pretense of negotiation. Their intent is clear: complete conquest and absorption of our nation. This war will not be decided by treaties, but by total victory or total collapse.
loc.siam.15.desc: The swift assault by the [SIA.GetAdjective] forces may have caught us off guard, but as their advance falters under mounting strain, their weakness is plain to see. What was meant to be a lightning campaign has become a grinding ordeal for the [SIA.GetAdjective] military. We could choose to be magnanimous and offer them a way out through concessions, yet the decision rests with us whether mercy serves our interests better than total victory.
loc.siam.16.desc: Our offensive has stalled, that is not the problem, the problem is that our enemy knows it. They have sent us an ultimatum, either surrender now with minimal losses, or continue the war with more bloodshed. The only difference is how many dead to bury.
loc.siam.17.desc: [FROM.GetName] has stated in no uncertain terms that it would rather see their entire country lit in flames than cede one single bit to us. The war continues.
loc.siam.18.desc: Intercepted communications from the enemy high command have confirmed our gravest fears, there will be no negotiated settlement, no concessions to bring this war to a measured end. They demand nothing less than the total capitulation of our nation, condemning us to life beneath yet another imperialist boot. If that is their aim then we have but one answer, we refuse to yield.
loc.siam.19.desc: [SIA.GetName], emboldened by growing nationalism and our perceived lack of strength in the region, has demanded the return of territories they deem core to their state. They are clearly trying to punch above their weight, but the territory they claim aren't necessarily worth fighting for with the world situation tumbling towards Armageddon.
loc.siam.19.a: It is not worth fighting for
loc.siam.20.desc: [FROM.GetName] has decided to hand back our territories, whether they recognize our sovereignty over these territories or if they are merely facing pressures from other actors are irrelevant, our cause remains just.
loc.siam.21.desc: [FROM.GetName] has refused our request. These imperialist cling to the last century with claw and chain, unable to admit to themselves that the sands of time for these so called \"great nations\"  has run out.
loc.siam.22.desc: Our Bureaucrats are ill suited for a modern economy, lacking the necessary training needed to drive growth. Fortunately there are plenty of countries with a modern, established bureaucracy, that we can send them to gain experience without importing their rule as well.
loc.siam.23.desc: The Baht cannot remain unmoored while [ROOT.GetName] seeks order in trade and finance. Our officials now argue that monetary stability requires a firm external anchor, one tied to a currency with the weight to reassure merchants, creditors and foreign partners alike. The choice before us is not merely technical. It will shape the direction of our trade, the character of our development and the foreign influence that comes to rest upon the [SIA.GetAdjective] economy.
loc.siam.24.desc: The [SIA.GetAdjective] Development Cooperative has given the state a new instrument for national improvement, but ambition still outruns domestic capital. Railways, workshops and electrical works demand outside finance if they are to rise with any speed. Now two paths stand before us. [ENG.GetAdjective] investment offers access to established markets, experienced firms and the financial prestige of London. [JAP.GetAdjective] investment promises closer industrial partnership with a rising Asian power eager to expand its influence. Either course may hasten development, though neither will come without obligations.
loc.siam.25.desc: King Prajadhipok is dead. The former King, whose name carried the memory of the old order through years of exile and upheaval, passes now from the affairs of men into history. For some, his death closes the final chapter of the struggle that began with the end of absolute rule. Yet the cause he came to embody does not perish with him. The throne endures, the dynasty remains and the work of restoring dignity and stability to [ROOT.GetName] must now continue in the name of the young King Ananda.
loc.siam.25.a: May His Majesty ascend to heaven.
loc.siam.27.desc: King Ananda remains in [SWI.GetName], away from the kingdom he is one day to rule. Distance, however, does not place him beyond our influence. Teachers may be chosen, subjects emphasized and habits encouraged, so that his mind is shaped toward the future we intend for [ROOT.GetNameDef]. Whether he returns as a soldier, a scholar, or something more, depends in no small part upon what he is made to study now.\n\nFor what is a King truly, if not the extension of the country?
loc.siam.27.c: Direct him toward administration and supply.
loc.siam.27.d: Educate him in industry and development.
loc.siam.28.desc: The long years of regency now draw to their appointed end. In Bangkok, before princes, monks, ministers and officers of the state, Ananda ascends the throne in his own right and receives the honors due to a Chakri king. The ceremonies proclaim continuity where there has been upheaval and sacred order where there has been strife. For the kingdom, this coronation is not merely a pageant but a declaration that the Crown endures, that the realm has not been broken by exile and civil conflict and that a new reign now begins over [ROOT.GetNameDef].
loc.siam.29.desc: Conventional tanks are still the kings of the battlefield, so we must learn from the best in order to create a powerful tank corps.
loc.siam.29.a: We will learn from the Germans
loc.siam.29.b: We will learn from the Americans
loc.siam.29.c: We will learn from the British
loc.siam.31.desc: The navy's expansion calls for a submarine arm, and we must decide where to source our vessels. Both [ENG.GetNameDef] and [JAP.GetNameDef] have made offers — but the choice carries implications beyond the shipyard.
loc.siam.31.a: The [ENG.GetAdjective] boats will serve us well.
loc.siam.31.b: We will build our submarine arm around [JAP.GetAdjective] designs.
loc.siam.32.desc: Our coastal waters require capable defense vessels, and we must choose our supplier. [ENG.GetNameDefCap] and [JAP.GetNameDef] both stand ready to deliver — the decision will shape both our fleet and our foreign relationships.
loc.siam.32.a: We will rely on [ENG.GetAdjective] vessels for our coastal defense.
loc.siam.32.b: We will rely on [JAP.GetAdjective] ships for our coastal fleet.
loc.siam.33.t: The Sale of Bangkok Dock Co.
loc.siam.33.desc: The sale of the Bangkok Dock Company has been completed, and the proceeds now sit in the treasury. The government must decide where these funds are best directed — whether to ease the financial burden on ordinary citizens, to accelerate the nation's technical ambitions, or to shore up confidence in the country's future.
loc.siam.33.a: Reduce the tax burden on our people.
loc.siam.33.b: Direct the funds toward naval research.
loc.siam.33.c: Use the windfall to reassure the nation.
loc.siam.34.desc: [FROM.GetAdjective] forces now press against [ROOT.GetNameDef], and their diplomats speak with the confidence of men who believe the matter already settled. They offer us the usual language of order and stability, yet what they truly seek is obedience. We may submit and preserve the state in diminished form, attach ourselves to their faction in hope of retaining some freedom of action, or answer this pressure with open defiance and order the invader from our shores.
loc.siam.34.a: We will join their faction and preserve our rule.
loc.siam.34.b: Tell them to get off our shores.
loc.siam.35.desc: [JAP.GetNameDefCap] has made its expectations clear: we are to increase the money supply to service their economic demands. The burden will fall on our own people through rising prices, while [JAP.GetAdjective] industry reaps the benefit. We have little room to refuse.
loc.siam.36.desc: [SIA.GetNameDefCap] has formally demanded we repay the costs incurred by the money-printing arrangement we compelled them to undertake. The arrangement served us well, but the bill has now come due.
loc.siam.36.a: Honor the debt and begin repayments.
loc.siam.37.desc: After our demands, [JAP.GetNameDef] has agreed to begin repaying the economic costs of the money-printing arrangement. The compensation will not fully undo the burden placed on our people, but it will bring some relief to the treasury.
loc.siam.37.a: A fair settlement. Our economy will recover.
loc.siam.38.desc: The [SIA.GetAdjective] government has come before us with an appeal for terms. Their ministers now concede what our guns have already demonstrated, that [ROOT.GetNameDef] holds the initiative in this struggle. We may accept their surrender and reduce them to obedience, bind them to our faction so that their government serves our wider cause, or reject all compromise and continue the campaign until Siam is fully overrun.
loc.siam.38.b: No. We will finish this by force.
loc.siam.39.desc: [FROM.GetLeader] has chosen to accept our submission. For now, [ROOT.GetNameDef] is spared further devastation, though not humiliation. The army is ordered to stand down and the government remains in place only by the sufferance of a stronger power. We preserve the state, but at the cost of pride and freedom of action.
loc.siam.40.desc: [FROM.GetLeader] has refused every overture sent from Bangkok. No submission is judged sufficient and no compromise acceptable. The enemy intends to settle the matter only through complete conquest. There is now nothing left for [ROOT.GetNameDef] but resistance. If they will not leave our shores by agreement, they must be driven off by force.
loc.siam.41.t: [FROM.GetNameDefCap] Sends Officials to Study Our Methods
loc.siam.41.desc: A delegation of [FROM.GetAdjective] officials has arrived to observe and study our administrative and research practices. [FROM.GetNameDefCap] appears intent on modernising its bureaucracy by drawing on foreign expertise, and has chosen [ROOT.GetNameDef] as its model. The visit is an implicit acknowledgement of our methods, and an opportunity to build goodwill with another government.
loc.siam.42.desc: [FROM.GetNameDefCap] has formally elected to anchor its currency to our own. The decision draws [FROM.GetNameDef] closer into our economic orbit and signals a degree of trust in the stability of our financial institutions. Trade between our nations should become more predictable, and [FROM.GetAdjective] merchants will find it easier to do business with ours.
loc.siam.42.a: A welcome development for our trade relationship.
loc.siam.43.desc: [FROM.GetNameDefCap] has extended an invitation for our engineers and specialists to assist in the development of their nation. The cooperative offers our industries a foothold in the region and strengthens the economic ties between our governments. It is a modest proposal, but one that may yield considerable returns over time.
loc.siam.44.desc: [FROM.GetNameDefCap] has placed an order for submarines built to our designs. The sale represents a meaningful vote of confidence in our naval industry and extends [FROM.GetAdjective] influence into the waters of Southeast Asia.
loc.siam.44.a: A welcome order for our shipyards.
loc.siam.45.desc: A delegation from [FROM.GetName] has arrived with a proposal from [FROM.GetLeader]. They argue that our separate alliances now pursue the same broad aims while dividing men, materiel and diplomatic influence between competing commands.\n\nBy merging our forces with theirs we would create a stronger bloc capable of coordinating strategy across a wider front. Such an agreement would strengthen the common cause, though it would also require us to accept [FROM.GetAdjective] influence over the future direction of the alliance.
loc.siam.46.desc: [FROM.GetLeader] has accepted our proposal to merge our alliances into a single coalition. What were once separate commands and diplomatic channels are now being folded into one structure, allowing our governments to coordinate war plans, supply arrangements and foreign policy with far greater clarity.\n\nThe arrangement is not without complications, but the necessity of unity has prevailed.
loc.siam.47.desc: [FROM.GetLeader] has rejected our proposal to merge our alliances. Their government claims that cooperation may continue where interests align, but they will not place their alliance within a broader coalition led from [ROOT.Capital.GetCapitalVictoryPointName].\n\nFor now, the division between our blocs remains. We must pursue our objectives without assuming their full commitment.
loc.siam.48.desc: [SIA.GetNameDefCap] has formally requested military aid against the forces invading their country. In return, the [SIA.GetAdjective] government is prepared to grant [JAP.GetAdjective] firms privileged access to strategic resources, infrastructure and commercial rights.\n\nSupporting [SIA.GetName] would expand our influence in Southeast Asia and secure valuable materials for the Empire, though it may also entangle us more deeply in regional conflicts.
loc.siam.49.desc: [JAP.GetNameDefCap] has agreed to support [ROOT.GetNameDef] in its struggle. [JAP.GetAdjective] advisers, equipment and supplies will soon begin arriving, while economic concessions have been granted to [JAP.GetAdjective] companies in accordance with the agreement.\n\nThough the cabinet celebrates the survival of the nation, many quietly wonder how much independence has been traded away for this assistance.
loc.SIA_japan_aid_request.4.desc: The government of [JAP.GetNameDef] has declined our request for military assistance. Tokyo claims that the Empire can not commit men and materiel to our struggle at this time.\n\nWithout foreign aid, [ROOT.GetNameDef] must now rely upon its own strength to survive the invasion.
loc.siam_adc.1.desc: A formal note has arrived from [FROM.GetNameDef], where [FROM.GetLeader] condemns our continued occupation of Asian countries as an intolerable affront to their right to self-determination. The message states that Asia is not a prize to be partitioned or administered at foreign pleasure, and demands that we immediately withdraw our forces and restore an independent government in [?var:SIA_adc_demand_country_to_be_released.GetNameDef].\n\nThe demand leaves no room for misunderstanding. [FROM.GetNameDefCap] expects compliance, and any refusal on our part is to be remembered as a deliberate insult to their nation.
loc.siam_adc.2.desc: Following [FROM.GetAdjective] acceptance of [SIA.GetNameDef] demands regarding the future of [ROOT.GetNameDef], [FROM.GetLeader] now places the final question before us. The occupation authorities are prepared to withdraw and recognize a sovereign [ROOT.GetAdjective] government, should we choose to stand alone once more.\n\nIndependence offers dignity and freedom of action, but it also leaves us to rebuild the state without the guarantees of [FROM.GetNameDef]. Remaining under their protection is a humbler course, yet one that may spare the country further disorder in these uncertain times.
loc.siam_adc.2.a: We will stand as a free nation.
loc.siam_adc.3.desc: The government of [?var:SIA_tag_that_was_released_due_to_sia_pressure.GetNameDef] has chosen independence. With the occupation administration now set to be dissolved, [var:SIA_tag_that_was_released_due_to_sia_pressure.GetNameDef] prepares to resume its place among the sovereign nations of the world.
loc.siam_air.1.desc: A Japanese technical mission has arrived with instructors, manuals, and the offer of aircraft. Our airmen must decide where their help will do the most good.
loc.siam_air.2.t: How Far to Push the Aviators
loc.siam_air.2.desc: Jungle flying is unforgiving, and green pilots are paying for it in wrecked aircraft. Do we press on and let the survivors become veterans, or ground the inexperienced until conditions improve?
loc.siam_adc.4.desc: Despite the opportunity to gain freedom, the government of [FROM.GetNameDef] has declined immediate independence. Their ministers argue that the state is not yet prepared to endure the burdens of full sovereignty and prefers, for now, to uphold the status quo.
loc.siam_adc.5.desc: [FROM.GetName] has made it clear that our demands are laughable at best. They point to our meager military as evidence that we are in no positions to challenge the status quo.
loc.siam_dem_event_count: The military is planning a campaign to smear longer we wait
loc.siam_dem.2.desc: At a private meeting of ministers and senior officers, a military representative has delivered a stern critique of the Yellow Dossier proposal. He argues that its authors speak too freely of state direction, redistribution and social obligation while giving too little regard to discipline, property and the burdens that would fall upon the officer corps and the countryside. In his view, [ROOT.GetNameDef] cannot be remade through theories drafted on paper while the world grows more dangerous by the month.
loc.siam_dem.2.a: The army has stated its case
loc.siam_dem.3.desc: The dispute has left the committee room. A newspaper widely regarded as a military proxy has printed a full denunciation of the Yellow Dossier, presenting it as an alien program dressed in patriotic language. Its editors warn that the proposal places class grievances above national unity, weakens confidence in established institutions and encourages dangerous expectations among workers and peasants. By the afternoon, the article is being repeated in barracks, offices and tea houses alike, and what had been an internal argument is now a public controversy.
loc.siam_dem.4.desc: Phibun has entered the quarrel openly and with unmistakable force. Speaking before supporters and officers, he condemns the Yellow Dossier as communist in substance, whatever language its defenders may prefer. He declares that any program which elevates the state above property, promises sweeping social transformation and stirs agitation among the lower classes carries the red poison into [ROOT.GetNameDef] by another name.
loc.siam_dem.5.desc: The old regime is broken and the Seri Thai stand triumphant. But triumph is not government, and the coalition that united against Phibun is far from agreed on what should follow him. Three names are spoken in the corridors of power: Pridi Banomyong, the conscience of the resistance; Khuang Aphaiwong, a man mild enough to offend no one; and General Phin Choonhavan, whose officers expect their due. Whom we raise up now will shape the peace to come.
loc.siam_dem.5.a: Pridi Banomyong shall lead. The resistance has earned it.
loc.siam_dem.5.b: Khuang Aphaiwong, a face all factions can accept.
loc.siam_dem.5.c: General Phin Choonhavan. The army will have its place.
loc.AST_election_events.1.desc.a: The votes are counted; the United Australia Party has won the election.\n\nThe UAP shall undergo a brief government formation period, before spending the next three years proving that the citizens' trust was rightfully placed on its representatives shoulders.
loc.AST_election_events.1.desc.b: The votes are counted; the Australian Labor Party has won the election.\n\nLabor shall undergo a brief government formation period, before spending the next three years proving that the citizens' trust was rightfully placed on its representatives shoulders.
loc.AST_election_events.2.desc:
The $AST_democratic_party_long$ has led [AST.GetName] since 1931, guiding the nation out of the Great Depression and away from anti-democratic sentiment. Through stable leadership, conservative leanings, and loyalty to Britain, the UAP has strengthened its support and made another term increasingly likely. Yet another party still has a say in the matter.

Still recovering from the no-confidence motion that removed it from power in 1931, the $AST_labor_party_long$ is beginning to regain momentum. With communist voices silenced, the working class now looks for another guiding light. In its mission to represent every citizen, the ALP has adopted a different perspective on imperialism and Australia’s loyalty to the Empire. Domestic needs shall come first, and foreign interests should no longer take priority.

One and a half years remain until the next federal election. If the UAP wishes to secure another victory, its leaders must accelerate reforms to preserve public support. Otherwise, ALP campaigning may restore its standing once more.
loc.AST_election_events.2.a: UAP shall enact its last reforms.
loc.AST_election_events.2.b: A campaign tour across Australia shall raise ALP support.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.1.desc: As part of its recent diplomatic endeavors, the Australian government seeks to sign non-aggression agreements with a few chosen Asian nations; we are one of them. Whether this attempt to avoid war exposes Australian officials as detached from reality, or if it paints them in honorable innocence, our response will partially decide.\n\nShall we sign a non-aggression pact with [AST.GetName]?
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.2.desc: The delegation sent to [FROM.GetNameDef] has cabled the nation's response to our non-aggression pact proposal. We knew the initiative was far-reaching, and so [FROM.GetLeader]'s refusal comes as little surprise.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.2.a: It was an honorable attempt, at least.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.3.desc: The delegation sent to [FROM.GetNameDef] has cabled the nation's response to our non-aggression pact proposal. Most pleasingly, [FROM.GetLeader] appreciated our initiative and has agreed to set his seal upon it.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.4.desc: [AST.GetNameDefCap] has long questioned the dependability of the Singapore Strategy; according to Australian officials, our ability to come to their aid in case of a Pacific war is uncertain. Transferring Pacific naval responsibilities to [AST.GetName] would lessen the burden on British shoulders, but it would also place that same burden upon Australian ones instead.\n\nCan we trust that increased Australian control would place our Pacific subjects and territories in a stronger position than if Singapore were to remain with us?
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.5.desc: Britain agrees to transfer Singapore to Australian authority. This will at last bring an end the outdated Singapore Strategy, placing us at the reins of our own defenses.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.5.a.tt:
§YSingapore§!:
  Is controlled by §YAustralia§!.
  Is owned by §YAustralia§!.
§YChristmas Island§!:
  Is controlled by §YAustralia§!.
  Is owned by §YAustralia§!.
§YCocos Islands§!:
  Is controlled by §YAustralia§!.
  Is owned by §YAustralia§!.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.6.desc: Britain refuses to transfer Singapore to Australian authority. The status quo will remain.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.6.a: The Singapore Strategy simply must hold.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.7.desc: [AST.GetNameDefCap] wishes to receive equipment from allies for its war effort, and requests our aid in managing the required shipments. Can we spare convoys to allow [AST.GetName] to make use of them?
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.8.desc: [USA.GetNameDefCap] has agreed to spare a number of convoys in order to aid [AST.GetName]'s supply efforts.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.8.a: They will be of great use!
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.9.desc: [USA.GetNameDefCap] has no convoys to spare for [AST.GetName]'s supply efforts.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.9.a: We must manage the shipments ourselves.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.10.desc: [AST.GetNameDefCap] values [USA.GetNameDef] allyship greatly and now requests that it be formalized in a common international wartime coalition. By joining forces, our two nations could assist each other in present and future conflicts.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.11.desc: [USA.GetNameDefCap] has agreed to join forces. As members of the [AST.GetFactionName], [AST.GetName] and [USA.GetName] will assist each other in present and future conflicts.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.12.desc: [USA.GetNameDefCap] has rejected our proposal to join forces. [AST.GetNameDefCap] and [USA.GetName] will remain divided in our respective war efforts.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.13.desc: During the process that united the Australian colonies into a federation, New Zealand ultimately decided not to take part. Ever since, however, the Australian Constitution has continued to define us as one of its Commonwealth's potential states, and does allow for our admission.\n\n[AST.GetName] now claims that the current world situation demands unity, requesting that [NZL.GetName] transfer to Australian authority. Shall we call a referendum on the matter?
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.13.a.tt: A referendum will be held, potentially resulting in the §Rannexation§! of §Y[NZL.GetName]§!
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.14.desc: Following the recently held referendum, [NZL.GetNameDef] has decided to invoke Clause 6 of the Australian Constitution. New Zealanders have agreed that their lands are more safe under Australian governance, and have therefore agreed to join [AST.GetNameDef].
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.15.desc: Following the recently held referendum, [NZL.GetNameDef] has decided not to invoke Clause 6 of the Australian Constitution. [NZL.GetNameDefCap] will remain as its own nation.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.15.a: Australia will remain as it is.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.16.desc: Despite Australian pressure, [NZL.GetNameDef] has decided not to hold a referendum to invoke Clause 6 of the Australian Constitution. [NZL.GetNameDefCap] will remain as its own nation.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.17.desc: The enemy is coming from the north, and it is only a matter of time before it arrives at our own doorstep, or so Australian officials claim at least. [AST.GetNameDefCap] proposes that we unite to form a single barrier, preferably by placing [INS.GetName] under Australian authority, but at the very least by granting military access.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.17.a: Agree to be placed under Australian authority.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.18.desc: [INS.GetName] has agreed to our request; our cooperation will have a great impact on both our nations' defense capabilities.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.19.desc: [INS.GetName] has refused our request; our nations will have to see to their own defenses.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.20.t: Summons to the British War Cabinet
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.20.desc: [GET_AST_BWC_COUNT][ENG.GetNameDefCap] summons the Australian Prime Minister to the British War Cabinet. The world situation is dire, prompting Britain to seek common strategies and military cooperation with its allies.\n\nHowever, Australia has its own concerns. Can we spare some of the Prime Minister's time in order to please the British?
loc.AST_bwc_count_2: For the second time, [ENG.GetLeader] requests [AST.GetLeader]'s attendance, claiming that our close cooperation is what will determine the outcome of our common struggle.\n\n
loc.AST_bwc_count_3: Yet again, [AST.GetLeader] is asked to cross the seas to maintain Commonwealth cooperation. Many more such requests are not expected, however, so long as we make clear whether our interests also lie with the common effort or in tending to our own affairs.\n\n
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.22.t: Successful Contributions to the British War Cabinet
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.22.desc: Over the past year, the Australian Prime Minister has regularly attended the British War Cabinet. Although [AST.GetNameDef] itself has had to pay the price at times, our nation has now grown stronger through British military cooperation.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.22.a: The cost was worth it in the end.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.23.t: [ENG.GetLeader] No Longer Seeks Australian War Influence
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.23.desc: [ENG.GetNameDefCap] has summoned the Australian Prime Minister to the British War Cabinet several times, but after repeated refusals [ENG.GetLeader] no longer sees any reason to continue doing so.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.24.desc: Australia's Prime Minister has had a great influence on the British Commonwealth's war effort. During his regular visits to London, Robert Menzies has won the trust of the British ministers while their faith in their own Prime Minister has faded. The ministers have now pressured the leader of [ENG.GetNameDef] to resign, and for Menzies to take his place.\n\nEven if [AST.GetName] loses their Prime Minister, they gain everlasting loyalty from their overlord, guarded by the Australian countryman now at Britain's reins. The land down under wants increased authority, and Robert Menzies is the first one to put his name to it.
loc.AST_diplomatic_events.25.desc: The rising tension among the Pacific nations is worrisome, and with Britain occupied in its own battles, our capacity to come to the rescue of our subjects appears implausible; or so [AST.GetName] claims.\n\nThey seek to reconstruct the British Commonwealth so that the nations of the Pacific and Indian Oceans are managed directly from Canberra. Shall we agree?
