loc.DESIGNER_REGIMENTAL_SUPPORT_COLUMN_TITLE: Regimental Support Companies. These are support troops attached to regiments.\n\nRegimental Support Companies do not affect the §YMax Speed§! of the Division (other than through terrain bonuses), and do not increase its §YCombat Width§!.
loc.DESIGNER_MAIN_COLUMN_TITLE: Line Battalions are your frontline troops.\n\nEach column is a Regiment of a specific base type like §YArmor§!, §YInfantry§! or §YMotorized Troops§!. The topmost type decides what else you can put in that Regiment column. The more Line Battalions you have the bigger your §YCombat Width§! and the fewer of these divisions you will be able to fit into the same battle.

loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_MOBILE_WARFARE_DESC: Hit them where they don't expect - mobile warfare doctrine seeks to break the trench deadlock of the First World War via aggressive maneuvers to pre-empt and disrupt the enemy.
loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_SUPERIOR_FIREPOWER_DESC: Send shells, not men - Superior Firepower emphasizes employing crushing masses of fire to pave the way for maneuver units to advance and capture territory.
loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_GRAND_BATTLEPLAN_DESC: With sufficient preparation, no obstacle is insurmountable - Grand Battleplan is characterized by patient, meticulous preparation of all arms, in both attack and defense.
loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_MASS_ASSAULT_DESC: Our willingness to sacrifice guarantees our victory - Mass Assault focuses on concentrating numerical superiority to force a breakthrough at the chosen time and place.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_MOBILE_INFANTRY_DESC: Focus our infantry on mobility to keep up the pace of advances and avoid getting bogged down in costly positional fighting.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_DEFENSIVE_POSTURES_DESC: A training and doctrinal emphasis on defensive tactics designed to stubbornly hold ground, inflicting casualties and delay upon the attacker.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_LARGE_UNIT_TACTICS_DESC: If we can master concentrated operations on a narrow front, we can create local superiority to overwhelm the enemy at the point of main effort and create a breakthrough.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_ASSAULT_INFANTRY_DESC: Organize the army with a combined arms approach to battle, with organic fire support assets integrated down to the smallest tactical unit.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_MOUNTED_INFANTRY_DESC: To update our cavalry for the 20th century, we need cross-country operational mobility while mounted, and to fight dismounted with fast, modern heavy weapons in support.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_COMMANDOS_DESC: Every Man An Emperor: Our troops need to be able to individually undertake difficult and demanding tasks, and carry their weight at all times. How we train them is vital for our success on the front.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_IRREGULARS_DESC: An asymmetric approach to infantry warfare in which direct combat with superior forces is avoided, using the guerilla tactics of ambush, misdirection, and harassment to wear down enemy resolve.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_GREAT_WAR_INFANTRY_DESC: A methodical approach to infantry fighting, featuring attacks with limited objectives followed by rapid entrenchment to tenaciously hold the won ground.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_FIRE_CONCENTRATION_DESC: By centralizing control of fire support assets, our army can concentrate firepower at the critical point rather than frittering it away in small packets.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_ANTI_TANK_FRONT_DESC: A unified approach to anti-tank defense at all tactical echelons, defending the flanks of friendly breakthroughs and channeling enemy armored attacks into pre-planned kill zones.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_FLYING_BATTERIES_DESC: An army-wide initiative to increase the mobility of supporting arms so they can keep pace with rapid motorized advances, and go into action quickly in support.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_AIR_CAVALRY_DESC: The helicopter offers the radical possibility of introducing the third, vertical dimension into land warfare. We can configure the army to exploit this new approach for maximum mobility and surprise.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_MOBILE_RECON_AND_ASSAULT_DES: With a combined arms approach backed up by extensive motorization, we can use reconnaissance units to find the enemy, and mobile heavy weapons to rapidly smash them.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SELF_PROPELLED_SUPPORT_DESC: Securing tracked mobility and protection for as much the army's heavy support weapons as possible: the way of the future.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SIEGE_ARTILLERY_DESC: No fixed fortification can stand for long against a steel rain of battleship-caliber shells.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_FIELD_ENGINEERING_DESC: The role of military engineers is to build bridges and lay mines, as well as destroy similar works of the enemy. With the right equipment, training, and a willingness to spill sweat to spare blood, we can dominate the modern battlefield.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_DISPERSED_OPERATIONS_DESC: When the skies belong to the enemy, our armies must refuse to present an easy target. Dispersed formations, hardened logistics, and dense anti-aircraft fire let us fight on where we cannot contest the air.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_ARMORED_SPEARHEAD_DESC: The tank offers the opportunity to create a war of movement rather than mere attrition. Our doctrine should emphasize rapid exploitation of breakthroughs to surround and destroy the enemy.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_ARMORED_INFANTRY_SUPPORT_DES: With their firepower and protection, tanks can rapidly knock out machine guns and other weapons that hinder the advance of the infantry. Tank-Infantry cooperation must be seamless.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_ARMORED_CAVALRY_DESC: Mechanized forces backed up by fast light tanks and armored cars can probe for weak spots and hit the enemy where they are most vulnerable.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_STREAMLINED_DEPLOYMENT_DESC: Offensive results on the strategic scale can only be achieved when all arms, including tanks, are massed to concentrate their striking power at the decisive point.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_MOBILE_DEFENSE_DESC: Armored forces are useful in defense as well as attack. With their mobility they can rapidly occupy strong defensive terrain, or move in to position to counter enemy breakthroughs.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_TANK_DESTROYER_FORCE_DESC: When faced with major enemy armored threats, we cannot count on our first line defenses always stopping the foe. Defense in depth by ambushing anti-tank units is essential.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_MISSION_TYPE_TACTICS_DESC: Our leaders should not be automatons. They must interpret their orders intelligently, and diverge from strict adherence to them if it accomplishes the mission. Victory is more important than blind obedience.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_LAST_STAND_DESC: When our backs are to the wall, and national survival is at stake, the only option is bitter, fanatical resistance by the entire population, turning every field, street and town into a battleground.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_INFILTRATION_TACTICS_DESC: Rather than bashing against enemy lines at their strongest point, we shall flow around them like water, maintaining offensive momentum and forcing the enemy to withdraw through threat of encirclement.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_GRAND_ASSAULT_DESC: Building upon hard-earned lessons from the First World War, we shall adopt a deliberate and methodical approach to pre-battle planning. Then, when every advantage has been leveraged, we fall upon the enemy like an avalanche.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_DEEP_BATTLE_DESC: The range and striking power of modern arms allows an enemy defense system to be overcome by striking it to its whole depth, simultaneously, with every weapon at our disposal.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_GUERILLA_WAR_DESC: Wear down a superior enemy through constant low-level attacks on his lines of communication, eroding his will to continue the fight. Avoid major set-piece battles to preserve our own limited forces.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_PEOPLES_WAR_DESC: The will of the people to resist, mobilized and guided by the state, guarantees our eventual victory over imperialism and counter-revolution.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_RAPID_DOMINATION_DESC: Asserting full-spectrum dominance over the enemy makes their further resistance physically and psychologically impossible.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_EXPEDITIONARY_WARFARE_DESC: All the combat power in the world means little if it cannot get to the fight. We shall create an organizational emphasis on force projection capability in service of our strategic aims.

loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_FLEET_IN_BEING_DESC: The Big Gun Club - A traditionalist focus on naval artillery and heavy armor, to overwhelm the enemy fleet and drown them in a storm of steel.
loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_CONVOY_RAIDING_DESC: Privateers for the modern age - An indirect approach to naval warfare focused on strangling maritime trade, starving the enemy of resources they need to fight the war.
loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_BASE_STRIKE_DESC: Hit hard, hit first - The new technologies of naval aviation offer the intriguing possibility of striking the enemy from beyond the horizon, before he knows he is fighting.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_LINE_OF_BATTLE_DESC: With our grand fleet in line astern and broadsides roaring, we will demonstrate that big guns still rule the waves.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_BATTLECRUISER_SUPREMACY_DESC: In a world where everyone has big guns, fast capital ships offer the ability to pick fights we want, and run from ones we don't.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_ARMORED_RAIDERS_DESC: Convoy escorts primarily focus on anti-submarine defense. Imagine their shock when a fully-armed capital ship appears in their midst, like a wolf among sheep.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_COASTAL_DEFENCE_DESC: Smaller warships, prioritizing firepower over range and operating close to friendly shores, can prove a considerable deterrent to a hostile fleet.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_NAVAL_GUNFIRE_SUPPORT_DESC: Once the enemy battle fleet is neutralized, our heavy naval guns are free to turn their wrath on land targets, to support our troops ashore.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_BATTLESHIP_ANTIAIR_SCREEN_DE: Battleships offer unrivaled opportunity for deck armaments. Equipping them to target enemy aircraft should be a priority to keep the skies clear for our task forces.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SCREEN_CONVOY_ESCORT_DESC: The chief duty of light ships is to secure the maritime trade upon which all our war efforts depend. Everything else is secondary.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SCREEN_INTEGRATED_OPERATIONS: Screening forces lack the firepower of capital ships, but using speed as armor, they can provide valuable service even in a pitched naval battle.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SCREEN_HUNTER_KILLERS_DESC: While enemy submarines threaten to strangle our war economy, well-organized and aggressive destroyer escorts can turn the hunter into the hunted.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SCREEN_TORPEDO_PRIMACY_DESC: An emphasis on aggressive, daring destroyer torpedo attacks in favor of defensive screening, to wear down the enemy battleline before the main engagement.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SCREEN_ANTI_AIRCRAFT_CRUISER: Light cruisers lack the staying power to stand in the line of battle, but they can be crammed with high-angle weapons and provide powerful AA protection for the fleet.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SCREEN_SUPPORT_FOCUS_DESC: Improvements to the training and organization of our support ship apparatus will indirectly but dramatically strengthen our main battle fleet.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SCREEN_JEUNE_ECOLE_DESC: A doctrinal concept emphasizing swarms of small ships, torpedo strikes, and indirect commerce warfare as an antidote to the old notion of a big gun slugging match on the high seas.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SCREEN_PATROL_BOATS_DESC: Cheap fast attack craft armed with torpedos are a powerful tool against a traditional battle fleet of heavy ships, particularly in coastal waters where they can strike from ambush.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_CARRIER_BATTLEGROUPS_DESC: The carrier is rapidly eclipsing the battleship as the chief naval weapon of our age. Our fleets should be centered around them.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_CARRIER_AIRFIELDS_DESC: A carrier deck is the most expensive piece of real estate on Earth. No effort must be spared in eking out the maximum amount of possible air power from it.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_ESCORT_CARRIER_SUPPORT_DESC: Small, economical escort carriers grant our convoys defensive air cover all the way to their destination. No enemy submarine may strike with impunity.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_BROAD_NAVAL_SUPPORT_DESC: With reconnaissance, air superiority, and strike capability all in one package, carriers are an invaluable Jack-of-all-trades tool in the hands of the task force commander.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_MASSED_CARRIER_FLEET_DESC: Just as much as on land, success in naval combat depends on concentrating as much striking power as possible at the single decisive point. Division breeds defeat.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_LIGHT_TASK_FORCES_DESC: Carriers are powerful, but vulnerable in direct combat. For them to deliver their payloads and contribute to victory, they must first be survivable.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SUBMARINE_WOLFPACKS_DESC: Hunt dispersed - strike in unison. Our submarines can spread out to cover vast stretches of ocean, then signal each other to converge when suitable prey is spotted.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SUBMARINE_FLEET_OPERATIONS_D: Mass integration of submarines in to the main battle fleet, to provide reconnaissance and ambush enemy ships during a general engagement.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SUBMARINE_CAPITAL_HUNTERS_DE: The proper role of the submarine in modern war is to avoid the distraction of lesser prey, and focus on sinking enemy capital ships above all else.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SUBMARINE_COASTAL_DEFENSE_DE: Small submarines operating close to shore can prove a consistent thorn in the side of a would-be invader.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SUBMARINE_COASTAL_MINELAYING: With their stealth and agility, submarines are an ideal platform from which to seed the sea lanes with mines and restrict enemy freedom of movement.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_SUBMARINE_LONG_RANGE_SUBMARI: When our fleets operate at extreme ranges our submarines need to be able to follow, in order to provide full support to our surface task forces.

loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_DESCRIPTION: The cornerstone of our military strategy, the Grand Doctrine shapes our overall approach to warfare.
loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_BENEFIT_DESCRIPTION: §gAssign a Grand Doctrine to make available a set of §HSubdoctrine§! tracks. Develop your Subdoctrines by earning £doctrine_mastery §HMastery§! from units in combat. Completed Subdoctrines activate §HMilestones§!, further elevating your Grand Doctrine.§!
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_DESCRIPTION: Through a Subdoctrine, we specialize and perfect our approach to warfare within a particular field.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_BENEFIT_DESCRIPTION: §gAssigning a Subdoctrine enables§! £doctrine_mastery §HMastery§!§g to be gained in this track. Upon reaching certain mastery thresholds, the Subdoctrine unlocks additional effects.§!
loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_STRATEGIC_DESTRUCTION_DES: Mass bombing of factories, refineries, and transport infrastructure deep in the enemy's hinterland, to cut off his warmaking potential at the source.
loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_BATTLEFIELD_SUPPORT_DESC: Techniques and training for close army-air force cooperation, with air strikes acting as flying artillery to blast a path for fast-moving ground operations.
loc.GRAND_DOCTRINE_OPERATIONAL_INTEGRITY_DES: Gaining and maintaining air superiority, as a prerequisite for domination of the battlespace by general purpose medium bombers carrying out operational strikes.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_ESCORT_FIGHTER_DESC: For our strike aircraft to operate with impunity, it is necessary that they be closely supported by fighters to sweep the skies of hostile aircraft.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_FIGHTER_HOMELAND_DEFENSE_DES: In order to prosecute the war effectively, our industry and infrastructure must be shielded from strategic bombardment at any cost.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_FIGHTER_BOMBERS_DESC: When not needed to combat enemy aircraft, our fighters can switch focus to strikes on ground targets to assist the army.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_TACTICAL_FLEXIBILITY_DESC: A focus on offensive air-to-air combat tactics designed to seize control of the skies.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_DOGFIGHTING_MASTERY_DESC: Almost uniquely in modern warfare, a fighter pilot fights alone. We must ensure the individual excellence of every pilot.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_FIGHTER_CENTRAL_FIELD_DESC: Air power is the dominant weapon of the age, and the aircraft carrier allows its devastating striking potential to have a global reach.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_FLYING_ARTILLERY_DESC: A generalist approach to strike prioritization, engaging targets of opportunity from the front line all the way out to operational depth.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_DIVE_BOMBERS_DESC: Air strikes on front line targets during an active land battle exposes aircraft to ground fire and can be risky for friendly troops, but the effects at the sharp end are dramatic.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_CARRIER_STRIKES_DESC: Almost all the world's industry and warmaking potential is within airstrike range of a coastline. Our carriers can put air power in the enemy's backyard.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_FLEXIBLE_FIRE_SUPPORT_DESC: With their speed and range, our strike craft can perform versatile double-duty supporting the army on land, or attacking enemy vessels at sea.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_NAVAL_STRIKE_TACTICS_DESC: Carrier aircraft must run a gauntlet of enemy fighters and AA to deliver their payloads. Our training will emphasize survivability and tenacity in pressing home the attack.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_NAVAL_TORPEDO_TACTICS_DESC: A few torpedos can be evaded. Dozens of them all at once can lay the most hardened target low through sheer volume.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_BOMBER_INTERCEPTION_DESC: Although their lack of agility can be a drawback against lighter aircraft, heavy fighters can carry destructive anti-bomber firepower.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_LONG_RANGE_ESCORT_DESC: Unescorted daylight bombing of the enemy homeland will incur ruinous losses. We need fighters with the range to accompany our bombers all the way there, and all the way back.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_OPERATIONAL_AIR_SUPPORT_DESC: A doctrine focused on dominating the operational battle area via persistent attacks by highly survivable medium aircraft.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_TACTICAL_BATTLEFIELD_SUPPORT: A fleet of light bombers raining devastation from the sky upon hostile strong points, paving the way for the advance of our own troops.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_THEATER_INTERDICTION_DESC: Freed from the risk of hitting friendly troops, our bomber fleet can range unhindered in the enemy's rear areas, sowing havoc and aiding the fighting fronts indirectly.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_AERIAL_RECONNAISSANCE_DESC: The oldest form of military aviation is reconnaissance. In this, as in every age, knowing where the enemy is and what he is up to can be more powerful than any weapon.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_NIGHT_BOMBING_DESC: Contrary to Douhet, the bomber does not, in fact, always get through. Flying at night reduces our accuracy, but vastly improves the survival rate of our planes and crews.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_CARPET_BOMBING_DESC: Trying to strike point targets from 30,000 feet is generally a waste of bombs. Flying in line abreast and creating a wide lane of destruction is a more reliable way to hit...something.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_DEEP_AIR_RAIDS_DESC: With the right equipment and training, there is no target too deep in the enemy's hinterland to be struck. The enemy will come to know that no place is safe from our bombs.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_FLYING_FORTRESSES_DESC: Large groups of bombers, flying in close formation and with heavy defensive armament, can force any attacking fighter to brave the fire of dozens of guns at once.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_COASTAL_AIR_PATROL_DESC: Traditional sea-level means of coastal defense are manpower-intensive and inefficient. Aerial mobility means we can keep an eye on friendly shores and punish any would-be invader.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_OPEN_OCEAN_AIR_PATROL_DESC: The range of modern aircraft allows for naval search and strike missions against enemy assets well before they threaten our coasts.
loc.SUBDOCTRINE_HEAVY_AIRCRAFT_FOCUS_DESC: The size and carrying capacity of large airframes gives them an unparalleled ability to carry a wide variety of mission-specific equipment for any military situation.

loc.YUG_instigate_in_bulgaria_desc: Almost the entirety of the South-Slavic workers have been freed by our state, all except the Bulgarians. Only by encouraging the Bulgarians to rise up against their oppressors can we truly claim to have liberated the Slavic workers of the Balkans.
loc.YUG_instigate_in_albania_desc: While the Albanian people do not identify as Slavic themselves, their closeness to our border and the cultural exchange between Albanians and South-Slavs makes them an ideal candidate to join the Pan-Slavic Worker’s Congress.
loc.YUG_propaganda_in_target_desc: Our target has been selected, all we need do now is supply our socialist allies with effective propaganda and soon enough we will have sewn the seeds of rebellion necessary to overthrow the upper classes of the Balkans.
loc.YUG_arm_communist_militants_desc: We cannot bring the revolution to our comrades across the border with words alone. We must provide our allies with the arms they need to overthrow their masters.
loc.YUG_communist_coup_desc: They have prepared long enough, all we need do now is give the militants across our borders our approval and they will attempt to stage a coup on their corrupt capitalist government!
loc.YUG_abandon_communist_effort_desc: It’s clear that the people of [YUG_communist_coup_target.GetNameDef] are not yet ready to free themselves from the confines of their government and we must abandon our efforts to instigate a communist coup in their nation.
loc.YUG_uprising_strength_tt: With their current support, the strength of the §YCommunists§! will be [YUG_communist_coup_target.Get_Yugo_Uprising_strength].\nThis is based on their current §YCommunist§! support and the number of times the peasants have been armed.
loc.no_other_country_claimed_tt: No other country invited to split Yugoslavia has a claim on §Y[This.GetName]§!
loc.ROM_change_sides_to_allies_desc: Changes in our government have facilitated a change in our alignment in the war. By joining with the Allies, our current “comrades” in this global conflict shall become confused as Romanian bullets find a new target.
loc.ROM_change_sides_to_commintern_desc: Changes in our government have facilitated a change in our alignment in the war. By joining with the Communist International, our current “comrades” in this global conflict shall become confused as Romanian bullets find a new target.
loc.ROM_change_sides_to_axis_desc: Changes in our government have facilitated a change in our alignment in the war. By joining with the Axis, our current “comrades” in this global conflict shall become confused as Romanian bullets find a new target.
loc.DOD_hungary.1.desc: in a speech in Budapest, [HUN.GetLeader] has demanded that his Austrian subjects be permitted to return to his rule. In a gesture of reconciliation, however, he has publicly noted that the Austrian people should be permitted to make that choice for themselves.
loc.DOD_hungary.1.a: Let the people have their say.
loc.DOD_hungary.1.b: Such things should be left to professionals.
loc.DOD_hungary.1.c: We will ensure the right results.
loc.DOD_hungary.2.desc: The results of the Referendum are in, and the preliminary count shows a significant majority for Union with Hungary.
loc.DOD_hungary.3.desc: Despite a well-orchestrated campaign by pro-Hungarian groups and monarchists, preliminary results show a small majority for maintaining the status quo.
loc.DOD_hungary.4.desc: Shortly after midnight, [AUS.GetLeader] announced that the Austrian people had voted for a union with Hungary. A telegram has arrived, formally offering [HUN.GetLeader] the crown of Austria in a first step to revive the double monarchy.
loc.DOD_hungary.5.desc: Despite our best efforts, the people of Austria have decided to keep the status quo.
loc.DOD_hungary.5.a: We must liberate the country and return it to its rightful ruler.
loc.DOD_hungary.6.desc: Austrian leader [AUS.GetLeader] has publicly declared that the entire country is united in their opposition to the Habsburgs, and that the very idea of a referendum on Austrian independence is utterly absurd.
loc.DOD_hungary.6.a: We shall see how united they really are.
loc.DOD_hungary.7.desc: The Hungarian offer of a referendum has put us in a tight spot internationally. We can't be seen to deny the people a choice, but we can't trust them to make the right one. Thankfully, there are ways and means to solve the issue. What result do we want from the referendum?
loc.DOD_hungary.10.desc: With the recent, dramatic shifts in the political landscape of the Balkans, the question of our relationship with the new Austro-Hungarian Empire has come up repeatedly. Today, the Hungarian ambassador has handed over an official note, formally requesting that we declare our position towards the Empire. The Habsburgs claim that, as old crown lands, Bohemia and Moravia belong to them. \n\nHowever, [HUN.GetLeader] has indicated that he would accept a compromise solution, with himself nominally head of state of our country, but with very little real power.
loc.DOD_hungary.10.a: We shall return to the Empire.
loc.DOD_hungary.10.c: We will never give up our freedom for safety!
loc.DOD_hungary.11.desc: Following discussion at the highest level that ran late into the night, the [CZE.GetAdjective] government has decided to accept our offer and proclaimed [HUN.GetLeader] the King of Bohemia and Margrave of Moravia. The soldiers of the former Czech Army have sworn an oath to their new King and Emperor, and the civil administration of the realms has been fully integrated.
loc.DOD_hungary.11.a: Another step on the way to reclaim our birthright.
loc.DOD_hungary.12.desc: Treading a careful balance between the republican and the monarchist factions in his government, [CZE.GetLeader] has opted for a compromise solution. [HUN.GetLeader] will be declared King of Bohemia and Moravia, but the [CZE.GetAdjective] constitution will limit his powers to only act with the advice and consent of parliament.
loc.DOD_hungary.13.desc: [CZE.GetNameDefCap] has refused to entertain any kind of settlement or agreement concerning their future relationship with us. When our ambassador arrived at the foreign office to discuss the official note he had delivered earlier, he was told that there was nothing to talk about, and quickly shown out the door. The [CZE.GetAdjective] ambassador to our government has declared that, while his government wants a peaceful and friendly relationship between our nations, there is no possibility of incorporating [CZE.GetNameDef] into the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
loc.DOD_hungary.20.desc: Following the outbreak of war in Hungary, the question of supporting them has come up repeatedly. Conservative newspapers have clamored for action to help the Hungarians, claiming that the King can not reasonably be expected to sit idle while his own son, now the King of Hungary, is under attack. A letter by an anonymous group of Army officers has been leaked to the press, stating that a large number of soldiers would be willing to go to Hungary to fight, if the government would let them. \n\nThe government has met to discuss a number of options.
loc.DOD_hungary.20.a: We can't afford to be drawn into this conflict.
loc.DOD_hungary.20.b: Send an observer mission to Hungary. Make it big.
loc.DOD_hungary.21.desc: Despite multiple appeals from both the Swedish king and elements of the Swedish military, the government of Sweden has refused to allow anyone to come to our aid. Even private individuals who wish to travel to Hungary to fight are refused traveling visas, and the government has pushed through legislation making it illegal to sell guns to us.
loc.DOD_hungary.22.desc: While the Swedish government is officially neutral, it has allowed a surprisingly large number of soldiers and officers to go on extended leaves of absence and even allowed them to take their personal weapons with them. The soldiers have made their way to Hungary and are now ready to join our military.
loc.DOD_hungary.23.desc: In a development surprising even experienced diplomats, the Swedish government has announced that they consider our survival to be a core national interest of Sweden. Rumor has it that the Swedish King himself has intervened on our behalf, threatening to abdicate and travel to Hungary in person to offer his service in the army unless the government offered something more than warm words of support.
loc.DOD_hungary.23.a: Will they get here in time?
loc.DOD_hungary.24.desc: Sweden has become embroiled in a bloody conflict. Making a rare appearance before both houses of parliament, the King has noted that he is deeply worried about his old home, and particularly about the fate his father and family should suffer if Sweden was to be defeated. In light of this, the government has decided to meet and discuss what can be done to help Sweden.
loc.DOD_hungary.24.a: We can't be drawn into their conflict.
loc.DOD_hungary.24.c: We stand side by side with the Swedes.
loc.DOD_hungary.25.desc: Despite a personal appeal by the Hungarian King, parliament has voted to deny any kind of support to Sweden. The opposition has threatened to remove [HUN.GetLeader] through a vote of no-confidence if he should try to do anything that would violate Hungarian neutrality.
loc.DOD_hungary.26.desc: Hungary has opened their old arsenals and sent us a number of refurbished rifles and other infantry equipment. Several thousand Hungarian volunteers have also made their way to us.
loc.DOD_hungary.27.desc: The Hungarian government has issued a statement proclaiming that any attack on Sweden is to be considered an attack on Hungary as well. The Hungarian Military has been placed at high alert and is expected to enter the war as soon as mobilization is complete.
loc.DOD_hungary.30.desc: The Hungarian government has approached us with the offer to renegotiate the Treaty of Trianon. Under their offer, the restrictions on army size in the treaty would be changed to allow Hungary to bring its current army to full strength. Hungary would further be permitted to spend a greater portion of its budget on expanding and modernizing its military industries. \n\nWith a democratic government firmly in charge of the country, there is considerable support for the scheme in our diplomatic service.
loc.DOD_hungary.30.b: And what would they need a bigger army for?
loc.DOD_hungary.31.desc: The government of [HUN.GetLeader] has scored a major political victory, as [From.GetNameDef] has just ratified the Revision to the Treaty of Trianon. We are now allowed to reinstate conscription and can openly earmark money for the construction of military factories in the budget.
loc.DOD_hungary.32.desc: The government of [From.GetNameDef] has refused to budge on the rearmament issue. Talks have broken down almost immediately, with the [From.GetAdjective] delegation stalling at every opportunity and turning minor issues such as the seating order into hour-long debates. It is clear that they don't intend on letting us rearm, but they want us to be the ones who walk out of the talks.
loc.DOD_hungary.32.a: Very well, we shall indulge them.
loc.DOD_hungary.33.desc: Hungary has recently started to feel out its neighbours about revising some of the restrictions placed on it after the last war. Specifically, they want to reintroduce conscription and expand their military industries. The Hungarian argument is that the world is becoming less safe with every passing day, and that they need a proper military to defend themselves. [From.From.GetNameDefCap] thinks otherwise.
loc.DOD_hungary.33.a: Hungary should be permitted limited rearmament.
loc.DOD_hungary.33.b: We can't upset the balance of power in the region.
loc.DOD_hungary.34.desc: The Ambassador from [From.GetNameDef] has made it clear that his government is strongly against our decision to deny the Hungarians the right to rearm. He further made it clear that should we insist on Hungary remaining disarmed, his government will take that into consideration when diplomatic issues concerning us arise in the future. \n\nIn other words, they are willing to gamble our current good relations on it.
loc.DOD_hungary.34.a: Let us pray they are not wrong.
loc.DOD_hungary.34.b: We must be firm on this issue.
loc.DOD_hungary.35.desc: The government of [From.GetNameDef] has informed us that they consider the question of revising the Treaty of Trianon to be a purely internal matter of the countries concerned, and have refused to get involved in the matter. It appears they care more about keeping good relations with their former allies than in justice.
loc.DOD_hungary.36.desc: Despite heavy political pressure from [From.From.GetNameDef], [From.GetNameDef] has categorically refused to discuss the issue. It seems that they are still afraid that we will use our weapons against them. \n\nWith all diplomatic avenues blocked, we will have to wait and see if we will get another opportunity in the future to revisit the issue.
loc.DOD_hungary.40.desc: [HUN.GetLeader] today publicly stated that he no longer considers [HUN.GetNameDef] bound by the treaty. More than that, he declared it null and void, claiming that it was forced on Hungary at gun point and therefore never legally binding. The Hungarian government has not even bothered to formally inform us of their decision.\n\n Many in the government favor a strong reply. If we show the Hungarians that we are not afraid of them, they will surely fold. However, they might also decide that we are bluffing.
loc.DOD_hungary.40.b: We can't afford a war right now.
loc.DOD_hungary.41.desc: Our recent decision to abandon the Treaty of Trianon has been met with a surprisingly strong rebuttal by [From.GetNameDef]. [From.GetLeader] reportedly demanded that the [From.GetAdjective] military prepare a plan for intervention at once. Meanwhile, the [From.GetAdjective] ambassador has asked that we clarify our statements regarding the Treaty, suggesting that the military option is still on the table.
loc.DOD_hungary.41.b: There appears to have been a misunderstanding.
loc.DOD_hungary.42.desc: Despite our strongly worded statements about the Treaty of Trianon, [From.GetNameDef] has not made any moves to stop us. In a recent press conference, [From.GetLeader] did all he could to not answer any questions about our decision to abandon the Treaty. This clearly shows what everyone already suspected: [From.GetNameDef] is nothing but a paper tiger.
loc.DOD_hungary.43.desc: It appears that our warning to [HUN.GetNameDef] has fallen on deaf ears. At a rally in Budapest last evening, the crowds reportedly shouted "Death to [From.From.GetNameDef]!" and [HUN.GetLeader] publicly vowed that any attempt to stop [HUN.GetNameDef] from reclaiming its rightful place in the world would be met with "a war the likes the world has never seen, a war that will make the great slaughter of 1914 to 1918 look like a mere bar fight".\n\nWe are at a crossroads. We must either go to war to defend our honor and credibility, or accept that we have been outmaneuvered.
loc.DOD_hungary.43.a: If the [HUN.GetAdjective]s want war, then we will give it to them.
loc.DOD_hungary.44.desc: With the threat of war on the table, the Hungarian government has suddenly become a lot more friendly. Our ambassador was invited to a private lunch with [HUN.GetLeader], where he was assured that [HUN.GetNameDef] wanted nothing but peace and friendly relations with us. Any statements in the sensationalist press should not be taken as coming from the Hungarian government, which has never wanted a war.
loc.DOD_hungary.45.desc: [From.GetNameDefCap] has declared a military intervention after [HUN.GetNameDef] openly renounced the Treaty of Trianon. They have asked us to join them in bringing down [HUN.GetNameDef] before it can regain its strength.
loc.DOD_hungary.45.a: We must strike before it is too late.
loc.DOD_hungary.45.b: We will not be drawn into this conflict.
loc.DOD_hungary.46.desc: The traitors and cowards in [From.GetNameDef] have refused to answer our call to arms! Instead of standing up to the bully in Budapest, they have rolled over and left us to face the [HUN.GetAdjective]s alone.
loc.DOD_hungary.46.a: We can do it on our own.
loc.DOD_hungary.50.desc: Transylvania was long a part of [HUN.GetNameDef], before its people freely decided to join us after the Great War. Unfortunately, [HUN.GetNameDef] never got over the loss of their territory. At various times, they have publicly claimed Transylvania as an integral part of their nation. With the recent shifts in the political situation, they have once again decided to advance their claims, demanding that we turn over the whole of Transylvania to them...or else.
loc.DOD_hungary.50.a: It's not worth the bloodshed of another war.
loc.DOD_hungary.51.desc: Rather than face the might of our armies, the cowardly [ROM.GetAdjective]s have decided to return our rightful territories. The entirety of Transylvania has been given over to our administration, and our forces have taken full control.
loc.DOD_hungary.52.desc: It is perhaps most telling that the [ROM.GetAdjective] ambassador, in a meeting with [HUN.GetLeader] this morning, felt the need to add "as always" to his flat refusal to even discuss the possibility of transferring the contested territories. Time and again, the [ROM.GetAdjective] government has publicly refused our claims, even ridiculing them. For years, we were too weak to push back.\n\nNot anymore.
loc.DOD_hungary.52.a: Anger is a poor guide in war. We will bide our time.
loc.DOD_hungary.52.b: They went too far this time.
loc.DOD_hungary.53.desc: [HUN.GetNameDefCap] has placed its forces in a state of heightened readiness. Hungarian recon planes have penetrated our airspace dozens of times in the last few hours. Our own intelligence service reports large troop movements towards the borders and air raid sirens howling in Budapest. It appears that the [HUN.GetAdjective]s are serious this time. We might be going to war.
loc.DOD_hungary.53.a: We made our gesture. No one wants a war.
loc.DOD_hungary.53.c: Perhaps it is time to compromise.
loc.DOD_hungary.54.desc: In response to our military preparations, [ROM.GetLeader] has signed General Order No. 1, putting the [ROM.GetAdjective] military on highest alert. The [ROM.GetAdjective] Air Force has occupied its war stations, and their fighters have engaged ours in mock dogfights. The [ROM.GetAdjective] ambassador has asked for his passport. No shots have been fired yet, but it is only a question of time before this crisis explodes into war. \n\nOur ambassadors in Britain, France and Germany report feverish activity in their respective foreign offices, indicating that these nations might take an interest in the brewing crisis. If we wish to solve this by force, we must strike quickly.
loc.DOD_hungary.54.a: This is spiraling out of control.
loc.DOD_hungary.55.desc: Despite the high tensions, there is still a chance to solve the issue through diplomacy. The other side has approached us through back channels, suggesting that they would not necessarily be against a commission of uninvolved nations to decide the issue. Who should we approach to argue our case?
loc.DOD_hungary.55.f: There is no one willing to hear our case...
loc.DOD_hungary.57.desc: Despite the harsh rhetoric still coming out of Budapest, Hungarian forces near the border have retreated. Violations of our airspace have ceased. It appears that [HUN.GetLeader] wants to keep this as quiet as possible, and there is consensus in the foreign office that he should be allowed to do so. A gesture of reconciliation is a small price to pay when we have so narrowly avoided a war.
loc.DOD_hungary.58.desc: With the situation in the Balkans quickly moving towards all-out warfare, Hungary has decided to ask for mediation of the Transylvanian dispute. They have approached us to request that we sit on the commission to decide the fate of Transylvania. They clearly believe that we will argue their case in the upcoming conference.
loc.DOD_hungary.58.b: Representing them is not in our interest.
loc.DOD_hungary.59.desc: Faced with increasing pressure from Hungary, Romania has asked for an impartial commission to decide the dispute over Transylvania. They have approached us to sound out our willingness to sit on that commission. No doubt they believe that we will defend their claims to the area.
loc.DOD_hungary.59.b: We have no interest in defending them.
loc.DOD_hungary.60.desc: Over the last few days, the tense relations between Hungary and Romania have broken down completely. Hungary has demanded Romania turn over the contested territories of Transylvania to them. Romania has refused. Both sides have now mobilized their forces, and war in the region seems inevitable.\n\nThe Foreign Office believes it to be imperative that we prepare an intervention to defend our interests in the region. There is also a chance that the mere threat of us getting involved will bring the other side to the negotiation table.
loc.DOD_hungary.60.c: It's just another stupid thing in the Balkans.
loc.DOD_hungary.61.desc: The [From.GetAdjective] ambassador has arrived at our Foreign Office this morning, informing us that his government watches the current crisis with grave concern. Our decision to risk war over Transylvania has forced the [From.GetNameAdj] government to consider a military intervention on the side of Hungary.
loc.DOD_hungary.61.a: We can not hope to stand against them.
loc.DOD_hungary.62.desc: Our ambassador to [From.GetNameDef] has been called in for consultations. During the meeting, he was informed that [From.GetNameDef] considers the territorial integrity of Romania to be in her national interest. Particularly the oil wells of Ploesti are very important to [From.GetNameDef]. Should Transylvania fall to us, or if we should try and occupy Romania as a whole, the oil supply would be greatly endangered. The [From.GetAdjective] government is evidently unwilling to accept the risk, and has gone so far as to threaten a military intervention on the side of Romania if war were to break out.
loc.DOD_hungary.62.b: This war will be over before they even get here.
loc.DOD_hungary.63.desc_HUN_refused: Despite our best attempts, we have been unable to secure any backing for our claims. Every nation we turned to has refused us, telling us that we should just accept the fact that Transylvania is part of Romania. \n\nHow does one accept the unacceptable?
loc.DOD_hungary.63.desc_HUN_nothing: The result of the conference on Transylvania has been a complete catastrophe. For reasons unknown, it has been decided that the entirety of Transylvania will remain with Romania. Although the final treaty has some provisions that are supposed to protect the rights of ethnic Hungarians, there can be no doubt that we have suffered a complete diplomatic rout.
loc.DOD_hungary.63.a: We have been betrayed by everyone!
loc.DOD_hungary.63.b: We will reclaim our lands, or die in the attempt!
loc.DOD_hungary.64.desc_ROM_refused: We have tried hard to gain support for our cause, but it appears that few countries these days care to defend the order created by Versailles and Trianon. With bullies like [HUN.GetLeader] around, the only thing that matters is strength.
loc.DOD_hungary.64.desc_ROM_nothing: It seems as if treaties and customs count for nothing anymore. The conference on Transylvania has ruled that the entirety of the disputed territories should go to Hungary. The entirety of the civil service is still reeling from the shock, but a decision must be made - do we accept this abomination, or do we fight it?
loc.DOD_hungary.65.t: Hungary refuses to accept result of mediation
loc.DOD_hungary.65.desc:
When informed of the results of the arbitration on the disputed territories, [HUN.GetLeader] refused to accept them. According to him, anything less than the full restoration of the old borders of Hungary would be considered an insult to every Hungarian alive or dead.

He went even further, saying that the time for negotiations and diplomacy had passed, and that there was only one way that this issue could now be settled. 

The Romanian government has asked where we stand in this dispute, considering that we have agreed to support them previously.
loc.DOD_hungary.65.a: The offer does not extend quite that far.
loc.DOD_hungary.65.b: The Hungarians must be stopped, before they subjugate the entire region.
loc.DOD_hungary.66.t: Romania refuses to accept result of mediation
loc.DOD_hungary.66.desc: The terms of the treaty negotiated in the recent conference have not been met with acceptance by the Romanian government. [ROM.GetLeader] reportedly did not even read the entire document before tearing it up and declaring that he would rather cut off his own hand than to sign anything this humiliating.\n\nThe Hungarian government has announced that they are perfectly willing to fight for what has been declared rightfully theirs, but they have also asked where we would stand in this conflict.
loc.DOD_hungary.66.b: We would be willing to support them.
loc.DOD_hungary.67.desc: Negotiations between the Great Powers have broken down completely, as the two nations have been unable to find any common ground. Any attempt at a compromise solution has been derailed by mutually unacceptable demands. The delegations have traveled back to their home countries, leaving the matter unresolved.
loc.DOD_hungary.67.a: It will be resolved by fire, blood and steel.
loc.DOD_hungary.68.desc: Both sides have approached us to decide who gets Transylvania. The Foreign Office has prepared the following brief:\n\n"It would be inadvisable, in the current situation, to award the entirety of Transylvania to one side. A compromise solution, unpopular but acceptable to both sides, should be preferred to avoid insulting one side to the point of refusing the settlement."
loc.DOD_hungary.68.a: Give all of Transylvania to Hungary.
loc.DOD_hungary.69.desc: After long hours spent negotiating, some kind of resolution seems to be close. The bad news is that we will have to give up some territory to Hungary. The northern part of Transylvania would go to them, while we keep the southern parts. It is not what we hoped for, but a realistic assessment of the situation points towards this being the best possible outcome.
loc.DOD_hungary.69.b: We won't give up a single inch of ground!
loc.DOD_hungary.70.desc: In the early morning hours, the delegations at the conference have succeeded at hammering out a compromise. Under these terms, we would get Northern Transylvania, while the southern parts of the area will remain with Romania. The Romanian delegation has already agreed to it. The Foreign Office warns that not accepting the proposal would isolate us diplomatically.
loc.DOD_hungary.70.a: It's the best we could ask for.
loc.DOD_hungary.71.desc: The diplomatic protocol dispensed with, the delegations from Hungary, Romania and [ROM_mediator.GetNameDef] have settled down to discuss the matter at hand. It has been agreed that, as representatives of the Hungarian side, we are permitted to make the first offer.
loc.DOD_hungary.71.a: Give all of Transylvania to Hungary.
loc.DOD_hungary.72.desc_HUN_all: The Hungarian side has presented us with an offer to solve the looming crisis. Unsurprisingly, they have demanded that the entirety of Transylvania is turned over to Hungary as soon as feasible. We can accept this offer, but it would no doubt upset our Romanian allies. \n\nWe could also make a counter-offer. Our Chief Diplomat strongly suggests the latter. A compromise solution would perhaps be more agreeable to both sides.
loc.DOD_hungary.72.desc_compromise: The Hungarian side has presented us with an offer to solve the looming crisis. In their offer, the northern part of Transylvania would be given to Hungary, the southern parts would remain with Romania. \n\nOur Chief Diplomat believes that this shows that the Hungarian side has gotten cold feet, and that we should push for even better terms.
loc.DOD_hungary.72.desc_HUN_nothing: The Hungarian side has surprisingly offered conciliatory terms. All of Transylvania would remain with Romania, in return for some minor concessions for ethnic minorities. The Romanian representative very strongly urges us to accept this offer, promising that the concessions would be pushed through within days if agreed upon.
loc.DOD_hungary.73.desc: Having decided to reject the Hungarian offer, it is now up to us to offer different terms.
loc.DOD_hungary.73.a: Give all of Transylvania to Hungary.
loc.DOD_hungary.74.desc_HUN_all: The Romanian side seems to suffer from great anxiety to see the issue finished, as they have rejected our previous, conciliatory offer and have instead offered to turn over all of Transylvania to Hungary. In private discussion, our delegations could not come up with a reason why they would make such an offer, but it seems genuine. We should take it.
loc.DOD_hungary.74.desc_compromise: The Romanians have offered a compromise solution, splitting Transylvania in two. Given the tensions between the two countries, this might be the best possible solution.
loc.DOD_hungary.74.desc_HUN_nothing: Unsurprisingly, the Romanian side did not budge on the Transylvanian issue. They seem to be fully committed to keeping all of Transylvania in Romania. At this stage in the negotiations, there is very little we can do - we either accept their offer or walk out.
loc.DOD_hungary.74.b: The consequences of this failure are on their hands!
loc.DOD_hungary.80.desc: The Hungarian government has approached us and asked that we hand over southern Slovakia to them, claiming that Hungarians in the area are being mistreated. At the same time, members of a terrorist group called the "Ragged Guard" have been arrested trying to cross the border from Hungary. While these people claim they have nothing to do with the Hungarian government, they were found with equipment carrying official Hungarian markings.\n\nWar is in the air, but we might be able to effect a diplomatic solution if we can secure the backing of a major nation.
loc.DOD_hungary.80.a: We can't hope to win a war. Give up the territory.
loc.DOD_hungary.81.desc: [From.GetName] has given up southern Slovakia and retreated its forces past the demarcation line. We are now in full control of the area.
loc.DOD_hungary.82.desc: The ambassador from [CZE.GetName] has come to us with an urgent request for help. Recently, [HUN.GetNameDef] has launched a major destabilization campaign aimed at southern Slovakia. Their goal is clear - they want to create a pretext for an invasion to protect people they consider their citizens. \n\nThe [CZE.GetAdjective] government has asked for our support in the matter.
loc.DOD_hungary.83.desc: [SLO.GetName] has recently come under heavy pressure from [HUN.GetNameDef] to return areas at its southern borders, which have belonged to Hungary in the past. The [HUN.GetAdjective] government has indicated that they are quite willing to fight for it, if it came to that. \n\nWe can ill afford a war breaking out in that region over something so small, and should push for a diplomatic solution.
loc.DOD_hungary.84.desc: [From.GetName] has refused to even discuss our demands, insisting that the territory has always been part of [From.GetName] and will be defended "To the last man, to the last bullet, to the last breath."
loc.DOD_hungary.84.a: We will have our chance, but it is not now.
loc.DOD_hungary.85.desc: The government of [From.GetNameDef] has notified us that the territorial integrity of Slovakia is not up for discussion. We were further instructed to withdraw any regular or irregular forces we may have in the area, or face the consequences.
loc.DOD_hungary.85.a: So much for the idea of national self-determination.
loc.DOD_hungary.85.b: We will take what is ours.
loc.DOD_hungary.86.desc: The [From.GetAdjective] government has declined our request to back us up in the face of blatant [HUN.GetAdjective] aggression. While they are sympathetic to our cause, they are not willing to risk blood or treasure for its defense.
loc.DOD_hungary.86.a: We can't win a war with warm words alone.
loc.DOD_hungary.90.desc: The [HUN.GetAdjective] government has started to apply more pressure on the issue of the Vojvodina, stating that it used to be part of Hungary during the Empire and therefore should be returned. They claim that the unification with Serbia at the end of the Great War was "invalid on account of outside pressure", and that the territory therefore still is legally [HUN.GetAdjective].
loc.DOD_hungary.90.a: This is not a conflict we can win.
loc.DOD_hungary.90.b: We will not support their delusions.
loc.DOD_hungary.91.desc: \n[FROM.GetNameDef] has agreed to cede the Vojvodina to us. Our forces have taken full control.
loc.DOD_hungary.92.desc: In a tense meeting with [FROM.GetLeader], our delegation was told that the sovereignty of the Vojvodina was not up for discussion, and that in any event the [FROM.GetAdjective] government would never bow to such pressure. The people of the Vojvodina had their say in 1919, and they choose to stay with [FROM.GetNameDef]. As far as the [FROM.GetAdjective] government is concerned, that is the end of the matter.
loc.DOD_hungary.93.t: Hungary suggests a reorder of Yugoslavia
loc.DOD_hungary.93.desc: Meeting in Zurich, representatives of the [HUN.GetAdjective] government have sounded us out about joint action against [YUG.GetNameDef]. The [YUG.GetAdjective] government has so far refused [HUN.GetAdjective] requests to return territories annexed by [YUG.GetNameDef] at the end of the Great War. Seeing how we, too, have contested territories with [YUG.GetNameDef], we could join forces and issue a strong ultimatum, but it might force us to go to war over it.
loc.DOD_hungary.93.a: They shall have our full support.
loc.DOD_hungary.93.b: We will not get involved in this matter.
loc.DOD_hungary.94.desc:
Negotiations through back channels with [From.GetNameDef] have led to an agreement, in principle, that Yugoslavia should be either dismantled entirely or at least severely reduced in size. 

With our new backers, we can now negotiate with the [YUG.GetAdjective] government from a position of overwhelming strength. We could also opt to solve the issue with force, while the Yugoslavian military is still unprepared.
loc.DOD_hungary.95.desc: \nAfter several rounds of negotiations, no agreement has been reached with the [From.GetAdjective] government on the issue of reorganizing Yugoslavia. A note signed by [From.GetLeader] himself states that any outstanding territorial issues would be solved on a bilateral basis, "when the situation calls for it."
loc.DOD_hungary.95.b: Then we will go at it alone!
loc.DOD_hungary.96.desc_HUN_GER: Instead of defusing the situation, our strong response to the latest Hungarian demands concerning the Vojvodina have apparently led to a pact between Hungary and Germany. In a recent speech, [GER.GetLeader] called Slovenia "one of the old, unredeemed provinces of the Reich" that should be reclaimed as soon as possible. The Hungarian and the German ambassador have both handed over a note to the effect that the Vojvodina and Slovenia are to be transferred to their control at once.
loc.DOD_hungary.96.desc_HUN_ITA: Instead of defusing the situation, our strong response to the latest Hungarian demands concerning the Vojvodina have apparently led to a pact between Hungary and Italy. In a recent speech, [ITA.GetLeader] referred to Dalmatia as "the unredeemed far shore of the Adriatic". The Hungarian and the Italian ambassador have both handed over a note to the effect that the Vojvodina and Dalmatia are to be transferred to their control at once.
loc.DOD_hungary.96.desc_HUN_both: Our refusal to bow to Hungarian demands have not led to a change of heart in Budapest. The angry rhetoric coming out of the Hungarian capital is now matched by equally disturbing statements from Rome and Berlin. Both nations have expressed support for the Hungarian position, while at the same time announcing their own set of demands. The ambassadors from the three countries have appeared together at the Foreign office to formally hand over a note demanding that the Vojvodina, Slovenia and Dalmatia be transferred to their respective claimants.
loc.DOD_hungary.96.a: We have no choice but to accept.
loc.DOD_hungary.96.b: We would rather die in battle!
loc.DOD_hungary.97.desc: Although they face overwhelming odds, the [YUG.GetAdjective] government have refused to see reason, telling our representatives that if we were to seek a military solution, it would find the [YUG.GetAdjective] military well prepared and ready.
loc.DOD_hungary.100.desc: The Hungarian government has approached us about the future status of Slovakia. They strongly believe that they should have full control over the fate of Slovakia, seeing how Slovakia used to be part of Hungary during the days of the Empire.\n\nWhile the Hungarian delegation shied away from issuing any explicit threats, our intelligence service reports an unsettling amount of activity inside the Hungarian military.
loc.DOD_hungary.100.b: We will not yield an inch.
loc.DOD_hungary.101.desc: Slovakia has returned to our control. The question is now how we should organize it. While many in the government favor outright annexation, calling it the "Return to the historical borders", some others are worried about the effect of trying to integrate so many non-Hungarians into our state. Their preferred option would be to set up a devolved government in Bratislava, with some powers over their internal policies, but closely aligned to us in all other matters.
loc.DOD_hungary.101.a: We will return to our old borders.
loc.DOD_hungary.102.desc: Negotiations about the transfer of Slovakia have stalled almost immediately. The [From.GetAdjective] delegation has stated their position as essentially being the status quo, with no major changes proposed. Our delegation, of course, restated that we consider Slovakia our territory, illegally seized at the end of the Great War.\n\nNo progress has been made, and the increasing frustration on both sides of the table make it unlikely that any will be made.
loc.DOD_hungary.102.b: Approach Germany about splitting up the country.
loc.DOD_hungary.103.desc: The Hungarian government has approached us with an offer to divide [CZE.GetNameDef]. We would get the western parts of the country, while Hungary would get most of Slovakia, with the demarcation line between our countries roughly bisecting the country. \n\nThey have assured us that as long as they get their share in the end, they are willing to let us make the first move.
loc.DOD_hungary.103.a: We will keep their interests in mind.
loc.DOD_hungary.104.desc: In a secret telegram, the German government has assured us that our interests will be considered when the fate of [CZE.GetNameDef] is decided. When that will be is still unknown.
loc.DOD_hungary.105.desc:
On hearing our proposal to split [CZE.GetNameDef], [From.GetLeader] reportedly flew into a rage, calling us "have-beens who have not the slightest clue about the realities of the world." 

Needless to say, our proposal has not been met with acceptance.
loc.DOD_hungary.105.b: We will take what is ours.
loc.DOD_hungary.106.desc: Despite the written promise of [From.GetLeader], the German government has not honored their commitments to us. In the recent negotiations about the fate of [CZE.GetNameDef], we have played no role except as a tool to pressure others into compliance. It appears that [From.GetLeader] never intended to keep his word.
loc.DOD_hungary.106.a: Protest in the strongest possible terms.
loc.DOD_hungary.107.desc_SLO_independent: Following several weeks of feverish activity in the Hungarian military, [HUN.GetLeader] has issued a proclamation, declaring that the current situation in Slovakia is a grave concern for Hungary, and demanding certain guarantees from us. \n\nAmongst other things, we would have to consult them before we enter any alliances or sign any treaties and would need to accept a military mission to coordinate our military.
loc.DOD_hungary.107.desc_SLO_puppet:
A Hungarian delegation has arrived to discuss the issue of Slovakia. They consider the country to be in their historic sphere of influence, and are greatly concerned by the influence we have on Slovakian policy.

The leader of the delegation went so far as to suggest that Slovakian territory may be used as a springboard to launch an invasion of Hungary.

They suggest that the Hungarian government should be permitted to wield a similar amount of influence on Slovakia as we currently enjoy.
loc.DOD_hungary.108.desc: Our Plenipotentiary has taken residence in Bratislava, ensuring that the Slovakian government will closely align their policies with our own.
loc.DOD_hungary.109.desc: Despite our best efforts, the government of Slovakia has refused to accept their subservient role compared to us. We must now consider the possibility of military action to secure our northern border.
loc.DOD_hungary.109.a: We will have it, one way or the other.
loc.DOD_hungary.110.t: Hungary wants to put pressure on Romania
loc.DOD_hungary.110.desc: [HUN.GetLeader] has arrived in Moscow to discuss the issue of Romania. At the end of the Great War, Romania illegally seized a number of territories, including Bessarabia and Transylvania. Our Hungarian comrades suggest we put pressure on Romania to return those territories to their rightful owners.
loc.DOD_hungary.111.desc: The governments of [HUN.GetNameDef] and [SOV.GetNameDef] have submitted a joint notice, stating that they consider our annexation of Transylvania and Bessarabia to be illegitimate. As far as they are concerned, these territories are under illegal occupation, and they give us one final opportunity to withdraw from the areas.
loc.DOD_hungary.111.c: A communist government might be able to get better results.
loc.DOD_hungary.112.desc: On his recent trip to Moscow, [HUN.GetLeader] had to endure several gruelling hours of meetings with [SOV.GetLeader], who repeatedly called him an idiot for trying to suggest such an obviously misguided scheme. Apparently, we have not quite understood the role of national territory in the revolutionary struggle yet, and have therefore come to the wrong conclusions about what our strategy should be.
loc.DOD_hungary.113.desc: The Romanian government under [ROM.GetLeader] has sent a delegation to Moscow to negotiate the issue of the contested territories. It seems that they believe that they can reach a compromise solution, where they would give up one part of the contested areas to hold onto the other. If we agree, which part should we demand?
loc.DOD_hungary.113.a: Force them to give up Transylvania
loc.DOD_hungary.113.b: Force them to give up Bessarabia
loc.DOD_hungary.113.c: Repeat our first offer more forcefully.
loc.DOD_hungary.114.desc: In a surprising move, [ROM.GetLeader] has offered to share power with the Romanian Communist Party, if in return we guaranteed their borders. This might be a good way to grow our influence in the region, without having to risk a war.
loc.DOD_hungary.115.desc: The [ROM.GetAdjective] government has refused to negotiate the contested territories. In a private meeting, the Romanian foreign minister went so far as to tell our ambassador that the only way we would ever gain these lands is by sacrificing a million men.
loc.DOD_hungary.115.c: Then a million men they shall have.
loc.DOD_hungary.116.desc_transylvania: After a meeting with our delegation, [SOV.GetLeader] has offered us a compromise of sorts. [SOV.GetNameDefCap] has agreed, in principle, that Bessarabia should remain with us, but an "independent border commission" made up by officials from the Soviet Union and Tannu Tuva has come to the conclusion that most of Transylvania should go to Hungary.
loc.DOD_hungary.116.desc_bessarabia: After a meeting with our delegation, [SOV.GetLeader] has offered us a compromise of sorts. With the Hungarian delegation notably absent, we were told that the Soviets are willing to drop the transfer of Transylvania if we agree to give them Bessarabia.
loc.DOD_hungary.116.desc_no_deal: During the meeting with our delegation, the Soviet-Hungarian side has reiterated their demands. Unless both Bessarabia and Transylvania are handed over to their respective claimants, they will consider military measures.
loc.DOD_hungary.116.b: We will never agree to such terms!
loc.DOD_hungary.117.desc: The Soviets have accepted our offer to put the Communists in charge. [SOV.GetLeader] personally assured our delegation that no further territorial claims will be made against us, at least not by the Comintern.
loc.DOD_hungary.117.a: We will hold him to it.
loc.DOD_hungary.118.desc: Our strong response to Soviet-Hungarian aggression seems to have born fruit. The 'Pravda' recently ran a main article speaking out against "anti-socialist revisionist claims", making particular note of the issues of the claims on Bessarabia and Transylvania as "imperialist behaviour that the developed socialist nations of the world do not engage in."\n\nHowever, the reaction in Budapest has been very muted in response. It is possible that [HUN.GetLeader] still has designs on our territories.
loc.DOD_hungary.118.a: We should love to see them try.
loc.DOD_hungary.120.desc: [HUN.GetLeader] has traveled to Moscow, bearing a proposal to offer a joint guarantee to [CZE.GetNameDef] in return for lifting restrictions on the Communist party and transfer of sovereignty of southern Slovakia to Hungary.
loc.DOD_hungary.120.b: Why should we get involved in imperialist wars?
loc.DOD_hungary.121.desc: The ambassadors of [HUN.GetNameDef] and [SOV.GetNameDef] have approached us with a joint offer to guarantee our borders against any enemy aggression. In return, we would have to guarantee the communists seats in government. Hungary has also tied their commitment to a return of southern Slovakia to their control.
loc.DOD_hungary.121.b: These are the demands we need to defend against!
loc.DOD_hungary.122.desc: Our offer of a guarantee has not been met with much enthusiasm by the [CZE.GetAdjective]s. The political concessions we asked for have caused an uproar in [CZE.GetNameDef], with several prominent Generals and political figures threatening to resign if the government accepted.\n\nCiting grave concerns that support could reach them in time, the [CZE.GetAdjective] government has official declined our offer.
loc.DOD_hungary.123.desc: Standing before a large map of Europe, [SOV.GetLeader] delivered an hour long lecture to our delegation, repeatedly pointing out shortcomings and flaws in the proposed plan and speaking at length about the exceptional foolishness of our proposal, even accusing us of making common cause with the Imperialists.\n\nOur delegation has returned from Moscow empty-handed, but alive.
loc.DOD_hungary.123.a: Perhaps this was not the best plan after all.
loc.DOD_hungary.124.desc: The [From.GetAdjective] Foreign Minister has arrived in Berlin to discuss a scheme to divide [CZE.GetNameDef] into two parts. Either party of the proposed treaty would have full control over their part of the territory. Naturally, we would be getting the western parts of Bohemia and Moravia, while they would get Slovakia.
loc.DOD_hungary.124.b: We will not tolerate their meddling in our neighbourhood!
loc.DOD_hungary.126.desc: The [CZE.GetAdjective] government has reportedly refused the offer of a guarantee, on account of the 'unbearable' concessions asked in return.\n\nHowever, our ambassador to [SOV.GetNameDef] reports that there is heavy activity in the [SOV.GetAdjective] foreign ministry. Rumors in diplomatic circles point towards a possible deal with Germany.
loc.DOD_hungary.127.desc: [GER.GetLeader] has signed the secret Treaty of Berlin, in which the German government agrees to split [CZE.GetNameDef] into two spheres of interest and promises to respect any decision made with regards to Slovakia.
loc.DOD_hungary.127.b: This is not the deal we were expecting.
loc.DOD_hungary.128.desc: In a meeting with our ambassador, [GER.GetLeader] has made it very clear that his government considers [CZE.GetNameDef] to be fully in their sphere of interest, and that any interference with its borders would be considered a hostile act.
loc.DOD_hungary.129.desc: The German ambassador has today handed over a note from [GER.GetLeader], demanding the immediate transfer governmental powers to him as the new "Reichsprotektor", pending the arrival of a specifically chosen administrator from Berlin. In the same note, the ambassador demanded that [From.From.GetNameDef] be given similar rights with regards to Slovakia.\n\nShould we refuse, the note promises "swift and decisive military action."
loc.DOD_hungary.130.desc: Despite initial successes, it seems that the government of [From.GetLeader] has changed their mind regarding the proposed treaty at the last minute. They have been very quiet about the exact reasons for their decision, but our intelligence service suspects a lack of readiness in their armed forces as the reason.
loc.DOD_hungary.140.desc: Citing the ever worsening political situation in Europe and the complete failure of the League of Nations to stop this, [HUN.GetLeader] has publicly announced that his government will seek to secure the support of neighboring nations to allow for a revision of the Treaty of Trianon. Without mentioning any territorial claims, [HUN.GetLeader] discussed only the restrictions on the Hungarian military.\n\nA delegation from Hungary has arrived in our capital to secure our formal agreement to Hungarian rearmament.
loc.DOD_hungary.140.a: They must be allowed to defend themselves.
loc.DOD_hungary.140.b: They plunged the world into war once already!
loc.DOD_hungary.141.desc: Without consulting us, the [From.GetAdjective] government has signed a treaty with Hungary, altering or removing the restrictions of the Treaty of Trianon. Hungary is now allowed to rearm freely and develop all manners of military equipment, including tanks and planes.\n\nWhile it has been an open secret that Hungary has been expanding its army, this new agreement will soon bring them to the point where they could be a military threat to us once again.
loc.DOD_hungary.141.a: We must strike before it is too late!
loc.DOD_hungary.142.desc: We have managed to secure [From.GetAdjective] support for a partial revision of the Treaty of Trianon. All restrictions on our military have been removed. The international arms inspectors have left the country, and the war ministry has drawn up initial plans for a modest expansion of our armed forces.
loc.DOD_hungary.143.desc: The [From.GetAdjective] ambassador has transmitted the following note: \n"The Government of [From.GetNameDef] is watching the recent developments in [HUN.GetNameDef] with grave concern. The Treaty of Trianon has long been a guarantee for peace and stability in the region. While the [From.GetAdjective] government accepts, in principle, that nations should be permitted to choose their own destiny, we must urge the government of [HUN.GetNameDef] in the strongest possible terms to abide by the treaty. The consequences of destabilizing the region any further could very quickly become uncontrollable."
loc.DOD_hungary.144.desc: Negotiations regarding a possible revision to the Treaty of Trianon did not progress much past the initial stage. The government of [From.GetNameDef] has made it clear that they won't move one bit from their position of maintaining the status quo.\n\nWe can either accept this or try to gain support from a third party.
loc.DOD_hungary.144.a: We must yield to their pressure.
loc.DOD_hungary.144.b: Appeal to a major power for support.
loc.DOD_hungary.145.desc: With negotiations in Bled in complete deadlock, we must regain the diplomatic initiative by introducing an outside actor. If we can get a major nation to back us, [From.From.GetLeader] might still be convinced to yield. Who should we approach?
loc.DOD_hungary.146.desc: The Hungarian government is currently attempting to alter the Treaty of Trianon to allow Hungary to begin rebuilding her military. The negotiations in Bled have been stalled for several days now. The Hungarian ambassador has approached our government with a request to exert diplomatic pressure on the other side.\n\nThe Foreign Office cautions that siding with Hungary would no doubt negatively impact relations with her neighbours and shift the balance of power in the area. However, denying the Hungarians might cause them to make an aggressive move and abandon diplomacy altogether, which could destabilize the entire region.
loc.DOD_hungary.146.a: Hungary must be permitted to rearm.
loc.DOD_hungary.146.b: Hungary must not be permitted to rearm.
loc.DOD_hungary.147.desc: In a personal letter, [From.GetLeader] has urged us to reconsider our stance on the Hungarian Rearmament Issue. In particular, he notes that even if permitted to rearm now, it will take the Hungarians years to raise an army powerful enough to threaten anything in the area. \n\nRemaining firm on this issue will isolate us diplomatically. We must decide if it is worth the added security.
loc.DOD_hungary.147.a: Let us pray that they are right.
loc.DOD_hungary.147.b: We know what is best for us.
loc.DOD_hungary.148.desc: After several days of heated negotiations, no progress has been made in Bled, and the delegations have returned to their respective home countries. Even the intervention of [From.From.GetLeader] achieved nothing. \n\nThere is considerable frustration inside the diplomatic service. Many senior diplomats suggest that we rearm anyway, just to show [From.GetLeader] what happens if he refuses to negotiate.
loc.DOD_hungary.148.a: We can not risk a war.
loc.DOD_hungary.148.b: Now is the time for deeds, not words!
loc.DOD_hungary.150.desc: A recent study of modern air combat has shown a critical weakness in our air force. Our fighters are severely behind developments in other countries. The Air Ministry has initiated a crash program to acquire a modern fighter as soon as feasible. Since domestic development would take an unacceptable amount of time, it has been decided to purchase a license from abroad. An additional budget has been authorized.\n\nExperts differ on what type of plane would be best suited to modernize our fighter wings.
loc.DOD_hungary.151.desc_light_fighter: The Air Ministry is looking to procure a new light fighter for offensive fighter sweeps and point defense, but the Foreign Office has suggested that political and diplomatic concerns should also play a role in deciding which country to buy from.
loc.DOD_hungary.151.desc_light_fighter_refus: Citing national security, the [From.GetAdjective] government has refused to release a production license. We may have better chances elsewhere, or we can look at upgrading our existing planes as an emergency stopgap.
loc.DOD_hungary.151.f: Use experience gained from the competition to improve our own planes.
loc.DOD_hungary.152.desc_heavy_fighter: The Air Ministry is looking to procure a new heavy fighter for long range interception and bomber escort, but the Foreign Office has suggested that political and diplomatic concerns should also play a role in deciding which country to buy from.
loc.DOD_hungary.152.desc_heavy_fighter_refus: Citing national security, the [From.GetAdjective] government has refused to release a production license. We may have better chances elsewhere, or we can look at upgrading our existing planes as an emergency stopgap.
loc.DOD_hungary.153.desc: The [From.GetAdjective] Air Force is currently holding trials for a new light fighter. According to our Air Attaché, our newest model is poised to win. A formal request from the [From.GetAdjective] government is expected shortly. \n\nRepresentatives of the manufacturer are strongly in favor of the sale, but there are national security concerns about selling our most modern equipment to a foreign country. Should we permit the sale to go through?
loc.DOD_hungary.154.desc: The [From.GetAdjective] Air Force is currently holding trials for a new heavy fighter. According to our Air Attaché, our newest model is poised to win. A formal request from the [From.GetAdjective] government is expected shortly. \n\nRepresentatives of the manufacturer are strongly in favor of the sale, but there are national security concerns about selling our most modern equipment to a foreign country. Should we permit the sale to go through?
loc.DOD_hungary.155.desc: Following negotiations with the manufacturer and state officials, we have successfully secured a production license for a new fighter. An example of the plane has already arrived to train mechanics on its maintenance, and a full set of drawings and blueprints is expected shortly. Production can commence at any time.
loc.DOD_hungary.160.desc: A study by the Air Ministry has revealed that our air forces are ill-equipped to support the army. Long range air strikes and close air support have both been identified as key areas in which we are critically deficient. The government has made money available for a crash program to acquire a modern bomber, but we must make a decision on which plane we should procure.
loc.DOD_hungary.160.a: A small bomber for close support.
loc.DOD_hungary.160.b: A larger plane with more range.
loc.DOD_hungary.161.desc_cas: The Air Ministry is looking to procure a new light bomber for close support of ground forces, but the Foreign Office has suggested that political and diplomatic concerns should also play a role in deciding which country to buy from.
loc.DOD_hungary.161.desc_cas_refused: Citing national security, the [From.GetAdjective] government has refused to release a production license. We may have better chances elsewhere, or we can look at upgrading our existing planes as an emergency stopgap.
loc.DOD_hungary.162.desc_tac: The Air Ministry is looking to procure a new medium bomber for long range interdiction and tactical air strikes, but the Foreign Office has suggested that political and diplomatic concerns should also play a role in deciding which country to buy from.
loc.DOD_hungary.162.desc_tac_refused: Citing national security, the [From.GetAdjective] government has refused to release a production license. We may have better chances elsewhere, or we can look at upgrading our existing planes as an emergency stopgap.
loc.DOD_hungary.163.desc: The [From.GetAdjective] Air Force is currently holding trials for a new light bomber. According to our Air Attaché, our newest model is poised to win. A formal request from the [From.GetAdjective] government is expected shortly. \n\nRepresentatives of the manufacturer are strongly in favor of the sale, but there are national security concerns about selling our most modern equipment to a foreign country. Should we permit the sale to go through?
loc.DOD_hungary.164.desc: The [From.GetAdjective] Air Force is currently holding trials for a new medium bomber. According to our Air Attaché, our newest model is poised to win. A formal request from the [From.GetAdjective] government is expected shortly. \n\nRepresentatives of the manufacturer are strongly in favor of the sale, but there are national security concerns about selling our most modern equipment to a foreign country. Should we permit the sale to go through?
loc.DOD_hungary.165.desc: Following negotiations with the manufacturer and state officials, we have successfully secured a production license for a new bomber. An example of the plane has already arrived to train mechanics on its maintenance, and a full set of drawings and blueprints is expected shortly. Production can commence at any time.
