loc.news_1941.1.desc:
On [GetDateText], Kiev, capital of the Ukrainian SSR, has been captured by the advancing [kiev_occupier.GetAdjective] armies in the Soviet Union. 

The capture of one of their most important cities is a serious blow to the Soviets, but the question still remains whether the [kiev_occupier.GetAdjective]s can keep up their momentum. Moments after the [kiev_occupier.GetAdjective]s had occupied the city, thousands of mines planted by the NKVD were apparently detonated in buildings along the Khreshchatyk main street, causing even more damage to the already ruined city.

Now the invading forces look to the east.
loc.news_1941.2.desc: After the recent occupation of Kiev by the [kiev_occupier.GetName], the Soviet counterattack has proven succesful. The Soviet Union controls the city once again, a key city to their resistance.
loc.news_1941.2.a: The Soviet bear has proven capable of fighting...
loc.news_1941.3.desc:
On [GetDateText], [moscow_occupier.GetAdjective] panzers smashed through hastily erected barriers on the streets of Moscow and half-tracks were seen unloading Panzergrenadiers on Red Square. 
Thick, billowing smoke from the many fires raging in the suburbs could be seen rising into the air as [moscow_occupier.GetAdjective] infantry stormed the Kremlin. Grenades and flamethrowers were reportedly needed to fight stubborn NKVD holdouts intent on defending every inch of the complex. The Russian capital is now in [moscow_occupier.GetAdjective] hands, but has been left a burning ruin. 

Unconfirmed reports indicate Lenin's embalmed corpse was safely evacuated east.
loc.news_1941.3.a: A strike at the heart of the Soviets...
loc.news_1941.4.desc: After the immense struggles and inevitable demise of Moscow, the Soviet Union has once again proven that its lack of equipment does not reflect their endless morale. Moscow is once again under Communist control.
loc.news_1941.4.a: Will the Soviets keep control this time?
loc.news_1941.5.desc: Advancing [stalingrad_occupier.GetAdjective] spearheads have seized Stalingrad, Stalin's namesake city on the banks of the Volga. \n\nAfter fighting their way through the ruined Stalingrad Tractor Factory and seizing the strategically vital Mamayev Kurgan heights, the [stalingrad_occupier.GetAdjective]s have forced the last Soviet defenders across the Volga to its eastern shore. It is to be seen whether the Romanians can hold their line, however...
loc.news_1941.6.desc: Today, the city of Stalingrad has been freed from [stalingrad_occupier.GetAdjective] troops. The battles were fierce and lasted for weeks in certain places. The flag of the United Soviet Socialist Republics is proudly hoisted above the city again.
loc.news_1941.7.desc:
Leningrad, birthplace of the Russian Revolution, has fallen to advancing [leningrad_fallen.GetAdjective] forces. 

Sporadic fighting can still be heard from some suburbs, but a strange calm appears to have settled over the rest of the ruined city.

Earlier today, columns of [leningrad_fallen.GetAdjective] soldiers marched past St. Isaac's Cathedral, whose great dome has been painted grey by Red Army engineers to avoid the attention of marauding Luftwaffe bombers. 
Despite their efforts, it is riddled with bullet holes and shrapnel impacts.
loc.news_1941.8.desc: After weeklong fights in the city known as the Birthplace of the Russian Revolution, the dust has finally settled. To any observer it is clear that the Soviets are once again in control. Whether this will remain is to be questioned.
loc.news_1941.9.desc:
The heavily fortified city of Sevastopol, base of the Soviet Black Sea Fleet, has finally succumbed to [sevastopol_occupier.GetAdjective] attacks. 

Its loss will severely hamper any Soviet attempt to contest the Black Sea, and the fall of the city is regarded as a significant [sevastopol_occupier.GetAdjective] victory.

An edict has already been issued from Berlin, stating that the city shall henceforth be known as 'Theodorichshafen' after Theodoric the Great.
loc.news_1941.10.desc: Sevastopol, the former base of the Soviet Black Sea Fleet has been retaken by the USSR. The temporarily exiled fleet can now operate at max efficiency again, now that their main harbor is open again. Lots of repairs remain to be done though...
loc.news_1941.11.desc:
Earlier today, [baku_occupier.GetAdjective] forces successfully occupied the city of Baku, a vital strategic objective in their war against the Soviet Union. 

Located on the shores of the Caspian Sea, the city is the key to the Caucasus, and its many oil fields are sure to benefit the German war effort.

Its capture puts the Axis in a position to expand the war into the Middle East and possibly even India.
loc.news_1941.12.desc: After weeklong fighting in the rich oil fields of Baku, the Soviet Union has proven that their morale is better than ever. They managed to fight off the [baku_occupier.GetAdjective] advance, outnumbered 2 to 1, and in bad terrain. This battle will prove vital to the Soviet tank production and will certainly cost the Germans a fair price to come...
loc.news_1941.12.a: Oil? Do they also not have democracy?
loc.news_1941.13.desc: Japanese forces have stormed and taken Honolulu, the largest city on the Hawaiian island of O'ahu. The naval base at Pearl Harbor, former headquarters of the US Pacific Fleet, has also fallen.\n\nAccording to witnesses, beleaguered American sailors and Marines retreated to Ford Island, where they continued to offer stubborn resistance until they were subjected to an intense artillery and aerial bombardment. With this island under its control, the long reach of the Imperial Japanese Navy has become greater still.
loc.news_1941.14.desc: Today, [GetDateText], Pearl Harbor was retaken by the American army. It was a combined effort, with weeklong shore bombardment done by the navy and air raids done by the air force. The Japanese held out incredibly long considering the circumstances, and hesitantly left the island. There are still a lot of Japanese in hiding nevertheless...
loc.news_1941.15.desc: Manila, capital of the Philippines, has fallen to the Japanese after the withdrawal of its American and Filipino defenders. The entrance to the strategically vital Manila Bay remained contested for some time after the city's fall due to the heavy concentration of American coastal artillery on Corregidor Island, but the guns eventually fell silent after a concerted Japanese attack.\n\nWith Manila under Japanese control, the rest of the Philippines are expected to follow shortly after. This is a stinging defeat for American forces in Asia and the Pacific.
loc.news_1941.16.desc: Combined United States and Philippino forces have today retaken the capital city Manila. It was vital to the Japanese structure of command in the Phillipines, and severely weakens their hold over the island. Although their influence in the Asian sphere is still big, it is becoming less and less threatening.
loc.news_1941.17.desc: Singapore, the 'Gibraltar of the East,' has been seized by Imperial Japanese forces despite having been considered an impregnable fortress by its former British owners.\n\nThe Japanese Military Administration of Singapore has chosen the Fullerton Building as its headquarters, and the city has been renamed Syonanto, which roughly translates to 'Southern Island gained in the age of Showa.' The Kempeitai can be seen patrolling the streets en masse to hammer in the message that the Japanese are there to stay.
loc.news_1941.18.desc: As quickly as Singapore fell, it was retaken. By overwhelming force, by over tens of thousands, the Japanese were attacked by a combined Indian, Malayan and English army group. Although their losses were major, their victory was astounding.
loc.news_1941.19.desc:
Forces from the Deutsches Afrikakorps combined with the Italian corps, have fought their way to Cairo, the capital city of Egypt. 

As Allied forces retreated further into the desert in disarray, German soldiers marching through Cairo were cheered as liberators by many citizens who had come to view the British as oppressors.

The fall of Cairo is a significant loss to the Allied war effort, and several experts have speculated that all of the Middle East now lies open to Axis conquest.
loc.news_1941.20.desc: Erwin Rommel - also known as the \"Desert Fox\", has always had an edge in North Africa due to his incredible command and good equipment. But now this edge is fading quickly by lack of equipment and overwhelming Allied force.
loc.news_1941.20.a: Will this mean the end of Axis controlled Africa?
loc.news_1941.21.desc:
Reports from London confirm that the English capital has been captured by advancing [london_taker.GetAdjective] troops. 

Small-arms fire can still be heard from some boroughs, but no significant British forces have been sighted within the city.

A detachment of Paratroopers have stormed Buckingham Palace, but it is believed that the Royal Family was evacuated well in advance of the attack. 

For the first time since William the Conqueror, London has fallen to a foreign invader.
loc.news_1941.22.desc: Fires are still being put out, and buildings blown off the side of the earth are being cleared, but this does not matter to the people of London. Their city is free of Axis occupation after weeks of fighting. This is a huge setback for the Axis, and it remains to be seen if they can hold on to their beachhead in England.
loc.news_1941.22.a: Not as great as William after all...
loc.news_1941.23.desc: The Atlantic Charter was a pivotal policy statement issued during World War II on 14 August 1941, which defined the Allied goals for the post war world. The leaders of the United Kingdom and the United States drafted the work and all the Allies of World War II later confirmed it. \n\nThe Charter stated the ideal goals of the war—no territorial aggrandizement; no territorial changes made against the wishes of the people, self-determination; restoration of self-government to those deprived of it; reduction of trade restrictions; global cooperation to secure better economic and social conditions for all; freedom from fear and want; freedom of the seas; and abandonment of the use of force, as well as disarmament of aggressor nations.
loc.news_1941.23.b: Our enemies are crawling together like snakes...
loc.news_1941.23.c: All hail our new Capitalist friends!
loc.news_1941.24.desc: By all accounts, a German submarine (later identified as U-652) fired upon the Greer, but made no contact. When news of the encounter reached the United States, public concern ran high. Initial reports reported that a British aircraft aided in repelling the attack. In response, Germany claimed \"that the attack had not been initiated by the German submarine; on the contrary, ... the submarine had been attacked with depth bombs, pursued continuously in the German blockade zone, and assailed by depth bombs until midnight.\" \nThe communique implied that the US destroyer had dropped the first depth bombs. Germany accused President Roosevelt of \"endeavoring with all the means at his disposal to provoke incidents for the purpose of baiting the American people into the war\".
loc.news_1941.24.b: The USA is purposefully provoking us!
loc.news_1941.24.d: The US edges closer and closer to the World War...
loc.news_1941.25.desc: On the 29th of September, the leaders of the Allies and Soviet Union came together to discuss the terms of aid for the Soviet Union, to be used against Nazi Germany. The representative of the USA was Averell Harriman, and Lord Beaverbrook represented the UK. Joseph Stalin was his own representative in the matter.
loc.news_1941.25.a: Our cooperation grows bigger by the day.
loc.news_1941.26.desc: After the occupation of parts of Greece by Bulgaria, a revolt broke out on 28 September 1941. With the guidance of the Macedonian politburo of the Communist Party of Greece, it started in the city of Drama and quickly spread throughout the surrounding area. In Drama, Doxato, Choristi and many other towns and villages clashes broke out with the occupying forces. On 29 September, Bulgarian troops moved into Drama and the other rebellious cities to suppress the uprising and seized all men between 18 and 45. They were reported to have executed over 3,000 people in Drama alone. An estimated 15,000 Greeks were killed by Bulgaria's occupation army during the next few weeks and in the countryside entire villages were machine-gunned and looted. Most of the members of the Macedonian politburo of the Communist Party of Greece were slaughtered by the Bulgarians, except for one member.
loc.news_1941.26.c: They fight for a better life.
loc.news_1941.27.desc: The Uprising in Serbia was initiated in July 1941 by the Communist Party of Yugoslavia against the German occupation forces and their Serbian quisling auxiliaries in the Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia. At first the Yugoslav Partisans had mounted diversions and conducted sabotage and had attacked representatives of Aćimović's quisling administration. In late August some Chetniks joined the uprising and liberated Loznica. The uprising soon reached mass proportions. Partisans and Chetniks captured towns that weak German garrisons had abandoned. The armed uprising soon engulfed great parts of the occupied territory. The largest liberated territory in occupied Europe was created by the Partisans in western Serbia, and was known as the Republic of Užice.
loc.news_1941.27.b: This is getting out of hand!
loc.news_1941.28.desc: The Uprising in Montenegro, commonly known as the 13 July Uprising was an uprising against Italian occupation forces in Montenegro. The insurgents were led by a combination of communists and former Royal Yugoslav Army officers from Montenegro. Some of the officers had recently been released from prisoner-of-war camps following their capture during the invasion of Yugoslavia. The communists managed the organisation and provided political commissars, while the insurgent military forces were led by former officers. The entire nation rejected the privileged position offered by its occupiers, rejected the capitulation in order to fight for Yugoslavia. Within three weeks of the start of the uprising, the insurgents managed to capture almost all the territory of Montenegro. The Italian troops were forced to retreat.
loc.news_1941.50.desc: Leningrad's capture was one of three strategic goals in the German Operation Barbarossa and the main target of Army Group North. The strategy was motivated by Leningrad's political status as the former capital of Russia and the symbolic capital of the Russian Revolution, its military importance as a main base of the Soviet Baltic Fleet, and its industrial strength, housing numerous arms factories. By 1939, the city was responsible for 11% of all Soviet industrial output. \n\nIt has been reported that Adolf Hitler was so confident of capturing Leningrad that he had invitations printed to the victory celebrations to be held in the city's Hotel Astoria.
loc.news_1941.50.a: We must assist our brothers in arms!
loc.news_1941.50.b: It will be a victorious fight!
loc.news_1941.51.desc: The first drop of snow has been sighted. The Russian winter, known as one of the contributing reasons to Napoleons defeat in 1812, has begun. Accompanied by another factor that impairs military maneuvering is the \"Rasputitsa\", or \"General Mud\" a phenomenon that occurs with autumnal rains and spring thaws in Russia, whereby transport over unimproved roads is made difficult by muddy conditions.
loc.news_1941.51.a: We are not prepared for this!
loc.news_1941.52.desc: The first drop of snow has been sighted. The Russian winter, known as one of the contributing reasons to Napoleons defeat in 1812, has begun. Accompanied by another factor that impairs military maneuvering is the \"Rasputitsa\", or \"General Mud\" a phenomenon that occurs with autumnal rains and spring thaws in Russia, whereby transport over unimproved roads is made difficult by muddy conditions.
loc.news_1941.52.a: This will be the turning point!
loc.news_1941.53.desc: The Nikolaev Massacre was a massacre which resulted in the deaths of 35,782 Soviet citizens, most of whom were Jews, during World War II, on September 16–30, 1941. It took place in and around the city of Mykolaiv (also known as Nikolaev) and the neighboring city of Kherson in (current) southern Ukraine (then USSR). The massacre was carried out by German troops of Einsatzgruppe D under the command of Otto Ohlendorf. The killings were committed by many of the same troops who carried out the massacre at Babi Yar, and the victims were counted and described in an Einsatzgruppen document dated October 2, 1941 as \"Jews and Communists\".
loc.news_1941.54.desc: Axis forces, mainly German, occupied Kiev on 19 September 1941. Between 20 and 28 September, explosives planted by the Soviet NKVD caused extensive damage in the city; on 24 September an explosion rocked Rear Headquarters Army Group South. Two days later, on 26 September, Maj. Gen. Kurt Eberhard, the military governor, and SS-Obergruppenführer Friedrich Jeckeln, the SS and Police Leader met at Rear Headquarters Army Group South. There, they made the decision to exterminate the Jews of Kiev, claiming that it was in retaliation for the explosions. Also present were SS-Standartenführer Paul Blobel, commander of Sonderkommando 4c, and his superior, SS-Brigadeführer Dr. Otto Rasch, commander of Einsatzgruppe C.
loc.news_1941.54.a: How can they live with this?
loc.news_1941.100.t: The Armistice of Saint Jean d'Acre
loc.news_1941.100.desc: On 10 July, as the Australian 21st Brigade was on the verge of entering Beirut, the Vichy defenders sought an armistice. At one minute past midnight on 12 July, a ceasefire came into effect and ended the campaign. The Armistice of Saint Jean d'Acre (also known as the "Convention of Acre") was signed on 14 July at the Sidney Smith Barracks on the outskirts of the city of Acre. This was a major victory for the allies, who now again fully control the former French colony.
loc.news_1941.100.b: We must defend our other territories!
loc.news_1941.100.c: How long can the Vichy regime hold on for?
loc.news_1941.150.desc: On december 7th, the Japanese Empire struck Pearl Harbor. The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor crippled or destroyed nearly 20 American ships and more than 300 airplanes. Dry docks and airfields were likewise destroyed. Most important, 2,403 sailors, soldiers and civilians were killed and about 1,000 people were wounded./n The day after the attack, Roosevelt delivered his famous Infamy Speech to a Joint Session of Congress, calling for a formal declaration of war on the Empire of Japan. Congress obliged his request less than an hour later. The attack was an initial shock to all the Allies in the Pacific Theater. Further losses compounded the alarming setback. Japan attacked the Philippines only hours later.
loc.news_1941.150.a: Good thing we have a non-aggression pact...
loc.news_1941.200.desc: An agreement was signed in 1936 which recognized territories in de facto possession by each country. However, by 1938 both nations were once again holding minor border skirmishes. In Quito, there were public demonstrations of people chanting \"Down With Peru! Long Live Ecuador!.\" Peru's response to the events taking place in Ecuador was provided by foreign minister Carlos Concha, who stated, \"In Peru we have not yet lost our heads, and the Government heads would have to be completely mad to think of war.\" \nOn 11 January 1941, alleging that the Ecuadorians had been staging incursions, the Peruvian president, ordered the formation of the North Grouping, a military unit in charge of the Northern Operational Theatre. On the fifth of july, the war was declared.
loc.news_1941.200.b: We must see to our defences!
loc.news_1941.200.c: Who cares about South America anyways?
loc.USA_1941.1.d: When Denmark fell to invading German forces, Great Britain sought to impose strict export controls on Iceland, preventing profitable shipments to Germany, as part of its naval blockade. London offered assistance to Iceland, seeking cooperation "as a belligerent and an ally", but Reykjavik declined and reaffirmed its neutrality. The German diplomatic presence in Iceland, along with the island's strategic importance, alarmed the British. After a few failed attempts at persuading the Icelandic government by diplomatic means to join the Allies and becoming a co-belligerent in the war against the Axis forces, the British invaded Iceland on 10 May 1940. We must seek to restore their neutrality.
loc.USA_1941.100.d: The United States of America has offered to protect the strategically valuable island of Iceland. We invaded it by force, partly because the government did not accept our invitation into the Allies. What should we do?
loc.USA_1941.2.d: When Denmark fell to invading German forces, Great Britain sought to impose strict export controls on Iceland, preventing profitable shipments to Germany, as part of its naval blockade. London offered assistance to Iceland, seeking cooperation "as a belligerent and an ally", but Reykjavik declined and reaffirmed its neutrality. The German diplomatic presence in Iceland, along with the island's strategic importance, alarmed the British. After a few failed attempts at persuading the Icelandic government by diplomatic means to join the Allies and becoming a co-belligerent in the war against the Axis forces, the British invaded Iceland on 10 May 1940. Today, the defence of Iceland was transferred to the United States of America.
loc.USA_1941.3.d: After fierce negotiating, the UK has accepted our offer! They have transferred the island nation to us, and henceforth we shall be its protectors.
loc.USA_1941.200.d: After fierce negotiating, the UK has rejected our offer! They have refused to transfer the island nation to our protection. It seems they seek distance from us.
loc.USA_1941.200.a: Then our distance we will keep too...
loc.USA_1941.4.d: After the threat to our navy and our peoples, it seems wise to seek a basic alliance of sorts with the United Kingdom. Should we initiate our first step?
loc.USA_1941.4.a: Yes. It is of enormous importance.
loc.USA_1941.4.b: No. They have betrayed us before.
loc.USA_1941.5.d: Today, the United States of America has come to us with an offer. They are willing to sign a document of mutual principles and hopes for a peaceful postwar world. Should we engage in the matter?
loc.USA_1941.5.a: Yes. It is of enormous importance.
loc.USA_1941.5.b: No. We will do this on our own.
loc.USA_1941.6.d: After we sent our message of peaceful cooperation, the United Kingdom graciously accepted our offer. It seems they believe yet in mutual assistance.
loc.USA_1941.7.d: After we sent our message of peaceful cooperation, the United Kingdom rudely rejected the offer. It seems they do not want the help of the United States of America.
loc.USA_1941.7.a: They will manage on their own.
loc.USA_1941.8.d: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill drafted the Atlantic Charter at the Atlantic Conference in Placentia Bay, Newfoundland. They issued it as a joint declaration on 14 August 1941 at Naval Station Argentia.\nThe eight principal points of the Charter were: \nno Territorial gains were to be sought by the United States or the United Kingdom; Territorial adjustments must be in accord with the wishes of the peoples concerned; All people had a right to self-determination; Trade barriers were to be lowered; There was to be global economic cooperation and advancement of social welfare; The participants would work for a world free of want and fear; The participants would work for freedom of the seas; There was to be disarmament of aggressor nations, and a common disarmament after the war.
loc.minor_1941.1.d: Ecuador owns rightfully Peruvian clay. It is time to set right a wrong.
loc.minor_1941.2.d: The cowardly nation of Ecuador has surrendered to our overwhelming forces. We have taken the state of Pastaza in the fighting.
loc.minor_1941.3.d: The Drama uprising was an uprising of the population of the northern Greek city of Drama and the surrounding villages on 28–29 September 1941 against the Bulgarian occupation regime. The revolt lacks organization or military resources, and we should be able to swifftly suppress them.
loc.minor_1941.3.a: We will deal with them quickly...
loc.germany_1941.1.t: Establishing the Government of National Salvation
loc.germany_1941.1.d: The Government of National Salvation, also referred to as the Nedić's regime, was the second Serbian puppet government, after the Commissioner Government, established on the Territory of the German Military Commander in Serbia during World War II. It was appointed by the German Military Commander in Serbia and operated from 29 August 1941 to October 1944. It was initially instated because the previous government did not have the means to control the Communist partisans.
loc.germany_1941.1.a: Instate the Government of National Salvation
loc.germany_1941.2.d: After we arrived in Ukraine, we faced an enormous amount of resistance from the Soviet Union. They blew up cities and used scorched earth tactics on every front it could be used on. Intelligence reports indicate that a large population of Jews and Communists live in the town of Nikolaev. Einsatzgruppe D under command of Otto Ohlendorf ordered their execution.
loc.germany_1941.2.a: Were they all jews and communists?
loc.germany_1941.3.d: The city of Babi Yar lies on the outskirts of Kiev in the Nazi-occupied Ukraine. \nSpecial SS squads prepared to carry out Adolf Hitler’s orders to exterminate all Jews and Soviet officials found there. Beginning on September 29, more than 30,000 Jews were marched in small groups to the Babi Yar ravine to the north of the city, and then murdered.
loc.germany_1941.4.desc: When we first came to Ukraine, the people of Ukraine hailed us as their saviours. Being oppressed heavily by the Soviet Union, purposefully starved, massacred and more, they saw the German Reich as their liberator. With the recent occupation of Ukrainian clay, the occupier had to decide on their policy against the Ukrainians. There are many considered \"unworthy\" by the German people, such as Slavs and jews, and the German people might turn against us if we do not act convincingly.
loc.germany_1941.5.d: The Uprising in Serbia was initiated in July 1941 by the Communist Party of Yugoslavia against the German occupation forces and their Serbian quisling auxiliaries in the Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia. At first the Yugoslav Partisans had mounted diversions and conducted sabotage and had attacked representatives of Acimovic's quisling administration. In late August some Chetniks joined the uprising and liberated Loznica. The uprising soon reached mass proportions. \n\nPartisans and Chetniks captured towns that weak German garrisons had abandoned. The armed uprising soon engulfed great parts of the occupied territory. The largest liberated territory in occupied Europe was created by the Partisans in western Serbia, and was known as the Republic of Uzice. Rebels shared power on the liberated territory; the center of the Partisan liberated territory was in Uzice, and Chetniks had their headquarters on Ravna Gora.
loc.germany_1941.5.a: We must take action against these peasants.
loc.germany_1941.6.d: Due to the collapse of the Yugoslav Army, the general population of Montenegro had easy access to large amounts of military arms and ammunition. By July 1941, the Communist Party of Yugoslavia had over 1,800 members and another 3,000 youth members, located in the area of Montenegro, Kotor and the Sandzak. Most of these were ready to commence an armed uprising against the Axis powers and the occupying Italians in particular. Grievances mainly related to the expulsion of Montenegrin people from the Kosovo region and Vojvodina, as well as the influx of refugees from other parts of Yugoslavia. Other refugees were fleeing the terror of the Ustaše in the regions along the borders with Bosnia and Herzegovina. \n\n But the event that triggered the uprising was the proclamation of a restored Kingdom of Montenegro headed by an Italian regent and led by Montenegrin separatist Sekula Drljević and his supporters, known as \"Greens\". This proclamation was announced by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It was issued to the Italian-convoked assembly of Montenegrin separatists held on 12 July 1941. The uprising broke out the following day.
loc.JAP_1941.1.d: Today, we stand on the biggest of crossroads. The Japanese Empire will, today, strike out against the United States of America. We will show that we are not to be trifled with, and we will ensure our continued hegemony in Asia. We will secure the vast oil fields, and will drive out the filthy American dogs.
loc.JAP_1941.2.d: After Japans daring attack on the Americans, they have asked us, as our brothers in arms, to help them in their struggle. We would do right by the Tripartite pact to help them.
loc.JAP_1941.2.a: It was only a matter of time...
loc.JAP_1941.3.d: Since the creation of our goal of conquest, Asia, we have always had our eyes on one of the more important countries: Thailand. When the Japanese government came to them for military access however, they denied our request. We have no other option than to attack, as they control infrastructure essential for our invasion plans.
loc.JAP_1941.4.d: After 5 hours of fighting, although fighting extremely valiantly, the Siamese have suffered unimaginable losses. They seek to make a ceasefire so that a fitting peacedeal can be made.
loc.JAP_1941.4.a: Yes, we can make good use of their ports...
loc.JAP_1941.4.b: No, we will prevail through steel!
loc.ENG_1941.1.d: For many decades, Iran and the German Empire had cultivated ties, partly as a counter to the imperial ambitions of Britain and the Russian Empire, and later, the Soviet Union. Trading with Germany appealed to Iran because the Germans did not have a history of imperialism in the region, unlike the British and Russians. Iranian embassies in occupied European capitals by Germans rescued over 1,500 Jews and secretly granted them Iranian citizenship, allowing them to move to Iran. The British began to accuse Iran of supporting Nazism and being pro-German. Although Reza Shah declared neutrality at an early stage of World War II, Iran assumed greater strategic importance to the British government, which feared that the Abadan Refinery might fall into German hands; producing eight million tons of oil in 1940, the refinery was a crucial part of the Allied war effort. \n\nFollowing Operation Barbarossa, the German invasion of the Soviet Union in June 1941, Britain and the Soviet Union became formal Allies, providing further impetus for an Allied invasion. With the German Army steadily advancing through the Soviet Union, the Persian Corridor formed by the Trans-Iranian Railway was one of the easiest ways for the Allies to get Lend-Lease supplies to the Soviets, sent by sea from the United States. British and Soviet planners recognised the importance of that railway and sought to control it. As increasing U-boat attacks and winter ice made convoys to Arkhangelsk dangerous, the railway became an increasingly attractive route...
loc.SOV_1941.1.d: When Germany attacked the Soviet Union in June 1941, many district governments took the initiative to begin a 'partial' scorched-earth policy to deny the invaders electrical, telecommunications, rail, and industrial resources. Parts of the telegraph network were destroyed, some rail and road bridges were blown, most electrical generators were sabotaged through the removal of key components, and many mineshafts were collapsed. Stalin has today given the official order to execute full-on scorched earth tactics. Every farm shall burn, and every house shall churn!
loc.SOV_1941.2.d: To boost the morale of our people, some newspapers have started to call the war the Great Patriotic War. It has enormously improved our mens will to fight, and has reignited the flame of our belief. We will defeat the German Reich. We will prevail.
loc.SOV_1941.3.d: The invasion of our country has revitalized our country's unity. Several nationalistic units have risen up in Stalingrad, and will fight till the end to protect our city!
loc.SOV_1941.3.a.tt: Spawns divisions along the Wolga river.
loc.SOV_1941.4.d: With the threat of Japan no longer a concern, we must immediately move these units forward to the front and protect Moscow from the fascist threat. These units are elite units trained in mountain and snow combat, and will no doubt face off against the German Reich without fear.
loc.SOV_1941.4.a.tt: Spawns 18 infantry divisions, 3 tank divisions, 14 mountain divisions near Yaroslavl.
loc.SOV_1941.5.d: You see comrade Germany is AI. Germany is Stupid. How do we fight stupid you might ask comrade. We add more stupid. You have a decision to give the German Reich extra divisions in the east.
loc.SOV_1941.5.a: Yes Comrade I want more stupid.
loc.SOV_1941.5.c: I am stupid enough myself and do not consider myself a Soviet.
loc.SOV_1941.5.a.tt: Spawns an enormous amount of divisions for Germany.\n
loc.SOV_1941.5.b.tt: Spawns an enormous amount of divisions for Germany and gives the event again.\n
loc.SOV_1941.5.c.tt: Spawns no divisions for Germany. Choose this if you are fine with the current amount of divisions.
loc.EFR_1941.1.d: After fierce fighting, it has become clear that we cannot hold on to our clay in Lebanon. It is time to make a deal.
loc.EFR_1941.2.d: The Vichy defenders of Lebanon have come to us with a deal. They seek an armistice, as they have realized they cannot stand up to our power.
loc.blitzkrieg_1941_desc: The initial spearhead into the Soviet Union was so effective the Soviet army is in dismay.
loc.luftwaffe_1941_desc: The Luftwaffe is at its peak performance. Never before has there been an airforce so frighteningly good at striking the enemy, and there never will be a better one.
loc.shattered_retreat_1941_desc: Stalin has ordered attacks to be fired all along the border, even though we are losing almost all battles. Our retreat is going poorly.
loc.soviet_air_forces_1941_1941_desc: After the surprise attack of the German Reich, our airforce reportedly lost 2000 aircraft on the first day of Operation Barbarossa. We must pick up the pieces.
loc.ukraine_massacre_bad_1941_desc: The Ukrainian people hailed us as their saviours. We have made clear we are not.
loc.ukraine_massacre_good_1941_desc: The Ukrainian people hailed us as their saviours. We have made clear we are indeed their saviours.
loc.news_1942.1.desc: After a diplomatic cable was made from the USA to the Vichy Regime, it was made clear that the Vichy Regime would not help the Allies. This led to a joint invasion of North Africa by American, English, and French forces, along with several Commonwealth members. There is a major sense of chaos as former compatriots are now fighting eachother. It remains to be seen whether the Vichy Regime can hold on to their colonial claims.
loc.news_1942.1.a: We must seize their home land!
loc.news_1942.2.desc: After a diplomatic cable was made from the USA to the Vichy Regime, it was made clear that the Vichy Regime would help the Allies, after threatening to invade the country. It was a major surprise for the Axis powers, who have now sought to occupy the remaining French clay.
loc.news_1942.2.a: We must seize their home land!
loc.news_1942.3.desc: After a diplomatic cable was made from the USA to the Vichy Regime, it was made clear that the USA would seek to protect Vichy neutrality. It was a major surprise for the Allies, who thought the USA would force an invasion of the country.
loc.news_1942.3.c: We will prevail on our own.
loc.news_1942.4.desc: After a diplomatic cable was made from the USA to the Vichy Regime, it was made clear that the Vichy Regime would not help the Allies. This led to a joint invasion of North Africa by American, English, and French forces, along with several Commonwealth members. The operation, named Operation Torch, existed of landings in north-west Africa. It would reduce pressure on Allied forces in Egypt, and enable an invasion of Southern Europe. Initially, the US commanders strongly opposed the plan, but combined Allied plans eventually still executed the plans.
loc.news_1942.4.a: They threaten our hold in Africa!
loc.news_1942.4.c: We must see to our defences!
loc.EFR_1942.1.desc: The French resistance in North Africa against the Vichy Regime is growing. If we want to do anything we should try right now. There are plans being made for the invasion of North-West Africa, but we could also try to coerce them peacefully.
loc.EFR_1942.2.desc: USA asks if we will join the Allies. Failure to comply will most certainly lead to military response. Especially as our counter-intelligence services seem to indicate that the resistance movement in North Africa is gaining traction and could rise against our authority.
loc.EFR_1942.3.desc: After diplomatic contact with the USA, they made clear that the Vichy Regime will be left out of this war, and their neutrality will not be broken.
loc.EFR_1942.4.desc: The Vichy Regime has made clear that they are not on our side in this fight. We must resort to military action immediately.
loc.EFR_1942.5.desc: Operation Anton, or Fall Anton, was the codename for the military occupation of Vichy France carried out by Germany and Italy in November 1942. It marked the end of the Vichy regime as a nominally-independent state and the disbandment of its army (the severely-limited Armistice Army), but it continued its existence as a puppet government in Occupied France. One of the last actions of its armed forces before their dissolution was the scuttling of the French fleet in Toulon to prevent it from falling into Axis hands.
loc.EFR_1942.5.b: We will install a puppet regime, and give Italy their claims.
loc.EFR_1942.5.c: We will install a puppet regime.
loc.SOV_1942.1.d: The Germans have started their summer strategic offensive in the Caucasus region. They are attempting to take our valuable oil fields, we must stop them at all costs!
loc.SOV_1942.2.d: The Germans have initiated their plans to encircle the Kursk salient. We must implement our plan, the Kursk Strategic Defensive Operation. This foolish operation of the Germans to try and encircle our army group could be our chance to finally exhaust their Eastern Front.
loc.SOV_1942.2.a: We will never let Kursk be taken!
loc.remaining_1943.1.d: The Allied invasion of Sicily, codenamed Operation Husky, was a major campaign of World War II, in which the Allies took the island of Sicily from the Axis powers. It began with a large amphibious and airborne operation, followed by a six-week land campaign, and initiated the Italian Campaign. \nHusky began on the night of 9–10 July 1943, and ended on 17 August. Strategically, Husky achieved the goals set out for it by Allied planners; the Allies drove Axis air, land and naval forces from the island and the Mediterranean sea lanes were opened for Allied merchant ships for the first time since 1941. The Italian leader, Benito Mussolini, was toppled from power in Italy and the way was opened for the Allied invasion of Italy. The German leader, Adolf Hitler, \"canceled a major offensive at Kursk after only a week, in part to divert forces to Italy\", resulting in a reduction of German strength on the Eastern Front.
loc.germany.500.desc: After the immense success in Africa, Erwin Rommel has been rewarded with the \"Order Of The Grand Cross Of The Iron Cross\", the second highest distinction a General or Field Marshal can obtain. He had fought with such high skill, such bravery, that he will forever be remembered by the German people.
loc.germany.501.desc:
For a time, Erwin Rommel was Hitler's favorite general. Gaining prominence in 1940 as a commander of a panzer division that smashed the French defenses, Rommel went on to command the Afrika Korps where his tactical genius, ability to inspire his troops and make the best of limited resources, prompted Hitler to elevate him to the rank of Field Marshall. In 1943, Hitler placed Rommel in command of fortifying the "Atlantic Wall" along the coast of France defenses intended to repel the inevitable invasion of Europe by the Allies. 

By the beginning of 1943, Rommel's faith in Germany's ability to win the war was crumbling, as was his estimation of Hitler. Touring Germany, Rommel was appalled at the devastation of the Allied bombing raids and the erosion of the peoples' morale. He also learned for the first time of the death camps, slave labor, the extermination of the Jews and the other atrocities of the Nazi regime. Rommel became convinced that victory for Germany was a lost cause and that prolonging the war would lead to his homeland's devastation. He came in contact with a growing conspiracy dedicated to ousting Hitler and establishing a separate peace with the western allies. 

On July 17, 1944, Rommel's car was hit by an Allied aircraft strike, severely wounding the Field Marshall. He was taken to a hospital and then to his home in Germany. Three days later, an assassin's bomb nearly killed Hitler. In the gory reprisals that followed, some suspects implicated Rommel. Rommel's "defeatist" attitude was enough to warrant Hitler's wrath. He forced Rommel to either undergo a trial where he would certainly be found guilty or take his own life. He chose the latter.
loc.germany.501.a: We have lost a true hero...
loc.germany_1943.1.d: Our implementation of Operation Isabella depends heavily on the involvement of Spain. We have 2 options: try to bargain with Spain, or take the iron route. Operation Isabella was a plan to further increase the pressure put on the United Kingdom by taking Gibraltar and securing airports in mainland Spain.
loc.germany_1943.1.b: We will take the iron route.
loc.germany_1943.2.d: Germany has contacted us through diplomatic means to implement Operation Isabella. Operation Isabella was a plan to further increase the pressure put on the United Kingdom by taking Gibraltar and securing airports in mainland Spain. We could make a good profit out of this war.
loc.germany_1943.3.d: Spain has sent us a response: they demand Gibraltar, Morocco and Cameroon if they are to join the war. This is hardly a reasonable request: Hitler has stated his beliefs that the WW1 state of Africa should be returned, a German Kamerun, so this is almost unthinkable.
loc.germany_1943.3.a: For the sake of our nation, we must agree.
loc.germany_1943.3.b: We cannot agree to this unreasonable request.
loc.germany_1943.4.d: Spain has sent us a response: they demand Gibraltar and Morocco if they are to join the war. This is a reasonable request: they have given up their claim to Cameroon which Hitler views as rightful German clay. How are we to react?
loc.germany_1943.4.a: For the sake of our nation, we must agree.
loc.germany_1943.4.b: This isn't a good enough deal.
loc.germany_1943.5.d: Spain has sent us a response: they demand only Gibraltar if they are to join the war. This is a very reasonable request: they have given up their claim to Cameroon which Hitler views as rightful German clay. How are we to react?
loc.germany_1943.5.a: For the sake of our nation, we will agree.
loc.germany_1943.5.b: This isn't a good enough deal.
loc.germany_1943.6.d: The Germans have given us our request and we will get our claims!
loc.germany_1943.7.d: The Germans have refused us our request and they will declare war!
loc.germany_1943.7.a: Seems that Germany *did* expect the Spanish Inquisition...
loc.germany_1943.8.d: It is time to initiate phase 2 of our Operation. This phase entails the attack on Portugal and Gibraltar. If we have not yet organised the attack with or against Spain we should hurry to do so.
loc.modern_tank_equipment_2_desc: Improved high-velocity piercing shells and highly slanted armor ensures these tanks can give as well as take more than their predecessors.
loc.modern_tank_equipment_3_desc: Development of universal high-explosive anti tank munition has rendered standard steel armor obsolete. In return, improved mobility, stealth and targeting ensures that with proper tank handling, enemies will not even get a chance to fire a return shot.
loc.modern_tank_equipment_4_desc: Improved high-velocity piercing shells and highly slanted armor ensures these tanks can give as well as take more than their predecessors.
loc.modern_tank_equipment_5_desc: Improved high-velocity piercing shells and highly slanted armor ensures these tanks can give as well as take more than their predecessors.
loc.modern_tank_equipment_6_desc: Improved high-velocity piercing shells and highly slanted armor ensures these tanks can give as well as take more than their predecessors.
loc.modern_tank_artillery_equipment_3_desc: Tank artillery has reached a turning point, switching from ever-increasing calibers to a higher rate of fire and better support roles with specialised smoke and incendiary shells.
loc.modern_tank_artillery_equipment_4_desc: Tank artillery has reached a turning point, switching from ever-increasing calibers to a higher rate of fire and better support roles with specialised smoke and incendiary shells.
loc.modern_tank_artillery_equipment_5_desc: Tank artillery has reached a turning point, switching from ever-increasing calibers to a higher rate of fire and better support roles with specialised smoke and incendiary shells.
loc.modern_tank_artillery_equipment_6_desc: Tank artillery has reached a turning point, switching from ever-increasing calibers to a higher rate of fire and better support roles with specialised smoke and incendiary shells.
loc.modern_tank_destroyer_equipment_3_desc: These tanks boast advanced ammunition and superb stealth, making up for their low damage with exceptional penetration values. They are the super-tank killers.
loc.modern_tank_destroyer_equipment_4_desc: These tanks boast advanced ammunition and superb stealth, making up for their low damage with exceptional penetration values. They are the super-tank killers.
loc.modern_tank_destroyer_equipment_5_desc: These tanks boast advanced ammunition and superb stealth, making up for their low damage with exceptional penetration values. They are the super-tank killers.
loc.modern_tank_destroyer_equipment_6_desc: These tanks boast advanced ammunition and superb stealth, making up for their low damage with exceptional penetration values. They are the super-tank killers.
loc.modern_tank_aa_equipment_3_desc: High-caliber autocannons aimed with newly developed portable radar trackers turn these rebuilt obsolete medium tanks into anti-air fortresses.
loc.modern_tank_aa_equipment_4_desc: High-caliber autocannons aimed with newly developed portable radar trackers turn these rebuilt obsolete medium tanks into anti-air fortresses.
loc.modern_tank_aa_equipment_5_desc: High-caliber autocannons aimed with newly developed portable radar trackers turn these rebuilt obsolete medium tanks into anti-air fortresses.
loc.modern_tank_aa_equipment_6_desc: High-caliber autocannons aimed with newly developed portable radar trackers turn these rebuilt obsolete medium tanks into anti-air fortresses.
loc.super_heavy_tank_equipment_2_desc: These tanks are rolling monstrosities, with high-caliber bunker smashing cannons and several layers of reinforced armor. But even with the most advanced engines and extra-wide double tracks, these tanks have trouble traversing marshes and have to ford rivers with a snorkel.
loc.super_heavy_tank_equipment_3_desc: These tanks are rolling monstrosities, with high-caliber bunker smashing cannons and several layers of reinforced armor. But even with the most advanced engines and extra-wide double tracks, these tanks have trouble traversing marshes and have to ford rivers with a snorkel.
loc.super_heavy_tank_artillery_equipment_3_d: Following the doctrine that bigger is always better, these artillery pieces stop any enemy in their tracks and start having problems with ammunition supply, reloading and gun barrels wearing out.
loc.super_heavy_tank_destroyer_equipment_3: Modern Super Heavy SP Tank Destroyer
loc.super_heavy_tank_destroyer_equipment_3_d: The ultimate answer to any kind of armor, these beasts do not need to be stealthy. Their armor is exceptional and their guns the deadliest. Their movement though...
loc.super_heavy_tank_aa_equipment_3_desc: This uncommon design of a rocket battery submerged within an armored box shows its worth right behind the battlefield, allowing full sky control while also absorbing the occasional shot.
loc.light_tank_equipment_4_desc: These tanks are light, designed to move fast and with great force - although they cannot take much of a beating.
loc.light_tank_equipment_5_desc: These tanks are light, designed to move fast and with great force - although they cannot take much of a beating.
loc.cv_jet_fighter_equipment_1_desc: An advanced fighter modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.
loc.cv_jet_fighter_equipment_2_desc: An advanced fighter modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.
loc.anti_air_equipment_4_desc: An advanced mobile flak gun with improved reach and firing capacity.
loc.artillery_equipment_6_desc: Light-weight artillery capable of packing a strong punch despite its size.
loc.rocket_artillery_equipment_3_desc: Rocks with increased range and power, making our already impressive artillery batteries even more effective.
loc.anti_tank_equipment_4_desc: Our new anti-tank guns can handle whatever the enemy throws at us.
loc.infantry_equipment_4_desc: Better equipment layouts and reductions in weight have led to great advances in efficiency and power.
loc.infantry_equipment_5_desc: Better equipment layouts and reductions in weight have led to great advances in efficiency and power.
loc.mechanized_equipment_4_desc: These vehicles can take our troops anywhere safely and effectively, bringing real power to the frontlines.
loc.mechanized_equipment_5_desc: These vehicles can take our troops anywhere safely and effectively, bringing real power to the frontlines.
loc.guided_missile_equipment_4_desc: We can now build highly accurate and long-reaching missiles that can punch a payload through the atmosphere.
loc.FRA_guided_missile_equipment_4_desc: Our bakers and rocket engineers have spent years on this project, and now we shall rain down hell on our enemies with the Intercontinental Balistic Baguette!
loc.GER_guided_missile_equipment_4_desc: A love letter from us to the enemy, raining death from above.
loc.USA_guided_missile_equipment_4_desc: May the spirit of Harambe guide your ICBM to the enemy safly.
loc.SOV_guided_missile_equipment_4_desc: A love letter from us to the enemy, raining death from above.
loc.GER_gw_armored_car_equipment_desc: The Büssing A5P armoured car was an armoured car developed by Büssing. It was one of the few German armoured cars during World War I.
loc.GER_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The Sd. Kfz. 221 was an armored car developed by Germany for the German Army. It was armed with a machine gun, and was mainly used for infantry support.
loc.GER_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The Sd. Kfz. 222 was an upgraded version of the Sd. Kfz. 221. The 222 was armed with a heavier gun than its counterpart.
loc.GER_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The Sd. Kfz. 231 was a heavier model armoured car. It featured heavier armour than its previous models.
loc.ENG_gw_armored_car_equipment_desc: The Rolls-Royce armoured car was an armoured car developed by Rolls-Royce. It became the most famous armoured car in the war.
loc.ENG_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The Morris armored car was unique armored car used by the British Army. It was used in smaller numbers during. World War II.
loc.ENG_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The Humber armoured car was a light armored car. It was extensively produced and used by the British Army.
loc.ENG_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The AEC mark III was a heavy armored car developed by Associated Equipment Company for the British Army.
loc.SOV_gw_armored_car_equipment_desc: The Russo-Balt Type C armoured car was an armoured car developed by Russo-Balt. The Type C was the first armoured car developed by Russo-Balt.
loc.SOV_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The BA-6 was a light armored car developed by the Soviet Union. It was used extensively in the Soviet Army.
loc.SOV_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The BA-10 armored car was a standard armored car used by the Soviet Union. The BA-10 was used in large numbers in the Red Army.
loc.SOV_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The BA-11 armored car was a heavy armored car used by the Soviet Union. The BA-11 was produced limitedly.
loc.ITA_gw_armored_car_equipment_desc: The Lancia Ansaldo IZ was an armoured car developed by Lancia Ansaldo. The IZ was developed in small numbers by the Italians but continued usage into World War II.
loc.ITA_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The FIAT AB 611 was an older armored car model used by the Italian army. Newer versions were used in 1936 in Ethiopia.
loc.ITA_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The AB 41 was an armored car developed by Autoblinda in mass numbers. It was extensively used by the Italian army.
loc.ITA_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The AS 42 was a medium armored car used by the Italian army mainly in Africa. Only a few were used on the mainland.
loc.FRA_gw_armored_car_equipment_desc: The Peugeot 1914/16 was an armoured car model developed by Peugeot. The model was changed and up-armed.
loc.FRA_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The Panhard 178 was a French armored car. The Panhard 178 was argued to have been the best French armored car during World War II.
loc.FRA_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The AMD 35 was a variant upon the Panhard 178 with slight armor differences. The AMD 35 was not as often used as the Panhard 178, although was common in the French army.
loc.FRA_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The SA 34 was a heavier variant of the Panhard 178. The SA 34 featured a heavier gun in comparison to its counterparts.
loc.USA_gw_armored_car_equipment_desc: The Jeffery armoured car was developed by the Jeffery company. It was used as the primary armoured car of the United States.
loc.USA_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The M1 armored car was a light armored car developed by the United States prior to World War II. It was used in small numbers.
loc.USA_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The M8 Greyhound was an armored transport developed in the United States. It was used extensively by American and British troops.
loc.USA_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The T18E2 Boarhound was an experimental armored car built nearing the end of the war. It was barely used but proved effective.
loc.JAP_gw_armored_car_equipment_desc: The Type 2587 Dowa armoured car was an armoured car developed by Crossley Motors. It was the first Japanese armoured car used by the Japanese.
loc.JAP_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The Type 93 Kokusan was an armored car developed by the Japanese Empire. It was designed specifically for usage on roads.
loc.JAP_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The Type 93 Chiyoda was an armored car developed by Japan. It was mass-produced and often used in Japanese armies in China.
loc.JAP_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The Type 93 Sumida was a Japanese armored car. It was known as the most numerical armored car used by the Japanese. It was used a lot in China.
loc.POL_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The wz.29 Ursus armored car was an armored car developed by Poland. The Ursus was limited in production, and the war staff soon advanced to a newer design.
loc.POL_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The wz.34 was an armored car developed by Poland. The wz.34 was more produced than its counterpart, although soon an upgraded version would be designed.
loc.POL_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The wz.34 was an upgrade of the original wz.34. The 34-II featured additional armor and a different gun.
loc.CZE_gw_armored_car_equipment_desc: The Škoda PA-I was a prototype armoured car produced by Škoda. It was succeeded by the PA-II, otherwise known as the OA vz. 23.
loc.CZE_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The OA vz. 23, also knwon as the Turtle, was an armored car developed by Skoda for the Czechoslovak army. Only a limited number saw service in the Czechoslovak army though.
loc.CZE_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The OA vz. 27 was Skoda's response to the several flaws that plagued the vz. 23. It also had enforced armor and relocated machine guns for better defense.
loc.CZE_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The OA vz. 30 was the latest armored car developed by Skoda before the invasion of Nazi Germany. Several models were acquired and used by the Germans when the invasion launched.
loc.SWE_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The L180 was an armored car developed by the Swedish company AB Landsverk. The L180 saw service with multiple armies, including the Danish, German and Dutch armies.
loc.SWE_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The Panserbil m/39 was an armored car developed by the Swedish AB Landsverk. The m/39 was solely built  for the Danish army, but as Swedish neutrality became the more threatened, the Swedish army started to use it themselves.
loc.SWE_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The m/40 was an upgraded variant of the m/39 by AB Landsverk. The main gun was replaced by a Bofors weapon, the same used on the Hungarian Toldi tank. It also had more horsepower through the employment of a new engine.
loc.HOL_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The Dutch Pantserwagen M39 was a modified version of the Swedish m/39 built by Landsverk. While the Dutch originally imported the Swedish m/39, they later made their own model.
loc.HOL_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The Overvalwagen was a Dutch armored car used mostly in Java against the Japanese. The Overvalwagen was only lightly armed but was rather quick.
loc.HOL_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The Braat Overvalwagen was a variant upon the standard Overvalwagen used in the Dutch East Indies. The Braat variant was armed with better guns than its predecessor.
loc.SPR_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The MC-36 was a truck-based vehicle used by Second Spanish Republic. While it was first developed as an unarmed truck, Nationalist Spain converted the vehicle to have a T-26 gun.
loc.SPR_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The UNL-35 was a modified armored car developed by the Second Spanish Republic. It was a variant upon the Soviet BA-20 armored car.
loc.SPR_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The AAC-1937 was an armored car developed by the Second Spanish Republic off of the Soviet BAI armored car.
loc.CAN_gw_armored_car_equipment_desc: The Jeffery-Russel was a modified version of the Jeffery armored car fielded by the Americans. It had several differences from the original, like the removal of the gun on the back of the vehicle.
loc.CAN_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The Fox armoured car was one of the primary armored cars developed by the Canadians. It was however soon replaced with the Lynx.
loc.CAN_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The Lynx Scout Car was a Canadian-built armored car that entered service. The Lynx was primarily used by the Canadians.
loc.CAN_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The Otter was a Canadian-built armored car. It was most prominently used in Italy during the allied invasion of Italy.
loc.YUG_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The Oklopna Kola is a Yugoslavian-built armoured car developed in 1944 as an improvised model under Tito's rule. It was used by the Yugoslavians in their fight against the Germans.
loc.SAF_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The Marmon-Herrington Mark I was the first armoured vehicle and armoured car developed in South Africa. It was armed with a Vickers machine gun.
loc.SAF_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The Mark III was an upgraded design from the Mark I which was longer and better armed. It was one of the most-produced variants of the vehicle.
loc.SAF_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The Mark IV was a completely redesigned version of the Marmon-Herrington, armoured with much thicker armour, and a heavier gun, the Mark IV was one of the most produced vehicles, as over 2,000 were built.
loc.RAJ_armored_car_equipment_1: Armoured Carrier Wheeled Indian Pattern Mark II
loc.RAJ_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The ACV-IP Mark II was the second version in the Armoured Car Wheeled Indian Pattern line of vehicles. Mark II introduced a new chassis to the vehicle.
loc.RAJ_armored_car_equipment_2: Armoured Carrier Wheeled Indian Pattern Mark IIA
loc.RAJ_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The ACV-IP Mark IIA introduced a modified hull which was tougher than the previous model's hull. These versions often came with additional machine guns as well.
loc.RAJ_armored_car_equipment_3: Armoured Carrier Wheeled Indian Pattern Mark IIB
loc.RAJ_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The ACV-IP Mark IIB came with thicker armour than the previous models and had an upgraded engine over them as well.
loc.AST_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The Daimler Dingo Scout Car was the first armoured car and armoured vehicle produced and used by the Australian Royal Army Corps.
loc.AST_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The Rover Light Armoured Car was the first in a series of armoured cars. The LAC was developed by the Australian company Rover.
loc.AST_armored_car_equipment_3: Rover Light Armoured Car Mark II
loc.AST_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The Rover Light Armoured Car Mark II was the second in the series of Rover-built armoured cars. The second variant featured different armour, developed by Ford, Canada.
loc.IRE_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The Leyland Armoured Car was one of the first Irish-built armed vehicles, based on the Landsverk L180.
loc.IRE_armored_car_equipment_2_desc: The Ford Mark V Armoured Car was an armoured car design based upon the previous mark IV. However, unlike the mark IV, the mark V was built in Ireland.
loc.IRE_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The Dodge Armoured Car was another home-built armoured car. The Dodge was one of the most-used Irish armoured cars during and after the war.
loc.HUN_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The 39M Csaba was an armored car used and developed by the Hungarian Royal Army. The 39M was the only armored car used by the Hungarians. It was designed by Nicholas Straussler, who also designed two Hungarian light tanks.
loc.BEL_gw_armored_car_equipment_desc: The Minerva armoured car was the Belgian attempt at armoured car production. It was literally a converted civilian vehicle armed with a machine gun and upped armour.
loc.MAN_armored_car_equipment_3_desc: The Type 90 Sumida was a modified variant of the original Sumida by Japan. The Type 90 was much heavier than its counterpart, with a new gun and thicker armour.
loc.MON_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The BA-6 was a light armored car developed by the Soviet Union. It was used extensively in the Soviet Army.
loc.AUS_armored_car_equipment_1_desc: The M35 was an armoured car developed by the Austrians in 1935 for police and military duties. The ADGZ featured heavy armour but light weaponry.
loc.HUN_armored_car_command_equipment_1_desc: 40M Csaba was a command armoured car developed by the Hungarian Royal Army. It was a modified version of the 39M Csaba.
loc.GER_armored_car_command_equipment_1_desc: The Sd. Kfz. 260 was a variant of the Sd. Kfz series. It was equipped with a long range radio for communications.
loc.GER_armored_car_command_equipment_2_desc: The Sd. Kfz. 261 was an upgraded variant of the Sd. Kfz. 260 and the Sd. Kfz. 221. It featured an extended range for the communicators.
loc.armored_car_command_equipment_1_desc: A command variant of the original vehicle.
loc.armored_car_command_equipment_2_desc: A command variant of the original vehicle.
loc.armored_car_equipment_3_desc: Armored cars were often used in conjunction with troops for light troop support.
loc.armored_car_command_equipment_3_desc: A command variant of the original vehicle.
loc.light_carrier_1_desc: Escort Carriers are small, slow and vulnerable but cheap to produce.  Suited primarily for escorting convoys and submarine defense.
loc.light_carrier_2_desc: Larger and more capable than escort carriers, light carriers can cover small independant operations and support fleet carriers.
loc.light_carrier_3_desc: A significant refinement of existing light carrier designs.  A budget alternative to a full size fleet carrier.
loc.light_carrier_desc: A less capable but more affordable version of the Aircraft Carrier, designed primarily for convoy protection and escorting more valuable warships.
loc.artillery_a_desc: The first shot is for the Devil, the second for God, and only the third is for the King.
loc.artillery_c_desc: Fine tooling and other adjustments made to every part of the battery have resulted in an overall increase in power and reliability.
loc.artillery_d_desc: The weight of our units has been reduced, increasing their effectiveness.
loc.artillery_e_desc: Artillery with streamlined rounds capable of achieving greater velocity.
loc.rocket_artillery_a_desc: One of the things that we can say with confidence is that we will have much lighter, much stronger materials, and this will reduce the cost of rockets.
loc.rocket_artillery_b_desc: The rockets... can be built so powerfully that they could be capable of lauching a man. So try not to end up on the moon, ok?
loc.rocket_artillery_d_desc: Rockets with increased speed and launch force.
loc.rocket_artillery_e_desc: The unit's casing has been refined, providing increases in efficiency and reliability.
loc.antiair_a_desc: Why does the Army need expensive new guns? Have the pilots we've been shooting at over the years started complaining?
loc.antiair_b_desc: On my left the shooting had the sharp explosion of the infantry artillery, on my right could be heard the sporadic cannon shots thundering from the front, and up above the sky was clear and the sun bright.
loc.antiair_d_desc: We have made great advances in linking our artillery systems to radar.
loc.antiair_e_desc: Further advanced in radar technology and linkage have allowed for maxiumum efficiency.
loc.antitank_a_desc: If the tanks succeed, then victory will follow. If they fail, we are lost.
loc.antitank_b_desc: Your heaviest guns will be your will to live. Keep them going, no matter what, and pray theirs aren't bigger.
loc.antitank_d_desc: Our rounds now have greatly increased penetration and force behind them.
loc.antitank_e_desc: The accuracy and manueverability of each shot is now improved considerably.
loc.infantry_at_a_desc: Aim steady, don't dare breathe. Fire - and then run like hell.
loc.infantry_at_b_desc: Aim steady, don't dare breathe. Fire - and then run like hell.
loc.infantry_at_c_desc: Aim steady, don't dare breathe. Fire - and then run like hell.
loc.infantry_at_d_desc: Aim steady, don't dare breathe. Fire - and then run like hell.
loc.advanced_infantry_weapons_a_desc: The guns, thank God, the guns. . .
loc.advanced_infantry_weapons_c_desc: The guns, thank God, the guns. . .
loc.advanced_infantry_weapons_d_desc: The guns, thank God, the guns. . .
