loc.FR3_war_front_2_desC: Choosing to focus on the frontline means gaining more war support but losing stability on the homefront.
loc.FR3_war_front_3_desc: Choosing to focus on the frontline means gaining more war support but losing stability on the homefront.
loc.FR3_support_italian_claim_desc: If we support Italy's claims in the Austro-Hungarian Empire it would be very likely that they will join our side in order to get a slice of the old Empire at the peace conference.
loc.FR3_give_ita_savoy_corsica: Cede Savoy and Corsica to Italy
loc.FR3_give_ita_savoy_corsica_desc: I would heavily advise against such an downplay on the power of our country but if we are to give the Italians Savoy and Corsica they would have no choice but to join the Entente.
loc.FR3_invite_britain_desc: With the Germans violating the Belgian neutrality the British have no choice but to join us in this conflict!
loc.FR3_britain_reinforcement_desc: The French Army alone will not be able to hold the Western Front together which is why we need the combined French and British armies to stay in a successful defensive posture and eventually counterattack.
loc.FR3_invite_italy_desc: Since Italy has accepted our offer we may now invite them into our faction
loc.FR3_send_troops_serbia_desc: In order to help our ally Serbia against the numerically superior forces of Austria we can send some of our troops to help hold the front line against any offensives.
loc.FR3_allied_blockade_greece_desc: In order to try and force the Pro-Central Powers monarch, Constantine I, we could force a blockade on Greece which would sow dissent in the country and force Constantine to abdicate in favor of his Pro-Entente Son, Alexander.
loc.FR3_invite_greece_desc: Since Constantine I has abdicated and been replaced with his Pro-Entente son we can now invite Greece into our faction.
loc.FR3_support_greece_desc: In order to support our ally Greece on their front with the Central Powers we can send them aid in the form of weapons which they might be lacking.
loc.FR3_troops_greece_desc: In order to put more pressure on the Central Powers we could send in the Armee d'Orient into Greece heavily reinforcing the Greek Army making it a formiddable force combined with our troops.
loc.FR3_russian_reinforcement_desc: Seeing as the Russian Empire has practically unlimited reserves, we could, in return for muntions, ask for several divisions to come to Western Front where we lack men and are in need of numerical superiority against the Germans.
loc.FR3_convince_romania_desc: We could try and convince the Kingdom of Romania to join the Entente, however the Eastern Front must be stabilizd before we do this or else the Romanians are heavily unlikely to join!
loc.FR3_invite_romania_desc: As we have succesfully managed to convince the Kingdom of Romania to join our side we can now invite them
loc.FR3_anti_german_proapganda_desc: With our humiliating defeat in the 1871 Franco-Prussian war and Germany's forceful annexation of the rightful French territory of Elsass-Lothringen we have nothing left for them but Anti-German sentiment...
loc.FR3_pro_russia_desc: Whilst the Russian Empire is in now way democratic they are still a very important ally to us against the German Empire which is now squashed in between us, as long as we are allies the Germans will not be a threat!
loc.FR3_agadir_crisis_desc: In order to expand further in Morocco we could deploy a substantial force of our troops into the interior of Morocco, however we might face a retaliation from Berlin.
loc.FR3_defend_border_desc: It wouldn't hurt to fortify our border with Germany even more.
loc.FR3_sacred_union_desc: The time of war is no time to be bickering about politics and drawing up dissent, we must all come together and let go of that for now.
loc.FR3_defend_colonies_desc: It wouldn't hurt to fortify our colonial strongholds.
loc.FR3_volunteers_1_desc: Since mainland France lacks as much manpower as the Germans can field we could always compensate with recruiting men from the colonies.
loc.FR3_volunteers_2_desc: Since mainland France lacks as much manpower as the Germans can field we could always compensate with recruiting men from the colonies.
loc.FR3_volunteers_3_desc: Since mainland France lacks as much manpower as the Germans can field we could always compensate with recruiting men from the colonies.
loc.FR3_unity_desc: As the time of war comes upon us, we must remain united against the enemy.
loc.FR3_war_effort_desc: Gain a boost of war support

loc.RUS_home_front_3_desc: Choosing to focus on the homefront means gaining more stability within your country instead of war support.
loc.RUS_shorter_training_desc: With the war dragging on and taking more and more lives we need more men to refill the casualties so shortening training would help with that.

loc.RUS_war_front_2_desC: Choosing to focus on the frontline means gaining more war support but losing stability on the homefront.
loc.RUS_war_front_3_desc: Choosing to focus on the frontline means gaining more war support but losing stability on the homefront.
loc.RUS_slavic_brotherhood_desc: Improving relations will all slavic nations in the Balkans
loc.RUS_support_serbia_desc: We need to show our support for Serbia in order to scare the Austrians from trying to use the Franz Ferdinand excuse to invade them!
loc.RUS_befriend_romania_desc: As far as Romania should be concerned we share on common rival, the Austrians.
loc.RUS_investments_from_west_desc: If we accept investments from the west we will face a largely foreign owned industry, however on the upside we would industrialize quicker.
loc.RUS_railway_construction_desc: Once we finish the Trans-Siberian railway we will have more control over the country and benefit economically greately having much easier access to the eastern port of Vladivostok.
loc.RUS_railway_construction_2_desc: Once we finish the Trans-Siberian railway we will have more control over the country and benefit economically greately having much easier access to the eastern port of Vladivostok.
loc.RUS_occupy_northern_persia_desc: In order to safeguard the Persian Oilfields it would be wise to occupy Northern Persia seeing Turkey may very well get involved in this conflict...
loc.RUS_brusilov_offensive_desc: Launching the Brusilov offensive will give you a timed idea with heavy military bonuses, but you must control a certain amount of territory, not being pushed back too far by the Austrians.
loc.RUS_petrograd_defense_desc: Since our capita, Petrograd, is a coastal city it would be wise to increase fortifications should the German fleet seek to bombard it in the future.
loc.RUS_mongolian_bufferstate_desc: Taking advantage of the chaos in China with their revolution we have the opportunity to back the creation of a Mongolian state in order to create a buffer between our two countries.
loc.RUS_russian_dominance_desc: We could take even more advantage of the situation in China and enforce a Russian dominance in the region
loc.RUS_take_manchuria_desc: Enforcing our dominance we have decided to move our troops into the territory of Manchuria where the Chinese who are already divided inside dealing with their own issues provided no retaliation.
loc.RUS_send_troops_france_desc: In order to help out our french allies on the Western Front we could send Russian troops to aid them against the numerically superior Germans.
loc.RUS_request_aid_desc: Whilst providing aid will prove rather difficult considering that the Baltic Sea and the Black Sea are cut off by the Central Powers, at least something would help considering our shortages.
loc.RUS_request_aid_2_desc: Whilst providing aid will prove rather difficult considering that the Baltic Sea and the Black Sea are cut off by the Central Powers, at least something would help considering our shortages.
loc.RUS_supress_revolutionaries_desc: The country has been recently filled with various radical revolutionaries, whilst we can supress them with secret police in the end we will have little control of the will of the people
loc.RUS_continue_russification_desc: In order to cut down on dissent from minorities we should continue our policy with Russification
loc.RUS_pan_slavism_desc: All Slavic people's should unite as one
loc.RUS_reinforce_tsars_authority_desc: The Tsar's authority shall not be undermined.
loc.RUS_nicholas_on_front_desc: Should Nicholas be transfered to the front, there will be a morale boost amongst the soldiers.
loc.RUS_form_polish_legion_desc: Forming a Polish Legion will give us a few extra Polish divisions to use.
loc.EN1_homefront_focus_1_desc: Choosing to focus on the homefront means gaining more stability within your country instead of war support.
loc.EN1_homefront_focus_2_desc: Choosing to focus on the homefront means gaining more stability within your country instead of war support.
loc.EN1_homefront_focus_3_desc: Choosing to focus on the homefront means gaining more stability within your country instead of war support.

loc.EN1_frontline_focus_1_desc: Choosing to focus on the frontline means gaining more war support but losing stability on the homefront.
loc.EN1_frontline_focus_2_desC: Choosing to focus on the frontline means gaining more war support but losing stability on the homefront.
loc.EN1_frontline_focus_3_desc: Choosing to focus on the frontline means gaining more war support but losing stability on the homefront.
loc.EN1_join_war_desc: Join the war on the side of the Entente.
loc.EN1_befriend_US_desc: We need the United States support in a major european war, so it would be wise to befriend them as much as we can in hopes they can someday assist us.
loc.EN1_bring_america_in_desc: The United States has for long enough retained its neutral stance, it is time for them to join the conflict
loc.EN1_anti_german_sentiment_desc: Over the past decade there has been an increasing amount of tension between Britain and Germany over the issue of the Naval Race which the Kaiser refuses to back down on theatening our naval superiorty and with that the Island of Britain.
loc.EN1_stay_neutral_desc: Perhaps it would be wise to sit it out for a year, if anything we can always join later.
loc.EN1_back_france_desc: With Belgium neutrality violated it is our duty to show that our words will not be walked over by some filthy kraut!
loc.EN1_north_sea_blockade_desc: In order to hopefully starve the Germans out and cut them off from the resources of the world it would be a great idea to implement a blockade.
loc.EN1_cosncript_irish_desc: Whilst it would be a bad idea to conscript the Irish seeing as how things went, previously with the Easter Rising, we need more men on the front and this will be plenty enough.
loc.EN1_dont_conscript_irish_desc: The Irish will not be conscripted, no matter if we need more men.
loc.EN1_nordic_country_trading: Call on Scandinavia to Break off Relations with Germany
loc.EN1_nordic_country_trading_desc: The Nordic countries, particularly Sweden provide the Germans with war supply which cannot be blocked off seeing as the Germans have control over the Baltic Sea, however we could always ask them to stop and break off relations with Germany.
loc.EN1_portugal_friend_desc: The Portuguese and Germans have faced a significant amount of tension with the Germans sinking a fair amount of Portuguese ships and colonial tensions in Africa, we could benefit off of this and align Portugal with us hopefully eventually getting them to join the Entente.
loc.EN1_invite_portugal_desc: The Portuguese have just about had enough of the Germans sinking their convoys and the tensions on their colonial borders and are ready to join the Entente.
loc.EN1_bulgaria_talks_desc: Whilst we cannot offer all that the Central Powers probably can in terms of territory, we must do as much as we can to get Bulgaria on our side, it would mean the imminent collapse of Turkey seeing how close the border is to Constantinople, offering territorial concessions to Bulgaria means pissing off the Serbs however it will just have to do.
loc.EN1_invite_bulgaria_desc: Bulgaria has agreed to our negotiations and is ready to join the Entente
loc.EN1_baltic_project_part_1_desc: A plan has been proposed by Admiral Lord Fisher who insures a speedy victory, his plan is to land a substantial force of British and or Russian soldiers on the flat beaches of Pomerania on the Northern German coast, less than 100 miles from Berlin. A substantial fleet would be required to keep the invasion safe from the Imperial German Navy, but Lord Fisher assures it will be completely worth it.
loc.EN1_baltic_project_part_2_desc: As we go from the planning phase into the preparation phase, we have started putting together the large specialist fleet which will contain more than 600 special vessels.
loc.EN1_fortify_suez_desc: It would be wise to fortify the Suez Canal in case of war.
loc.EN1_secure_southern_persia_desc: In order to secure the Persian Oilfields in the South and the path to India we must put Southern Persia under British occupation for the time being seeing Turkish involvment is likely.
loc.EN1_hold_back_turk_ships_desc: The Ottoman Empire has bought two vessels which have been completed, however seeing as how Turkish involvement in the war is very likely it would be wise to confiscate them to make sure it doesn't get into the hands of the enemy.
loc.EN1_arab_revolt_desc: If we support Arab Nationalism in Hedjaz we could open up another front for the Turks to worry about, these Arabs will work closely with us to put an end to the Ottoman Empire.
loc.EN1_colonial_focus_desc: Focusing on our colonies means helping them develop an industry
loc.EN1_indian_manpower_desc: The British Raj contains millions of men ready for military service, these reserves will be of great help to our cause.
loc.EN1_plan_gallipoli_campaign_desc: If we are to quickly knock out the Turks from the war, one way to do it would be to launch a naval invasion onto the Gallipoli peninsula taking hold and then moving onto Constantinople, a seriously important symbol of the Empire.
loc.EN1_execute_gallipoli_desc: The time has come to launch the Gallipoli naval invasion, may God be with us!
loc.EN1_canadian_troops_desc: If we wish, we could request several Canadian divisions over to the Western Front where they are most certainly needed.
loc.EN1_grant_south_african_indep_desc: The cries for South African independence have not been drowned, we shall do as our people ask.
loc.EN1_united_people_desc: With war approaching we must stay united against our enemies.
loc.EN1_defence_of_realm_act_desc: The Defence of the Realm Act (DORA) will give the government wide-ranging powers such as requisitioning buildings or land needed for the war effort, or making regulations creating criminal offenses and authoritarian social control mechanisms, such as censorship.
loc.EN1_military_service_act_desc: Whilst it would be nice if conscription was not needed, we are not getting enough men through our current recruitment methods which calls for universal conscription.
loc.INT_GER_reconstruction_commission_desc: Phase I - Reconstruction. Returning soldiers, strained municipal services and factories built for wartime orders need a coordinated transition to civilian production. Establish a commission to choose reconstruction priorities and open one-time industrial projects.
loc.INT_GER_roaring_twenties_desc: Phase III - The Roaring Twenties. A stable currency opens a window for investment, new machinery and rising urban demand. Choose rapid expansion backed by foreign credit or a slower approach built on domestic savings. Credit can accelerate growth, but a withdrawal of lending will leave industry exposed. If this focus is completed after the 1929 crash, the investment program proceeds without a boom bonus.
loc.INT_GER_electrification_desc: Coal alone cannot power a modern economy efficiently. Link generating stations and industrial districts, opening a one-time electrification project for a controlled German core state.
loc.INT_GER_domestic_capital_desc: Savings banks and retained earnings offer an alternative to volatile foreign borrowing. Organize domestic investment and open a savings campaign; the following reserve focus can cushion a later credit shock.
loc.INT_GER_build_reserves_desc: Set aside resources before the crash rather than committing every available mark to expansion. Reserves soften the additional penalty from foreign-credit exposure; they cannot prevent the worldwide Depression. This optional preparation must be finished before 24 October 1929.
loc.INT_GER_export_guarantees_desc: Machinery and chemical producers need secure orders as much as new equipment. A limited guarantee program opens a one-time export drive during the boom, strengthening manufacturing without promising unlimited foreign demand.
loc.INT_GER_bank_restructuring_desc: Phase IV - Depression and Recovery. Consolidate distressed balance sheets and restore the flow of working capital. The banking crisis must be addressed before the broader recovery program can succeed; any additional foreign-credit burden remains until that program is completed.
loc.INT_GER_industrial_recovery_desc: Repaired banks, retrained workers and a coherent employment policy can support a lasting recovery. Open a final one-time industrial investment project and prepare German industry for the next decade.
loc.INT_GER_reconstruction_projects_tt: Unlocks one-time reconstruction decisions in the German Industrial Development category.
loc.INT_GER_roaring_twenties_tt: Opens an investment-policy event. Foreign credit offers faster growth but adds exposure to the 1929 crash. Domestic savings favor resilience. Boom bonuses cannot be gained after the crash.
loc.INT_GER_electrification_tt: Unlocks the one-time industrial electrification decision.
loc.INT_GER_domestic_capital_tt: Unlocks a domestic savings decision and the focus to build pre-crash reserves.
loc.INT_GER_export_guarantees_tt: Unlocks a one-time export promotion decision during the boom years.
loc.INT_GER_industrial_recovery_tt: Unlocks a final one-time industrial recovery project.
loc.INT_GER_industry_desc: Reconstruction (1919-1923) gives way to currency stabilization and the Roaring Twenties (1924-1929), followed by Depression and recovery. Complete focuses to reveal one-time investment projects. Foreign credit accelerates growth but creates additional exposure to the 1929 crash; pre-crash reserves reduce that exposure. Construction requires a peaceful, fully controlled German core with room for the building.
loc.INT_GER_industry_reconstruction_projects: Invest 75 Political Power to restore one civilian factory in a controlled core state before currency stabilization, and no later than 1923. This project can be funded only once.
loc.INT_GER_industry_roaring_investment_desc: Invest 100 Political Power in one civilian factory during the boom. Financing the project places a temporary public works burden on the economy for 540 days. This opportunity closes with the 1929 crash.
loc.INT_GER_industry_electrification_grid_de: Invest 75 Political Power to add one infrastructure level to a controlled core state below the infrastructure limit and permanently improve industrial productivity. This project does not require an empty factory slot.
loc.INT_GER_industry_housing_program_desc: Commit 60 Political Power to municipal housing. Gain stability immediately and support workers for one year, at the cost of higher consumer goods requirements. This is a social investment, not an additional factory.
loc.INT_GER_industry_modernize_machinery_des: Invest 60 Political Power in new machinery, gaining an industrial research bonus and a production efficiency cap bonus for two years.
loc.INT_GER_industry_domestic_savings_desc: Under the domestic-savings policy, commit 75 Political Power to a reserve fund before the crash. Restricted spending imposes a temporary austerity burden for 540 days. This offers an alternative to the reserve focus and cannot be repeated if reserves already exist.
loc.INT_GER_industry_export_guarantees_desc: Spend 50 Political Power on a limited export campaign. Guarantees support investment and confidence for up to two years, ending early if the worldwide credit crisis breaks out.
loc.INT_GER_industry_bank_restructuring_desc: After restructuring the banks, spend 40 Political Power on a one-time campaign to restore depositors' confidence. Gain stability while the broader recovery program is still being prepared.
loc.INT_GER_industry_recovery_program_desc: A final industrial investment can turn recovery into durable productive capacity.
loc.INT_GER_industry_reconstruction_desc: State coordination is rebuilding productive capacity after war and inflation.
loc.INT_GER_industry_reconstruction_cautious: Reconstruction is proceeding slowly, with an emphasis on monetary confidence.
loc.INT_GER_industry_credit_boom_desc: Foreign credit is financing a remarkable industrial expansion, but it leaves Germany exposed to an external shock.
loc.INT_GER_industry_savings_path_desc: Savings and retained earnings provide a steadier foundation for industrial growth.
loc.INT_GER_industry_electrification_desc: A broader electrical grid is raising productivity across the industrial economy.
loc.INT_GER_industry_export_support_desc: Public guarantees support German exporters and keep orders flowing.
loc.INT_GER_industry_public_works_burden_des: Recent investment has created a temporary fiscal burden.
loc.INT_GER_industry_austerity_burden_desc: A savings drive is limiting public spending while its benefits accumulate.
loc.INT_GER_industry_credit_crash_desc: The collapse of foreign lending has hit German production and confidence hard.
loc.INT_GER_industry_credit_crash_buffered_d: Reserves are cushioning the industrial economy from the collapse of foreign lending.
loc.INT_GER_industry_recovery_desc: Recovery policy is restoring orders, employment and confidence after the depression.
loc.INT_GER_industry_bank_reform_desc: Reorganized banks are once again able to support productive investment.
loc.INT_GER_industry_reserve_fund_desc: Liquidity set aside before the crash can cushion foreign-credit exposure. The fund is deployed when the crash arrives.
loc.INT_ger_industry.1.d: Investment committees are considering a renewed expansion of German industry. Foreign lending promises rapid growth, while savings and retained earnings offer a slower and less exposed foundation. The policy chosen here shapes our gains during the boom and our vulnerability when international lending contracts.
loc.INT_ger_industry.2.d: The Reconstruction Commission has submitted two approaches to rebuilding civilian production. State coordination can restore capacity quickly, while a cautious program puts greater emphasis on household confidence. These emergency programs are useful during reconstruction; once monetary stabilization or a later crisis has overtaken them, the recommendations instead strengthen the government's planning authority.
loc.INT_ger_industry.3.d: The global crisis has ended the investment boom. Firms reliant on foreign credit face an additional contraction; reserves prepared before the crash can soften this blow. An economy built on domestic savings avoids that extra exposure, but it still suffers the wider Depression. Bank reform and a sustained recovery program are now essential.
loc.INT_ger_industry.4.d: The worst of the depression has passed. Orders are returning and a more durable industrial policy can now replace emergency measures.
loc.INT_GER_industry_recovery_project_desc: Invest 100 Political Power in a final civilian factory in a controlled core state. The banking, employment and industrial recovery programs must be completed first. This project can be undertaken only once.
loc.INT_GER_industry_housing_support_desc: Public housing supports working households while drawing resources into civilian consumption.
loc.INT_GER_industry_modern_machinery_desc: Recent investment in machinery lets existing production lines operate more efficiently.
loc.INT_GER_industry_credit_risk_tt: Foreign-credit exposure adds an extra economic penalty when the 1929 crash arrives. Completing reserves before the crash reduces this penalty; neither choice prevents the worldwide Depression.
loc.INT_ger_industry.1.d_late: The years of easy expansion have passed. Our investment committees can still supply useful plans, but they cannot bring back the pre-crisis credit boom. Either recommendation now provides 25 Political Power without changing the current economic phase.
loc.INT_GER_parliamentary_commissions_desc: The young republic can give elected members stronger oversight of administrative work or coordinate their efforts through the cabinet. A choice event establishes the balance and opens future parliamentary decisions.
loc.INT_GER_civic_education_desc: Schools and civic associations can explain the new constitution and give citizens a stronger voice in its institutions. Gain an electronics research bonus and democratic support.
loc.INT_GER_social_compromise_desc: Employers and trade unions can settle practical disputes over work, wages and demobilization. Stability and civilian manpower reflect a more durable settlement.
loc.INT_GER_local_government_reform_desc: Municipal governments need the authority to rebuild services and commission useful civilian projects. Gain a civilian factory and limited administrative capacity.
loc.INT_GER_republican_crisis_cabinet_desc: After the global economic crash, republican parties must decide whether to prioritize coalition relief or fiscal restraint. A choice event shapes the political cost of defending parliamentary government.
loc.INT_GER_defend_constitution_desc: Civic organizations and constitutional parties can preserve democratic participation through the emergency. Strengthen democratic resilience and support.
loc.INT_GER_shop_floor_committees_desc: Workplace committees can coordinate production methods and draw workers into the council system. Gain industrial research progress and communist support.
loc.INT_GER_workers_planning_board_desc: The new council government must choose between dispersed worker committees and a central planning office. A choice event sets the character of economic coordination.
loc.INT_GER_socialist_welfare_desc: Local councils can coordinate food, housing and employment relief. The program raises stability and brings workers back into the civilian labor pool.
loc.INT_GER_red_training_schools_desc: Instructors from the reorganized army can train a new officer corps. Gain army experience and land doctrine research progress.
loc.INT_GER_workers_republic_constitution_de: Consolidate the institutions of the council state after its military and civilian branches are established. Improve stability and communist support.
loc.INT_GER_prussian_administration_desc: Experienced provincial offices can restore records, procurement and fiscal administration under a conservative government. Gain industrial research and political capacity.
loc.INT_GER_federal_chambers_desc: A constitutional monarchy can preserve regional representation through a permanent chamber of the states. This stabilizes the federal settlement.
loc.INT_GER_monarchist_reconciliation_desc: Negotiate a workable balance between the crown and the state governments. Gain political capacity and stability for the constitutional route.
loc.INT_GER_royal_railways_desc: The restored administration can commission civilian rail and freight works. Gain one civilian factory and an industrial research bonus.
loc.INT_GER_restored_court_desc: The restored monarchy can organize a stable court after bringing the princes and civil service into the new order. Gain stability and neutral support.
loc.INT_GER_rapallo_commission_desc: Set priorities for German-Soviet cooperation: commercial exchange or restricted military research. A choice event shapes the projects that follow.
loc.INT_GER_eastern_trade_network_desc: Use the trade commissions to build civilian links with the Soviet economy. Gain one civilian factory and limited political capacity while relations remain open.
loc.INT_GER_eastern_exercises_desc: Staff contacts can improve army training without granting unrestricted rearmament. Gain army experience and a land doctrine bonus.
loc.INT_GER_joint_aviation_trials_desc: Technical cooperation can test aviation practices in the east. Gain air experience and light-air research progress when the Soviet partner exists.
loc.INT_GER_diplomatic_treaty_revision_desc: The government must decide whether to publicize legal objections to Versailles or prepare covert procurement. A choice event opens related one-time decisions; the existing revision chain remains available.
loc.INT_GER_foreign_press_campaign_desc: Publish Germany's case for revision in foreign newspapers and diplomatic circles. Gain political capacity and limited stability.
loc.INT_GER_hidden_procurement_desc: Build restricted armament capacity under the treaty regime. Gain one military factory and a small increase in war support.
loc.INT_GER_officer_professionalization_desc: Develop a smaller but more capable staff through disciplined training. Gain army and command experience and land doctrine progress.
loc.INT_GER_party_administration_desc: The new authoritarian government can prioritize bureaucratic control or a propaganda apparatus. A choice event establishes how state offices will be directed.
loc.INT_GER_controlled_press_desc: Political control of reporting strengthens support for the ruling party while imposing a cost on civic stability.
loc.INT_GER_reich_labor_front_desc: Mobilize labor for state priorities after the political takeover. Add available manpower and war support at a cost to stability.
loc.INT_GER_state_contracts_desc: Channel public orders to civilian firms. Gain one civilian factory and industrial research progress.
loc.INT_GER_arms_contracts_desc: After the 1935 rearmament decision, commission a military factory and give the army experience with new production.
loc.INT_GER_republic_path_desc: Decisions for civic rights, elections and coalition recovery.
loc.INT_GER_communist_path_desc: Decisions for councils, transport and social welfare.
loc.INT_GER_monarchist_path_desc: Decisions for federal administration and the restored court.
loc.INT_GER_eastern_path_desc: Decisions for trade, training and technical exchange.
loc.INT_GER_versailles_path_desc: Decisions for diplomacy, public advocacy and procurement.
loc.INT_GER_fascist_path_desc: Decisions for labour mobilization, administration and contracts.
loc.INT_GER_paths_public_education_desc: Teach constitutional rights and parliamentary procedure through a national civic programme.
loc.INT_GER_paths_municipal_charters_desc: Give local councils clearer powers to deliver services and represent their communities.
loc.INT_GER_paths_social_compromise_desc: Bring employers, unions and parties into a durable settlement over wages and welfare.
loc.INT_GER_paths_constitutional_guard_desc: Train officials and judges to defend the constitutional order during emergencies.
loc.INT_GER_paths_election_registers_desc: Prepare accurate voter rolls and transparent polling procedures for the next election.
loc.INT_GER_paths_cabinet_recovery_desc: Use the crisis cabinet's mandate to restore confidence in government and public finance.
loc.INT_GER_paths_shop_floor_desc: Give workplace committees a formal role in production and labour relations.
loc.INT_GER_paths_transport_committees_desc: Put railway workers and planners together to keep the national network moving.
loc.INT_GER_paths_social_welfare_desc: Direct relief and public health resources toward workers and their families.
loc.INT_GER_paths_red_training_desc: Build a cadre of officers and organizers trained in the new republic's defence.
loc.INT_GER_paths_workers_constitution_desc: Settle the balance between local councils and the central workers' republic.
loc.INT_GER_paths_prussian_administration_de: Rebuild a professional state service while the monarchy finds its footing.
loc.INT_GER_paths_federal_chambers_desc: Give the Länder a lasting voice in the restored constitutional order.
loc.INT_GER_paths_royal_railways_desc: Use the crown's prestige to coordinate long term railway investment.
loc.INT_GER_paths_restored_court_desc: Reestablish the court as a symbol of continuity and public service.
loc.INT_GER_paths_monarchist_reconciliation_: Bring republican veterans, federalists and royalists into a common settlement.
loc.INT_GER_paths_eastern_trade_desc: Coordinate contracts and clearing arrangements with markets to the east.
loc.INT_GER_paths_eastern_exercises_desc: Exchange field lessons with a partner whose army also studies modern warfare.
loc.INT_GER_paths_joint_aviation_desc: Test aircraft and training methods beyond the reach of the treaty inspectors.
loc.INT_GER_paths_eastern_credit_desc: Use commercial ties to keep reconstruction finance available when western lenders hesitate.
loc.INT_GER_paths_treaty_legalists_desc: Prepare a careful legal case for revising the restrictions imposed on Germany.
loc.INT_GER_paths_foreign_press_desc: Present Germany's grievances to foreign editors and parliamentary audiences.
loc.INT_GER_paths_hidden_procurement_desc: Quietly acquire equipment and expertise while public negotiations continue.
loc.INT_GER_paths_officer_professionalizatio: Standardize training and staff work so that a smaller army can still learn quickly.
loc.INT_GER_paths_labor_front_desc: Coordinate labour exchanges and industrial arbitration through the new state structure.
loc.INT_GER_paths_controlled_press_desc: Create a unified public information service for the regime's policies.
loc.INT_GER_paths_arms_contracts_desc: Use carefully managed contracts to build military capacity before the 1936 transition.
loc.INT_ger_paths.1.d: The new commissions can either hold ministers to account or help the cabinet move legislation through a crowded Reichstag.
loc.INT_ger_paths.1.a: Let the commissions oversee the cabinet
loc.INT_ger_paths.1.b: Give the cabinet a coordinating hand
loc.INT_ger_paths.2.d: The coalition has survived its first crisis. Its next decision will shape whether recovery rests on relief or retrenchment.
loc.INT_ger_paths.3.d: Delegates disagree over whether the new plan should be built from the shop floor or directed through a central office.
loc.INT_ger_paths.4.d: The restored states must decide how much authority belongs to the federal compact and how much belongs to the crown.
loc.INT_ger_paths.4.a: Bind the crown to a federal compact
loc.INT_ger_paths.5.d: The commission can make eastern cooperation an open commercial programme or keep its most sensitive research discreet.
loc.INT_ger_paths.6.d: A public legal campaign may build international support, while quiet procurement would give negotiations a stronger backstop.
loc.INT_ger_paths.7.d: The new administration can emphasize orderly bureaucracy or a more forceful public information apparatus.
loc.INT_GER_paths_republic_oversight_desc: Commissions keep ministers answerable to the Reichstag.
loc.INT_GER_paths_cabinet_coordination_desc: A disciplined cabinet can move policy quickly through parliament.
loc.INT_GER_paths_civic_education_desc: Citizens and officials know the rights and procedures of the constitution.
loc.INT_GER_paths_social_compromise_spirit_d: Employers and organized labour have a reason to defend the settlement.
loc.INT_GER_paths_constitutional_guard_spiri: Officials are prepared to defend constitutional government in a crisis.
loc.INT_GER_paths_workers_councils_desc: Shop floor representation has a recognized place in economic administration.
loc.INT_GER_paths_central_planning_desc: Production targets and material allocations are coordinated nationally.
loc.INT_GER_paths_social_welfare_spirit_desc: Public welfare institutions stabilize the workers' republic.
loc.INT_GER_paths_red_training_spirit_desc: A trained cadre shares lessons across the revolutionary armed forces.
loc.INT_GER_paths_federal_compact_desc: The Länder and the crown share authority under a negotiated compact.
loc.INT_GER_paths_crown_prerogative_desc: The restored court retains a stronger coordinating role in the state.
loc.INT_GER_paths_royal_administration_desc: A professional civil service carries the monarchy's programme into every Land.
loc.INT_GER_paths_eastern_commerce_desc: Trade offices turn eastern contacts into reliable commercial exchange.
loc.INT_GER_paths_eastern_training_desc: Joint exercises and discreet schools spread new military methods.
loc.INT_GER_paths_legal_revision_desc: A public legal campaign gives treaty revision diplomatic credibility.
loc.INT_GER_paths_covert_procurement_desc: Quiet acquisitions improve military expertise while carrying political risk.
loc.INT_GER_paths_bureaucratic_coordination_: Party offices and state ministries share a coordinated administrative chain.
loc.INT_GER_paths_propaganda_apparatus_desc: A unified information service keeps the regime's message in the public sphere.
loc.INT_GER_paths_coalition_relief_spirit_de: Emergency relief steadies the republic while drawing civilian factories into public provision. This program expires after two years.
loc.INT_GER_paths_retrenchment_spirit_desc: Budget cuts free some industrial capacity and strengthen the cabinet, but deepen public discontent. This program expires after two years.
loc.INT_depression.1.d: The collapse of financial confidence in October 1929 has spread across the world economy. Trade and credit are contracting, factories are slowing, and unemployment is rising. Our government must choose how to answer the crisis.
loc.INT_great_depression_desc: The global downturn has reduced demand, credit and industrial activity.
loc.INT_GER_great_depression_desc: Dependence on foreign credit and collapsing trade have made Germany especially vulnerable.
loc.INT_USA_great_depression_desc: Bank failures, collapsing demand and mass unemployment have struck the American economy.
loc.INT_ENG_great_depression_desc: Exports and investment have weakened across Britain and its trading partners.
loc.INT_FRA_great_depression_desc: The global slump has reached France through trade, finance and falling industrial demand.
loc.INT_ITA_great_depression_desc: Shrinking markets and credit have increased pressure on Italian industry.
loc.INT_JAP_great_depression_desc: The collapse of export markets has hit Japanese producers and workers.
loc.INT_SOV_great_depression_desc: Central planning limits the direct financial shock, though falling world trade still affects industrial imports.
loc.INT_depression_aftershock_desc: Emergency measures have contained the worst damage, but the economy has not fully recovered.
loc.INT_GER_recovery_program_desc: Industry and public finances have begun to recover from the crisis.
loc.shared_INT_depression_emergency_desc: Mobilize the government to contain bank failures and unemployment.
loc.shared_INT_depression_public_works_desc: Invest in infrastructure and industry to create jobs and sustain demand.
loc.shared_INT_depression_austerity_desc: Protect public finances through spending restraint, despite the immediate social cost.
loc.shared_INT_depression_stabilization_desc: The worst of the downturn can be contained, although its effects will linger.
loc.INT_GER_depression_response_desc: Phase IV - Depression and Recovery. The global collapse of credit and demand requires an emergency response. Choose between public works and austerity, support municipal relief, and prepare a restructuring of the banks. This response does not require completing the boom-era investment projects.
loc.INT_GER_public_works_desc: Use public investment to employ workers and revive industry.
loc.INT_GER_austerity_desc: Cut spending to defend public finances, accepting greater hardship in the short term.
loc.INT_GER_recover_from_depression_desc: With a response to unemployment chosen and the banks restructured, begin a broader recovery from 1933. End the Depression and any additional foreign-credit shock, then retrain workers and rebuild industrial confidence.
loc.INT_UKR_fragmented_army_desc: Rival commands struggle to coordinate the front as exhausted formations lack weapons and trained replacements. Disrupted arsenals cannot keep pace with losses, weakening both offensive operations and the defense of our territory. These penalties last through the civil-war period until 1923.
loc.INT_eastern_fragmented_army_desc: Regional formations answer to competing authorities, while disrupted arsenals struggle to supply a unified army. Training and production suffer, and units have difficulty sustaining coordinated operations. These penalties last through the civil-war period until 1923.
loc.INT_SOV_red_army_mobilization_desc: The struggle against the White armies demands a coordinated military effort. Central arsenals supply replacement weapons, recruits reinforce the front, and commissars organize training and supply. This mobilisation lasts for the Russian Civil War.
loc.INT_reckless_progress_desc: Pushing our borders will result in quick process.
loc.INT_steady_progress_desc: To achieve a thriving economy, we must focus on steady progress.
loc.INT_war_economy_to_consumer_goods_war_ec: War Economy Transformed into Consumer Goods
We have succeeded in reforming our wartime productions into consumer goods. This will severly heighten our ability to produce for the people.
loc.INT_war_economy_to_consumer_goods_civili: Although we did not have a war economy in the period of WW1, we have still thrived to improve the situation for the consumers.
loc.INT_war_economy_to_resource_extraction_w: War Economy Transformed into Resource Extraction
We have succeeded in reforming our wartime productions into resource extraction. This will severly heighten our ability to produce more equipment for the people.
loc.INT_war_economy_to_resource_extraction_c: Although we did not have a war economy in the period of WW1, we have still thrived to improve the situation of our resource extraction.
loc.don_kuban_stability: Stability in the Don Kuban Region
loc.don_kuban_stability_2: Stability in the Don Kuban Region
loc.INT_GER_postwar_unrest_desc: Defeat, shortages and political violence continue to unsettle Germany.
loc.INT_GER_reichswehr_arrangement_desc: A professional army remains available to the government, though its loyalties cannot be taken for granted.
loc.INT_GER_weimar_constitution_desc: The republic is founded on constitutional government and civil rights.
loc.INT_GER_currency_stabilized_desc: Monetary reform has ended the worst of the inflation crisis.
loc.INT_GER_unemployment_insurance_idea_desc: The national insurance system cushions job losses but requires continuing public spending.
loc.INT_GER_dawes_credit_desc: Foreign loans and a revised payment schedule support reconstruction.
loc.INT_GER_young_plan_desc: Reparations have been rescheduled again, easing some immediate economic pressure.
loc.INT_GER_presidential_cabinet_desc: Emergency decrees have displaced ordinary parliamentary coalitions.
loc.INT_GER_democratic_resilience_desc: Republican institutions have survived their gravest political test.
loc.INT_GER_revolutionary_transition_desc: The new socialist order is still consolidating its authority.
loc.INT_GER_socialist_planning_desc: Heavy industry is reorganized under public direction.
loc.INT_GER_red_reichswehr_desc: The armed forces have been reorganized for the socialist government.
loc.INT_GER_constitutional_monarchy_desc: The Kaiser reigns under a constitution and an elected parliament.
loc.INT_GER_imperial_restoration_desc: The restored imperial government places authority in the hands of the crown.
loc.INT_GER_clandestine_rearmament_desc: Military research and organization continue despite treaty restrictions.
loc.INT_GER_balanced_budget_desc: Spending restraint eases pressure on the treasury but deepens social hardship.
loc.INT_SOV_left_opposition_desc: The party leadership is contested by advocates of international revolution.
loc.INT_SOV_party_center_desc: Centralized appointments strengthen the governing party apparatus.
loc.INT_SOV_nep_compromise_desc: A mixed economy balances state industry with peasant trade and cooperatives.
loc.INT_SOV_party_democracy_desc: Competing socialist programs can be argued within the party.
loc.INT_SOV_first_plan_desc: Heavy industry grows quickly, but the new targets strain consumption.
loc.INT_SOV_collectivization_crisis_desc: Rapid changes in the countryside depress stability and supply.
loc.INT_SOV_collective_farms_desc: Equipment and stable procurement restore some agricultural output.
loc.INT_SOV_second_plan_desc: The industrial drive now emphasizes machinery, transport and productivity.
loc.INT_SOV_cooperative_industry_desc: State investment and cooperative production grow together.
loc.INT_SOV_left_industry_desc: Public investment is guided by worker councils and technical institutes.
loc.fascist_propaganda_surrender_desc: The recent propaganda of the fascist regime has thoroughly ensured our people that our country will fight to the end, and that their support is necessary.
loc.no_faction_joining_desc: This is to disable AI from joining factions in ways its not supposed to. If you are a player, please do not join a faction.
loc.no_faction_joining_poland_desc: Having recently gained its independence, this country is unwilling to bind itself to another power.
loc.no_ally_calling_desc: This nations AI can't call other allies into the war due to crashes or game accuracy.
loc.ww1_fokker_desc: Fokker produced famous designs such as the Fokker Dr.I Triplane, and the Fokker Eindecker, a monoplane.
loc.albatross_desc: Albatros was well known for being a main supplier of the German Airforce in WWI later merging into Focke-Wulf
loc.gothaer_desc: During WWI Gothaer constructed several successful bomber designs for the German Airforce
loc.kaiserliche_werft_desc: It was one of the three main shipyards that solely produced warships for the German Navy
loc.cheap_rations_desc: Hurr Durr I Don't Like Rations ;P
loc.MEX_unpopular_dictatorship_1_desc: The Diaz dictatorship has grown widely unpopular throughout Mexico making soldiers less likely to stay loyal or join forces with the government
loc.jihad: The Call Goes Out for Jihad
loc.AUS_war_exhaustion_desc: The people of Austria-Hungary are tired of the fighting, it is clear the Empire is losing and mass desertions as well as workers strikes plague what is left of it.
loc.GE1_war_exhaustion_desc: The people of Germany are tired of the war, the support for the war is going down each day, people are starving, soldiers are barely getting enough food. The people of Germany have given up.
loc.BNN_war_exhaustion_desc: Bulgaria has fought valiantly with the Central Powers but the Kingdom is war weary and our troops are under equiped, some starving, and many deserting. Day by day the support for the war wanes and so does our chance for survival.
loc.TUR_war_exhaustion_desc: The Ottoman Empire has fought bravely and has achieved more than expected but we stand no chance against the allies who have already penetrated us deeply taking Jerusalem and Bagdhdad and rapidly advancing further north.
loc.AUH_multiethnic_desc: Austria-Hungary is a multiethnic Empire which has not served it well with several ethnicities in one division it makes it hard to communicate and direct orders as well as patriotism which is non-existant amongst non Austrians and Hungarians.
loc.GER_lowsupply_desc: Germany's home front is failing which is reflected on the war front as supplies gets harder to come by with each day with our industrial base deteriorating and the fresh American giant on the enemy side.
loc.GER_kaiserschlacht_desc: On March 21st, 1918 the German High Command executed Operation Michael in a last ditch effort to take out the European allies before U.S. troops arrive in large numbers.
loc.FRA_hundred_days_offensive_desc: With the German Spring Offensive a clear failure the Allies retaliated by launching a counter attack which led to a series of rapid victories against the now weary retreating German Army.
loc.GRE_vardar_offensive_desc: In September 1918 the Greeks with allied support launched an offensive against Bulgaria in Vardar Macedonia which ultimately led to the Bulgarian Collapse
loc.central_research_institute_of_shipbuildi: Central Research Institute of Shipbuilding Technology
loc.fabrica_nacional_de_canones_de_trubia: Fábrica Nacional de Cañones de Trubia
loc.fabrica_nacional_de_armas_portatiles_de_: Fábrica Nacional de Armas Portátiles de Oviedo
loc.estrada_de_ferro_central_do_brasil: Estrada de Ferro Central do Brasil
loc.electric_traction_company_of_hong_kong__: Electric Traction Company of Hong Kong
loc.compania_minera_e_industrial_de_chile: Compañía Minera e Industrial de Chile
loc.alliance_and_dublin_consumers__gas_compa: Alliance and Dublin Consumers' Gas Company
loc.electric_traction_company_of_hong_kong_: Electric Traction Company of Hong Kong
loc.soviet_occupation_war_exhaustion_desc: Additionally to the army debuffs, this idea adds 1 daily §RWar Exhaustion§! while at war and removes the ability to lose §RWar Exhaustion§! while at peace. We should attempt to fix the resistance problem as soon as we can.

loc.treaty_of_versailles_desc: The post-war settlement restores the Rhineland and Palatinate to Germany while granting France resource rights there and in the Ruhr, Moselland and Westerwaldkreis. Germany pays consumer-goods reparations of 20% each to France and Britain. Its military is limited to a 100,000-man Reichswehr; naval and air rearmament are prohibited.
loc.versailles_reparations_recipient_desc: German reparations reduce consumer-goods requirements by 20%.

loc.INT_world_news.1.d: On 9 November 1923, Bavarian police stopped Adolf Hitler and his allies as they marched through Munich toward the Feldherrnhalle. The attempted seizure of power collapsed, and the government moved to ban the Nazi Party and prosecute its leaders. The immediate revolt is contained, but the violence of the currency and Ruhr crises has exposed the fragility of Germany's constitutional order.
loc.INT_world_news.2.d: After the Reichstag burned on 27 February 1933, President Hindenburg signed an emergency decree at the Hitler cabinet's request. Fundamental civil liberties are suspended, allowing police to detain political opponents and suppress publications and meetings. Berlin calls the measures a defense against revolution; the republic's constitutional protections are being dismantled.
loc.INT_world_news.3.d: Armed revolutionary groups and their supporters have seized parts of central Berlin in January 1919, as the new republic prepares to elect a national assembly. The government calls on loyal forces to regain the streets while workers' demonstrations and rival claims to authority divide the capital. The fighting threatens to deepen the split within the German left.
loc.INT_world_news.4.t: A Council Republic Proclaimed in Bavaria
loc.INT_world_news.4.d: On 7 April 1919, revolutionary councils in Munich proclaimed a Bavarian republic governed through workers' and soldiers' councils. The elected state government has left the city and is seeking support to restore its authority. Armed groups are gathering on both sides, presenting the national government with another challenge to its fragile postwar order.
loc.INT_world_news.5.t: The Munich Council Republic Is Suppressed
loc.INT_world_news.5.d: Government troops and volunteer formations took Munich in early May 1919 after fierce fighting. The council government is gone, but deaths in the streets and reprisals against suspected supporters are deepening the divide between revolutionary workers and the republic's leaders. Restoring civil administration will take more than a military victory.
loc.INT_world_news.6.t: Germany Leaves the League of Nations
loc.INT_world_news.6.d: On 14 October 1933, the Hitler government announced Germany's withdrawal from the League of Nations and the disarmament talks in Geneva. Berlin argues that the other powers refuse Germany equal treatment in armaments. Foreign governments see the withdrawal as a challenge to the international settlement, and diplomacy loses a forum that the Weimar republic worked to enter only seven years ago.
loc.INT_world_news.7.d: British and German representatives signed an agreement on 18 June 1935 allowing the German navy to reach 35 percent of British naval tonnage overall, with a separate provision for submarines. London hopes a defined limit will prevent an uncontrolled naval race; Berlin treats the deal as recognition of its rearmament. France was not included in the negotiation.
loc.INT_world_news.8.d: At the Nazi Party rally in Nuremberg on 15 September 1935, the regime announced laws stripping Jewish Germans of full citizenship and prohibiting marriages and intimate relationships between Jews and people classified by the state as German blood. Racial persecution is now written into national law, deepening the exclusion already imposed through dismissals, boycotts, and violence.
loc.INT_world_news.9.d: On 1 September 1923, a devastating earthquake struck the Tokyo-Yokohama region. Fires spread through the wreckage, communications failed, and ruined infrastructure made relief and reconstruction an urgent national task. The scale of the disaster has shaken Japan's government and economy.
loc.INT_world_news.10.d: On 23 October 1922, Conservative MPs ended the coalition with David Lloyd George. Andrew Bonar Law formed a ministry seeking a mandate of its own, while Britain faced the postwar debt burden, industrial unrest, and arguments over the direction of trade policy.
loc.INT_world_news.11.d: Ill health forced Andrew Bonar Law from office in May 1923. Stanley Baldwin took over the premiership as arguments over tariffs, unemployment, and the future of the Conservative government dominated the House of Commons.
loc.INT_world_news.12.d: A general election in October 1924 gave the Conservatives a majority, and Stanley Baldwin returned as prime minister in November. Labour's short first ministry has ended, while the new government faces pressure over industrial relations, housing, and the gold standard.
loc.INT_world_news.13.d: The general election of May 1929 left Labour as the largest party in the Commons. Ramsay MacDonald returned to Downing Street to form a second ministry, taking office as unemployment rises and the international economy shows signs of strain.
loc.INT_world_news.14.d: Ramsay MacDonald stepped aside as leader of the National Government in June 1935. Stanley Baldwin returned to the premiership as the cabinet faced questions of defence, unemployment, and European security.
loc.INT_world_news.15.d: On 18 August 1920, Tennessee became the final state needed to ratify the Nineteenth Amendment. The Constitution now prohibits denying the vote on grounds of sex, bringing women into national elections after decades of campaigning.
loc.INT_world_news.16.d: The Immigration Act signed on 26 May 1924 imposes national-origin quotas and excludes immigrants from much of Asia. Washington presents the measure as a restriction on population and migration, while critics warn that it makes racial hierarchy a principle of American law.
loc.INT_world_news.17.d: Herbert Hoover entered the White House on 4 March 1929 after promising continued prosperity and efficient government. His administration inherits a booming but increasingly speculative economy, with confidence in American growth still high as the new term begins.
loc.INT_world_news.18.d: President Hoover signed the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act on 17 June 1930, raising American duties across a broad range of imports. Supporters call the measure protection for domestic producers; trading partners warn that retaliation could further restrict world commerce during the depression.
loc.INT_world_news.19.d: Congress authorised the Reconstruction Finance Corporation in January 1932 to lend to banks, railroads, and other institutions under pressure. Washington hopes emergency credit will prevent further failures, though the agency begins work while unemployment and the wider depression continue to deepen.
loc.INT_eastern.1.d: Polish forces have secured the remaining West Ukrainian positions in Eastern Galicia. Lwów and Stanisławów are now administered from Warsaw, although the region's competing national claims remain unsettled. The war between the Polish and West Ukrainian governments is drawing to a close.
loc.INT_eastern.2.d: Polish and Soviet delegates have signed a peace treaty in Riga. The agreed frontier places western Volhynia, Polesie, Nowogródek, and Wilejka under Polish administration and ends the fighting between the signatories. The status of Vilnius remains a separate Polish-Lithuanian dispute.
loc.INT_eastern.11.d: The Polish-West Ukrainian fighting in Eastern Galicia is ending. Polish authorities now administer Stanisławów alongside Lwów, while West Ukrainian forces withdraw from the region. The territory's future remains a source of dispute.
loc.INT_eastern.12.d: Poland and Soviet Russia have concluded peace at Riga. Their new frontier divides the contested lands of western Belarus and Ukraine, bringing the Polish-Soviet War to an end. The Polish-Lithuanian dispute over Vilnius is not resolved by this treaty.
loc.INT_eastern.12.a: A new map of Eastern Europe
loc.INT_france.1.d: The Republic enters the peace under President Raymond Poincaré. His government faces the twin tasks of securing France's borders and repairing the country after four years of war.
loc.INT_france.2.d: The parliamentary chambers have elected Alexandre Millerand to the presidency. His assertive view of executive authority may test the customs of the Third Republic.
loc.INT_france.3.d: Gaston Doumergue succeeds Millerand after the latter loses parliamentary support. He promises to act as a constitutional arbiter while a new coalition takes office.
loc.INT_france.4.d: Paul Doumer has won the presidential election. A veteran of public finance and colonial administration, he takes office as France struggles with falling trade and cabinet instability.
loc.INT_france.5.d: Following Doumer's assassination, the chambers have elected Albert Lebrun. The new president inherits an unsettled political scene and a deepening economic slump.
loc.INT_france.5.a: A new president must steady France.
loc.INT_france.6.d: The postwar election sends a conservative majority to the Chamber. Veterans and advocates of a firm peace have gained influence, while the government must still finance reconstruction.
loc.INT_france.7.d: French and Belgian forces have entered the Ruhr after Germany falls behind on deliveries. Paris hopes to enforce reparations, but the occupation is already provoking resistance and international concern.
loc.INT_france.7.a: The question of payment now becomes a confrontation.
loc.INT_france.8.d: The Cartel des Gauches has won the parliamentary election. Its parties agree on opposition to the old majority but differ over tax, religion, and security policy.
loc.INT_france.9.d: The franc's collapse has brought Raymond Poincaré back to lead a broad cabinet. Ministers from rival parties are accepting painful fiscal measures in the hope of restoring confidence.
loc.INT_france.9.a: A national union faces the crisis.
loc.INT_france.10.d: Parliament has adopted a new monetary law after years of exchange-rate instability. The franc's lower parity reflects wartime debt and inflation, but the government hopes the settlement will give households and businesses a dependable currency.
loc.INT_france.11.d: The international depression is reaching French commerce and industry. Falling demand and tax revenue are forcing the cabinet to consider relief, public works, and a disputed budget.
loc.INT_france.11.a: The crisis can no longer be treated as distant.
loc.INT_france.12.d: A financial fraud case has raised questions about political patronage and police protection. Opposition leagues use the affair to attack parliament, while the cabinet struggles to establish the facts and retain confidence.
loc.INT_france.12.a: The Republic faces a crisis of trust.
loc.INT_france.13.t: Violence on the Place de la Concorde
loc.INT_france.13.d: Demonstrators have clashed with police near the Chamber of Deputies. Dead and wounded lie in the streets, the government is under immense pressure, and parties across France disagree sharply over what the violence means for the Republic.
loc.INT_france.13.a: The cabinet cannot ignore the streets.
loc.INT_france.14.d: Parties of the left have agreed to act together against the leagues. Their common demonstrations and negotiations are becoming an electoral alliance, though the program and its leadership remain unsettled.
loc.INT_france_news.1.d: France's newly elected Chamber has convened with a large conservative majority. Many deputies served in uniform; their debates turn on reparations, veterans' pensions, and reconstruction. The government must turn victory into a workable peace.
loc.INT_france_news.2.t: France and Belgium Occupy the Ruhr
loc.INT_france_news.2.d: French and Belgian forces have entered Germany's Ruhr district to enforce reparations deliveries. The German government denounces the action, and workers are organizing resistance. Europe's fragile settlement faces a serious test.
loc.INT_france_news.3.t: The Cartel des Gauches Wins in France
loc.INT_france_news.3.d: The alliance of French radicals and socialists has defeated the postwar majority in the legislative election. Its leaders promise a change in domestic policy and a less confrontational approach abroad, but the coalition must first agree on a government.
loc.INT_france_news.4.d: France's currency crisis has returned Raymond Poincaré to the premiership. His cabinet draws support from across the Chamber and seeks to restore fiscal order. Investors welcome the appointment, though its measures will be contested.
loc.INT_france_news.4.a: The franc is at the center of politics.
loc.INT_france_news.5.d: The French parliament has fixed a new value for the franc. The measure formalizes a substantial departure from the prewar gold parity and follows two years of monetary stabilization. Supporters expect calmer markets; critics question the social cost of the policy.
loc.INT_france_news.6.d: Factories and merchants in France report falling orders as the international slump spreads. Government receipts are weakening and cabinet ministers disagree over relief and retrenchment. The country has escaped the first shock, but it cannot escape the world economy.
loc.INT_france_news.7.d: The Stavisky affair has brought allegations of corruption into the center of French politics. Parliamentary opponents demand an inquiry, while leagues call for action in the streets. Confidence in the government is eroding quickly.
loc.INT_france_news.8.d: Violence has erupted near France's Chamber of Deputies during demonstrations against the government. Police and protesters have suffered heavy casualties. The cabinet's survival is uncertain, and the country's parties offer sharply different explanations for the crisis.
loc.INT_france_news.9.d: French socialists, radicals, and communists are moving toward a common front against the leagues. Their cooperation has produced large demonstrations and talks on a joint program. Whether this alliance can govern remains an open question.
loc.INT_FRA_war_damage_desc: Industrial districts and public finances remain burdened by the destruction of the Great War.
loc.INT_FRA_veterans_support_desc: Pensions, medical care, and employment aid help former soldiers reenter civilian life.
loc.INT_FRA_reconstruction_desc: Public contracts and coordinated credit accelerate repairs in the devastated regions.
loc.INT_FRA_heavy_industry_desc: Coal, steel, and heavy manufacturing receive focused support.
loc.INT_FRA_agricultural_recovery_spirit_des: Recovered farmland helps ease the pressure of wartime shortages.
loc.INT_FRA_industrial_credit_spirit_desc: State-backed loans help firms replace destroyed machinery.
loc.INT_FRA_fiscal_pressure_desc: Debt and uncertain revenue constrain the treasury.
loc.INT_FRA_stable_franc_desc: A more credible currency restores confidence in trade and public finance.
loc.INT_FRA_public_works_desc: Infrastructure projects sustain employment and domestic demand.
loc.INT_FRA_depression_pressure_desc: Falling trade and investment are weakening industry.
loc.INT_FRA_budget_restraint_desc: Spending limits defend the treasury but slow construction.
loc.INT_FRA_parliamentary_majority_desc: The postwar Chamber gives the government a working majority.
loc.INT_FRA_cartel_government_desc: The left coalition promises change but must manage its diverse parties.
loc.INT_FRA_national_union_desc: Rival parties are cooperating during a period of crisis.
loc.INT_FRA_cabinet_stability_spirit_desc: Longer-lived governments can carry reforms through the Chamber.
loc.INT_FRA_political_tension_desc: Scandal and street agitation have undermined confidence in parliament.
loc.INT_FRA_popular_front_spirit_desc: The parties of the left have agreed to defend republican government together.
loc.INT_FRA_reparations_expectation_desc: Reconstruction plans rest partly on German payments that remain uncertain.
loc.INT_FRA_frontier_security_desc: Defensive plans prioritize the northeastern approaches.
loc.INT_FRA_collective_security_desc: France seeks strength through treaties and coordinated responses.
loc.INT_FRA_european_cooperation_desc: Diplomacy and commerce strengthen ties with neighboring states.
loc.INT_FRA_trained_reserve_desc: Reserve formations preserve military readiness after demobilization.
loc.INT_FRA_maginot_construction_desc: Parliament has funded a major eastern fortification program.
loc.INT_FRA_mobile_reserve_spirit_desc: A more mobile field army complements the frontier defenses.
loc.INT_FRA_air_defense_desc: Fighter groups and warning systems receive attention.
loc.INT_FRA_mediterranean_security_spirit_de: Shipyards and planners concentrate on the sea lanes linking metropolitan France and North Africa.
loc.INT_FRA_rearmament_desc: Industry is preparing new weapons orders for the armed services.
loc.INT_FRA_armistice_desc: The guns have fallen silent. Ministers must turn wartime administration toward demobilization, reconstruction, and the uncertain peace conference.
loc.INT_FRA_veterans_ministry_desc: Millions return from the front with wounds, pensions, and claims on the Republic. A dedicated ministry must give them a voice.
loc.INT_FRA_rebuild_north_desc: Rail yards, factories, and villages in the occupied departments need an organized reconstruction program.
loc.INT_FRA_restore_railways_desc: Reopening rail links will reconnect mines, towns, and the ports that supply reconstruction.
loc.INT_FRA_clear_battlefields_desc: The former front still contains shattered roads and dangerous munitions. Engineers must make it usable again.
loc.INT_FRA_coal_and_steel_desc: Mining and metallurgical production are essential to restoring housing, rail, and industry.
loc.INT_FRA_housing_program_desc: The state will support housing in towns that lost much of their building stock during the war.
loc.INT_FRA_agricultural_recovery_desc: Farms near the old front need seed, tools, labor, and cleared land before harvests can recover.
loc.INT_FRA_industrial_credit_desc: Public guarantees will keep credit flowing to firms replacing destroyed equipment.
loc.INT_FRA_balance_war_debt_desc: The treasury must confront enormous wartime borrowing while preserving funds for reconstruction.
loc.INT_FRA_poincare_franc_desc: The currency's weakness is undermining confidence. A credible budget and central-bank program can arrest the slide.
loc.INT_FRA_monetary_law_desc: The franc can now be stabilized in law after a long struggle over debt and exchange rates.
loc.INT_FRA_municipal_works_desc: Local works can keep the economy moving when private investment contracts.
loc.INT_FRA_depression_response_desc: The world slump has reached France. The cabinet must weigh austerity against jobs and credit.
loc.INT_FRA_protect_employment_desc: Public orders and relief can limit unemployment, though they strain the budget.
loc.INT_FRA_budget_retrenchment_desc: A restrained budget may stabilize public finances, at the cost of slower recovery.
loc.INT_FRA_modernize_industry_desc: New machinery and management can raise productivity after the first wave of reconstruction.
loc.INT_FRA_social_insurance_desc: Illness and old age should no longer throw working families into destitution.
loc.INT_FRA_blue_horizon_desc: The 1919 election has produced a conservative majority shaped by the men who fought the war.
loc.INT_FRA_republican_institutions_desc: The Chamber and the Senate must contain bitter divisions without sacrificing the authority of civil government.
loc.INT_FRA_women_civic_campaign_desc: Organizations pressing for women's political rights deserve a hearing, even while the Senate resists reform.
loc.INT_FRA_cartel_des_gauches_desc: The left's electoral alliance challenges the postwar majority and promises a different course for the Republic.
loc.INT_FRA_herriot_cabinet_desc: A new majority wants tax reform and a less confrontational foreign policy.
loc.INT_FRA_laicite_debate_desc: Religious education and the status of Alsace-Lorraine test the coalition's ability to govern.
loc.INT_FRA_poincare_national_union_desc: A monetary crisis brings rivals into a broad cabinet pledged to restore confidence.
loc.INT_FRA_cabinet_stability_desc: Longer-lived ministries can act where rapid cabinet turnover has stalled reform.
loc.INT_FRA_election_1928_desc: Voters judge the government's recovery program and the future direction of the Chamber.
loc.INT_FRA_antiparliamentary_leagues_desc: Street movements denounce the parliamentary system and test the state's ability to keep public order.
loc.INT_FRA_stavisky_crisis_desc: A financial scandal has deepened suspicion of ministers, police, and parliamentary influence.
loc.INT_FRA_february_sixth_desc: Violence outside the Chamber brings the regime's legitimacy into question.
loc.INT_FRA_doumergue_union_desc: An emergency cabinet seeks to calm the streets and restore parliamentary confidence.
loc.INT_FRA_popular_front_desc: Socialists, communists, and radicals unite against the leagues and prepare a common electoral program.
loc.INT_FRA_republican_program_desc: The left alliance begins drafting a common platform for the next election. Its parties still differ over labor, finance, and the defense of parliamentary government.
loc.INT_FRA_peace_conference_desc: French delegates seek security and reparations in the postwar settlement.
loc.INT_FRA_reparations_commission_desc: An international body must turn treaty promises into enforceable payments.
loc.INT_FRA_rhineland_security_desc: A demilitarized Rhineland and Allied guarantees are central to the French security plan.
loc.INT_FRA_little_entente_desc: Relations with Czechoslovakia, Romania, and Yugoslavia can strengthen the continental settlement.
loc.INT_FRA_ruhr_occupation_desc: German defaults have prompted a Franco-Belgian move into the Ruhr. Coercion may secure payment but risks a wider crisis.
loc.INT_FRA_dawes_compromise_desc: A revised payment schedule offers a way to end the Ruhr confrontation without abandoning reparations.
loc.INT_FRA_locarno_desc: Western border guarantees and German admission to European diplomacy could reduce the risk of another war.
loc.INT_FRA_briand_kellogg_desc: Aristide Briand's proposal to renounce war now has broad international support.
loc.INT_FRA_young_plan_desc: Negotiators have reached a further revision of German reparations.
loc.INT_FRA_european_union_desc: Economic cooperation may do more for lasting peace than another round of threats and guarantees.
loc.INT_FRA_league_security_desc: French security policy needs allies, law, and an effective forum for collective action.
loc.INT_FRA_colonial_exhibition_desc: The Paris exhibition presents the empire to the public while prompting debate over its costs and obligations.
loc.INT_FRA_defend_belgium_desc: Cooperation with Belgium remains central to preventing another invasion through the north.
loc.INT_FRA_eastern_alliance_desc: Eastern partners need credible consultation and material support as European tensions rise.
loc.INT_FRA_review_armed_forces_desc: The army must retain lessons of the Great War while adapting to peacetime limits.
loc.INT_FRA_army_demobilization_desc: The army must bring men home without losing its professional core.
loc.INT_FRA_reserve_system_desc: A shorter active term requires sound mobilization plans and trained reserves.
loc.INT_FRA_fortification_commission_desc: Engineers and generals debate how permanent works should protect the eastern frontier.
loc.INT_FRA_maginot_program_desc: Parliament votes a major line of fortifications for the vulnerable frontier.
loc.INT_FRA_mobile_reserve_desc: Motorized units will give field commanders a response beyond static defense.
loc.INT_FRA_modern_artillery_desc: Modern fire control and ammunition supply should give the army more than its wartime inheritance.
loc.INT_FRA_air_ministry_desc: A unified ministry can coordinate aircraft procurement, bases, and doctrine.
loc.INT_FRA_fighter_defense_desc: Fighter groups and ground observers must protect French cities and industry.
loc.INT_FRA_fleet_modernization_desc: The navy must balance capital ships, cruisers, and protection for long imperial routes.
loc.INT_FRA_mediterranean_security_desc: Sea lanes through the Mediterranean remain vital to France and the empire.
loc.INT_FRA_degaulle_proposals_desc: Officers arguing for concentrated armor challenge the army's inherited methods.
loc.INT_FRA_rearmament_review_desc: French industry and the services must coordinate orders as German rearmament accelerates.
loc.INT_france.15.d: Delegates at Locarno have agreed on Germany's western borders and European arbitration. Paris sees a chance to supplement its security with British and Italian guarantees, while remaining cautious about the eastern frontier.
loc.INT_france.15.a: A new framework for European security.
loc.INT_france.16.d: The Chamber has approved a five-year program to fortify the eastern frontier. André Maginot argues that permanent works will protect France while the army mobilizes. Critics question the expense and the danger of relying too heavily on fixed defenses.
loc.INT_france.17.t: A New Left Majority in the Chamber
loc.INT_france.17.d: The legislative election has returned a second left majority, but radicals and socialists disagree over the next ministry. The president must find a government able to command the Chamber amid falling revenues and rising public frustration.
loc.INT_france.18.d: Gaston Doumergue has assembled a cabinet drawing support from several parties after the February riots. It promises public order and institutional reform, but its members disagree on how far to change the Republic.
loc.INT_france.19.d: France, Britain, and Italy have met at Stresa in response to German rearmament. Their declaration reaffirms existing treaties and Austrian independence, but they have not settled how they will act if the agreements are breached.
loc.INT_france.19.a: The powers seek a common position.
loc.INT_france.20.d: France and the Soviet Union have signed a mutual-assistance treaty. The agreement is presented as a support for collective security, though its practical military meaning depends on the League of Nations and future diplomacy.
loc.INT_france.21.d: Reparations experts have proposed a revised schedule for German payments. The plan may ease political confrontation while giving France a more predictable basis for its claims.
loc.INT_france_news.10.d: European governments have concluded agreements at Locarno. Germany's western borders receive new guarantees, while arbitration mechanisms are meant to contain future disputes. Supporters call this a step toward reconciliation; critics note that eastern security remains less certain.
loc.INT_france_news.11.t: France Votes Funds for the Maginot Line
loc.INT_france_news.11.d: France's parliament has approved a large multi-year program of frontier fortifications. The planned works will guard key routes from the east while the army mobilizes. Debate continues over whether fixed defenses will be enough in a future war.
loc.INT_france_news.12.d: French legislative elections have returned a new left majority. The result weakens the governments that dominated the late 1920s, but the winning parties have not agreed on a stable cabinet. The economic slump makes the struggle over policy more urgent.
loc.INT_france_news.12.a: Paris faces another change of course.
loc.INT_france_news.13.d: France, Britain, and Italy have issued a common declaration at Stresa after Germany's announcement of rearmament. They reaffirm treaty obligations and Austria's independence. Whether the understanding can withstand other disputes between its members remains uncertain.
loc.INT_france_news.14.t: France and the Soviet Union Sign a Pact
loc.INT_france_news.14.d: France and the Soviet Union have signed a treaty of mutual assistance. Both governments describe it as a defense against unprovoked aggression within the League of Nations system. Diplomats elsewhere are weighing how the agreement may affect European security.
loc.INT_france_news.14.a: A new treaty enters the diplomatic map.
loc.INT_france_news.15.t: Reparations Experts Submit the Young Plan
loc.INT_france_news.15.d: International negotiators have put forward a new plan for German reparations. It aims to replace temporary schedules with a longer settlement and to ease disputes that have strained relations since the war. Ratification and implementation still lie ahead.
loc.INT_france.22.d: Paul Deschanel has entered the Élysée after his election by the parliamentary chambers. He inherits the burdens of peace and reconstruction from Raymond Poincaré. His presidency begins amid debate over how much authority the head of state should exercise.
loc.INT_FRA_war_damage_law_desc: The law of 17 April 1919 recognizes a public duty to compensate civilian war damage. Claims offices must now turn that promise into rebuilding across the devastated departments.
loc.INT_FRA_social_insurance_law_desc: The laws of 1928 and 1930 establish compulsory insurance for many wage earners against sickness, maternity, disability, old age, and death.
loc.INT_FRA_family_allowances_law_desc: The law of 11 March 1932 requires employers in covered occupations to participate in family allowance funds. Benefits reach working households with children.
loc.INT_FRA_marquet_public_works_desc: Adrien Marquet's 1934 program commits funds to roads and other public works in an effort to relieve unemployment and improve national infrastructure.
loc.INT_FRA_tours_congress_desc: The socialist congress divides over membership in the Communist International. A majority forms the communist party while Léon Blum and his allies retain the SFIO.
loc.INT_FRA_election_1932_desc: Voters return a left majority to the Chamber. Radicals and socialists must negotiate policy amid the deepening economic crisis.
loc.INT_FRA_february_antifascism_desc: After the violence of 6 February, trade unions and left parties demonstrate against the leagues. Their cooperation begins to bridge old divisions.
loc.INT_FRA_polish_alliance_desc: France and Poland sign a political agreement on 19 February 1921, pledging consultation on European affairs and laying the basis for military cooperation.
