loc.INT_ita_news.17.d: French and Italian leaders have reached agreements in Rome covering Austrian independence and colonial disputes. Their rapprochement may shape Europe's response to German rearmament.
loc.INT_ita_news.18.d: A Nazi coup attempt in Vienna has killed Chancellor Dollfuss. Italy has moved troops toward the Brenner and signaled opposition to a German move against Austria.
loc.INT_ita_news.19.t: Fascist National List Wins Italian Election
loc.INT_ita_news.19.d: The National List has won Italy's election under the Acerbo law. Opposition parties denounce intimidation and violence during the campaign.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.1.d: The speculative boom has broken. Factories lose orders and banks face mounting demands for credit.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.2.d: Prime Minister Hara has been stabbed at Tokyo Station. His death leaves the party cabinet without its central figure.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.3.d: Japan has accepted limits on capital ships at Washington. Naval officers debate whether the new ratio can protect the empire's Pacific interests.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.4.d: A devastating earthquake has struck the Tokyo-Yokohama region. Fire and ruined infrastructure make relief and reconstruction an urgent national task.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.5.d: The revised election law has expanded the vote to adult men without a tax qualification. The Diet now answers to a much wider electorate.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.6.d: Emperor Taisho has died, and Crown Prince Hirohito succeeds him. The new reign opens amid economic uncertainty and sharpening political disputes.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.7.d: Banks have suspended payments as the weakness of the postwar credit system becomes plain. The cabinet faces a struggle to keep businesses and savers solvent.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.8.d: A bomb has killed the Manchurian warlord Zhang Zuolin. The attack draws suspicion toward Japanese officers and tests Tokyo's authority over the Kwantung Army.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.9.d: The yen has returned to the prewar gold parity. Tight credit and falling prices threaten firms already struggling with weak export demand.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.10.d: The government has ratified further naval limits despite opposition within the services. The dispute raises a larger question about civilian control of defense policy.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.11.d: Prime Minister Hamaguchi has been gravely wounded by an assassin. The attack sharpens conflict around his cabinet's economic and naval policies.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.12.d: An explosion on the South Manchuria Railway has become the pretext for a Kwantung Army offensive. Tokyo must reckon with a campaign initiated outside normal cabinet control.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.13.d: The new cabinet has abandoned the gold constraint. A weaker yen and public spending may relieve deflation, though prices and budgets will change rapidly.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.14.d: A new state has been proclaimed in Manchuria under Japanese protection. Foreign governments question whether it is independent in more than name.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.15.d: Naval officers have killed Prime Minister Inukai. A non-party cabinet is taking shape as the military's political influence grows.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.16.d: The League has rejected Japan's position in Manchuria. Japan has announced its withdrawal, deepening its isolation from the postwar international order.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.17.t: Notice to End the Washington Treaty
loc.INT_japan_interwar.17.d: Japan has given notice that it will leave the Washington naval limitation system. The treaty remains in force until the end of 1936, but fleet planners now look beyond it.
loc.INT_japan_interwar.18.d: Political attacks on the constitutional theory of the emperor are intensifying. The dispute places cabinet government under fresh pressure.
loc.INT_japan_news.1.d: Prime Minister Hara Takashi has been killed at Tokyo Station. The assassination unsettles Japan's party government.
loc.INT_japan_news.2.d: Japan, Britain, the United States, France and Italy have signed a treaty limiting capital ships and reshaping naval competition.
loc.INT_japan_news.3.d: Japan has adopted universal manhood suffrage, extending the vote to adult men without the old tax qualification.
loc.INT_japan_news.4.d: Emperor Taisho has died. Hirohito has succeeded him, beginning the Showa reign.
loc.INT_japan_news.5.d: A banking panic has spread through Japan, exposing unresolved postwar debts and threatening wider industrial activity.
loc.INT_japan_news.6.d: Zhang Zuolin has died in a railway bombing near Mukden. Suspicion falls on officers of Japan's Kwantung Army.
loc.INT_japan_news.7.d: Japan has approved the London Naval Treaty. Opposition among naval officers remains strong.
loc.INT_japan_news.8.d: Prime Minister Hamaguchi Osachi has been shot at Tokyo Station. His condition is serious.
loc.INT_japan_news.9.d: After an explosion near Mukden, Japanese forces are moving across Manchuria. The speed of the operation raises questions about who directs it.
loc.INT_japan_news.10.d: Japan has suspended gold exports and allowed the yen to depreciate as the government seeks relief from deflation.
loc.INT_japan_news.11.d: Authorities in Manchuria have proclaimed a new state closely tied to Japan. Other powers question its independence.
loc.INT_japan_news.12.d: Prime Minister Inukai Tsuyoshi has been killed by naval officers. The attack ends Japan's run of party cabinets.
loc.INT_japan_news.13.d: Japan has announced its withdrawal from the League of Nations after condemnation of its actions in Manchuria.
loc.INT_japan_news.14.d: Japan has notified the other powers that it will end its participation in the Washington naval treaty when its terms expire.
loc.INT_JAP_postwar_settlement_desc: The war has enlarged Japan's position in the Pacific. The peace settlement now tests how securely those gains can be held.
loc.INT_JAP_hara_cabinet_desc: Hara Takashi's cabinet brings party politics closer to the centre of government.
loc.INT_JAP_march_first_desc: Korean independence demonstrations force Tokyo to reconsider its colonial administration.
loc.INT_JAP_colonial_administration_desc: Administrative reforms answer some of the unrest in Korea while imperial rule remains in place.
loc.INT_JAP_hara_assassination_desc: The prime minister's murder shakes the party cabinet and its claim to political stability.
loc.INT_JAP_cabinet_succession_desc: The transition after Hara's death tests whether party-led government can endure.
loc.INT_JAP_constitutional_coalition_desc: The coalition formed around Kato Takaaki seeks broader parliamentary authority.
loc.INT_JAP_manhood_suffrage_desc: The new election law expands the franchise to adult men without a tax qualification.
loc.INT_JAP_peace_preservation_desc: The government strengthens its power to suppress movements it regards as threats to the state.
loc.INT_JAP_showa_accession_desc: The death of Emperor Taisho brings Hirohito to the throne.
loc.INT_JAP_first_mass_election_desc: The first election under universal manhood suffrage gives party politics a wider public base.
loc.INT_JAP_hamaguchi_cabinet_desc: Hamaguchi's government pursues fiscal discipline and naval diplomacy amid growing strain.
loc.INT_JAP_may_fifteenth_desc: The assassination of Inukai Tsuyoshi ends the succession of party cabinets.
loc.INT_JAP_national_unity_desc: Saito Makoto's cabinet draws on non-party figures as the services gain political influence.
loc.INT_JAP_emperor_organ_desc: Attacks on constitutional interpretations of the emperor deepen the political crisis.
loc.INT_JAP_export_boom_desc: Wartime demand has expanded Japanese exports and industrial capacity.
loc.INT_JAP_postwar_recession_desc: The speculative boom collapses and exposes fragile firms and banks.
loc.INT_JAP_bank_liquidity_desc: Emergency credit helps contain the immediate financial panic.
loc.INT_JAP_zaibatsu_growth_desc: Large industrial and financial groups strengthen their hold over the postwar economy.
loc.INT_JAP_kanto_earthquake_desc: Tokyo and Yokohama face a catastrophe that demands immediate relief and rebuilding.
loc.INT_JAP_rebuild_capital_desc: The government directs funds, labour and materials toward rebuilding the capital region.
loc.INT_JAP_transport_recovery_desc: Repairing transport and utilities reconnects the devastated cities with the wider economy.
loc.INT_JAP_showa_financial_crisis_desc: Bank failures expose weaknesses left unresolved since the earthquake and postwar slump.
loc.INT_JAP_bank_restructuring_desc: Emergency measures and consolidation stabilize the banking system.
loc.INT_JAP_restore_gold_desc: The yen returns to gold at the old parity, tightening credit during a world downturn.
loc.INT_JAP_showa_depression_desc: Deflation and collapsing export demand deepen the economic crisis.
loc.INT_JAP_leave_gold_desc: The government abandons the gold constraint and lets the yen depreciate.
loc.INT_JAP_takahashi_reflation_desc: Takahashi Korekiyo combines deficit spending and easier money to revive demand.
loc.INT_JAP_public_works_desc: Public works provide employment and support domestic demand.
loc.INT_JAP_industrial_recovery_desc: Exports and government demand have restored much of Japan's industrial momentum.
loc.INT_JAP_shipbuilding_industry_desc: Shipyards expand as naval planning turns toward the end of treaty limits.
loc.INT_JAP_paris_peace_desc: Japan joins the peace conference seeking recognition of its wartime gains.
loc.INT_JAP_league_membership_desc: Japan becomes a founding member of the new international organization.
loc.INT_JAP_shandong_question_desc: The disposition of German rights in Shandong strains relations with Chinese nationalists.
loc.INT_JAP_washington_conference_desc: Negotiators seek security in the Pacific through a new naval and diplomatic settlement.
loc.INT_JAP_five_power_treaty_desc: Japan accepts capital-ship limits as part of the Washington naval system.
loc.INT_JAP_nine_power_treaty_desc: The powers affirm Chinese sovereignty and equal commercial opportunity.
loc.INT_JAP_siberian_withdrawal_desc: The last Japanese troops leave the Russian Far East after a costly intervention.
loc.INT_JAP_shidehara_diplomacy_desc: Diplomacy and trade take precedence over military adventurism in the mid-1920s.
loc.INT_JAP_tanaka_china_policy_desc: The government adopts a firmer line as conflict spreads across China.
loc.INT_JAP_jinan_incident_desc: Japanese and Nationalist Chinese forces clash in Shandong.
loc.INT_JAP_zhang_assassination_desc: The Kwantung Army's killing of Zhang Zuolin exposes the limits of civilian control.
loc.INT_JAP_london_naval_treaty_desc: The government accepts further naval limits despite intense opposition at home.
loc.INT_JAP_mukden_incident_desc: The Kwantung Army uses a railway explosion to launch an occupation of Manchuria.
loc.INT_JAP_manchukuo_desc: The new state in Manchuria formalizes Japanese influence while drawing international criticism.
loc.INT_JAP_league_withdrawal_desc: The League's rejection of Manchukuo prompts Japan to leave the organization.
loc.INT_JAP_denounce_washington_desc: Japan gives notice that it will leave the capital-ship limitation system when the treaty expires.
loc.INT_JAP_imperial_staff_desc: The Army reviews its wartime experience and its responsibilities across the empire.
loc.INT_JAP_naval_lessons: Lessons of the Great War at Sea
loc.INT_JAP_naval_lessons_desc: The Navy studies new weapons and the changing balance among Pacific powers.
loc.INT_JAP_capital_ship_policy_desc: Treaty limits force planners to choose carefully among capital ships and supporting forces.
loc.INT_JAP_carrier_experiments_desc: Naval aviation begins to challenge assumptions about the battleship's primacy.
loc.INT_JAP_army_modernisation_desc: The Army updates training and equipment for a more mobile battlefield.
loc.INT_JAP_naval_air_service_desc: The Navy expands its flying service and develops carrier-based operations.
loc.INT_JAP_kwantung_command_desc: The command in Manchuria gains influence far beyond its original security mission.
loc.INT_JAP_land_doctrine_desc: Army planners examine the demands of a prolonged campaign on the Asian mainland.
loc.INT_JAP_submarine_program_desc: Submarines remain a key part of the Navy's strategy for a Pacific war.
loc.INT_JAP_carrier_doctrine_desc: Exercises refine the coordination of carrier aircraft and surface forces.
loc.INT_JAP_fleet_expansion_desc: Naval planners prepare for construction beyond the treaty framework.
loc.INT_JAP_army_expansion_desc: The Army broadens training as commitments in China continue to grow.
loc.INT_JAP_joint_planning_desc: The services attempt to coordinate plans despite their institutional rivalry.
loc.INT_JAP_imperial_commitments_desc: The postwar empire imposes new administrative and security costs.
loc.INT_JAP_postwar_slump_desc: The collapse of speculative demand has cut industrial output.
loc.INT_JAP_kanto_damage_desc: Destruction around Tokyo and Yokohama has disrupted transport, industry and civilian life.
loc.INT_JAP_kanto_reconstruction_desc: State-backed rebuilding restores transport and productive capacity.
loc.INT_JAP_banking_crisis_desc: Failures and frozen credit strain businesses and households.
loc.INT_JAP_gold_deflation_desc: The restored prewar parity tightens credit and weakens industrial demand.
loc.INT_JAP_reflation_desc: Easier money and public spending support industry and employment.
loc.INT_JAP_colonial_unrest_desc: Independence protests expose the costs of imperial rule.
loc.INT_JAP_party_cabinets_desc: Party politicians exert a stronger influence on cabinet government.
loc.INT_JAP_military_pressure_desc: Officers increasingly challenge civilian authority over national policy.
loc.INT_JAP_national_unity_cabinet_desc: A non-party cabinet seeks to hold together the government after political violence.
loc.INT_JAP_league_cooperation_desc: Japan's League membership supports diplomacy and international trade.
loc.INT_JAP_naval_limitations_desc: Treaty limits restrain capital-ship construction while planners adapt the fleet.
loc.INT_JAP_kwantung_autonomy_desc: The Manchurian command acts with growing independence from Tokyo.
loc.INT_JAP_naval_expansion_desc: Shipyards and planners prepare for construction beyond treaty limits.
loc.INT_JAP_naval_aviation_desc: Carrier aircraft receive stronger institutional support within the Navy.
loc.INT_JAP_home_rule_review_desc: Tokyo reviews the imperial constitution and the division of authority between ministers, officials and the throne.
loc.INT_JAP_reform_bureaucracy_desc: Professional administration can give party cabinets more room to govern.
loc.INT_JAP_korean_cultural_policy_desc: The March First demonstrations prompt a limited effort to ease cultural restrictions while imperial rule remains.
loc.INT_JAP_local_assemblies_desc: Advisory assemblies offer colonial communities a narrow channel into imperial administration.
loc.INT_JAP_womens_associations_desc: Organized women press for education, welfare and a greater voice in civic life after the franchise debate.
loc.INT_JAP_rural_voters_desc: Party organizers build support among farmers who have become a decisive part of the mass electorate.
loc.INT_JAP_cabinet_rules_desc: Clearer cabinet procedures strengthen the prime minister's hand in a still fragile party system.
loc.INT_JAP_election_funding_desc: Campaign finance rules seek to curb the influence of private money without ending competitive politics.
loc.INT_JAP_labour_mediation_desc: Government mediation brings employers and organized labour into a cautious social truce.
loc.INT_JAP_press_law_desc: The government defines the boundaries of public order while trying to preserve a parliamentary press.
loc.INT_JAP_youth_leagues_desc: Youth organizations teach public service and national responsibility across the home islands.
loc.INT_JAP_civilian_control_desc: The cabinet seeks legal authority over military policy as officers challenge party government.
loc.INT_JAP_emperor_in_council_desc: Constitutional advisers attempt to reconcile the emperor's position with responsible cabinet government.
loc.INT_JAP_prewar_political_settlement_desc: The cabinet and the services reach an uneasy settlement before the 1936 handoff.
loc.INT_JAP_trade_missions_desc: Commercial missions turn wartime export connections into durable markets for Japanese manufacturers.
loc.INT_JAP_light_industry_desc: Textiles, chemicals and consumer goods provide work while heavy industry recovers from the war boom.
loc.INT_JAP_rural_credit_desc: Directed credit gives farmers and provincial firms a bridge through the postwar contraction.
loc.INT_JAP_electric_grid_desc: Reconstruction is an opportunity to extend reliable power and modern utilities through the Tokyo region.
loc.INT_JAP_reconstruction_bonds_desc: Long-term bonds spread the cost of rebuilding across the state and private investors.
loc.INT_JAP_small_industry_desc: Loans and procurement contracts let smaller workshops participate alongside the zaibatsu.
loc.INT_JAP_exchange_controls_desc: Careful controls contain capital flight as the banks repair their balance sheets.
loc.INT_JAP_rice_marketing_desc: Cooperatives and clearer markets temper the collapse in farm prices that has shaken the countryside.
loc.INT_JAP_farm_relief_desc: Debt relief and rural works answer the political crisis created by falling rice prices.
loc.INT_JAP_textile_exports_desc: Japanese mills return to overseas markets with competitive prices and improved organization.
loc.INT_JAP_merchant_fleet_desc: Commercial shipping expands to carry the recovery's exports and secure supply lines.
loc.INT_JAP_state_credit_desc: Public credit channels Takahashi's reflation into firms able to expand production.
loc.INT_JAP_machine_tools_desc: Domestic machine tools reduce dependence on imported equipment as industrial recovery gathers pace.
loc.INT_JAP_steel_modernisation_desc: Investment in steel plants gives the recovery a stronger heavy-industrial foundation.
loc.INT_JAP_south_seas_mandate_desc: Japan seeks recognition of its former German islands and their strategic value in the Pacific.
loc.INT_JAP_pacific_guarantees_desc: League diplomacy promises that the Pacific settlement will be upheld by consultation rather than force.
loc.INT_JAP_china_trade_desc: Commercial interests press for an accommodation that keeps Japanese firms active in Chinese ports.
loc.INT_JAP_equal_treatment_desc: Tokyo publicly accepts equal opportunity in China while protecting its existing economic position.
loc.INT_JAP_soviet_border_talks_desc: After the Siberian withdrawal, diplomats seek practical rules for a tense frontier.
loc.INT_JAP_asian_commerce_desc: Trade links across East Asia offer an alternative to costly military expansion.
loc.INT_JAP_manchurian_railway_desc: The South Manchuria Railway remains the centre of Japanese economic and security policy on the mainland.
loc.INT_JAP_northern_frontier_desc: The Army studies the Soviet Far East while the Washington system still limits naval solutions.
loc.INT_JAP_london_compromise_desc: Negotiators balance fleet ambitions with the cabinet's desire to preserve Anglo-Japanese cooperation.
loc.INT_JAP_noninterference_debate_desc: League principles force Tokyo to debate how far sovereignty and commerce should restrain intervention.
loc.INT_JAP_manchuria_administration_desc: Officials and officers argue over how directly Tokyo should control the new continental position.
loc.INT_JAP_recognize_manchukuo_desc: Formal recognition ties Japan to the state established after the Mukden crisis.
loc.INT_JAP_anti_league_bloc_desc: Diplomats cultivate states dissatisfied with the League's judgement on Manchuria.
loc.INT_JAP_new_order_in_asia_desc: The end of treaty diplomacy opens a debate over a Japanese-led order across East Asia.
loc.INT_JAP_staff_college_desc: The Army turns wartime lessons into a professional curriculum for future staff officers.
loc.INT_JAP_nco_training_desc: Better trained non-commissioned officers make conscript formations more dependable.
loc.INT_JAP_field_artillery_desc: Artillery schools and new equipment prepare the Army for firepower-intensive campaigns.
loc.INT_JAP_mechanised_trials_desc: Small experiments with trucks and tracked vehicles test how mobility can support continental operations.
loc.INT_JAP_mountain_warfare_desc: Specialist training adapts Japanese formations to the difficult terrain of East Asia.
loc.INT_JAP_logistics_school_desc: The Army gives transport, supply and staff planning a larger place in its expansion programme.
loc.INT_JAP_joint_staff_desc: A permanent secretariat tries to make Army-Navy planning more than an occasional conference.
loc.INT_JAP_naval_academy_desc: The Navy widens technical education for officers entering an age of aviation and radio.
loc.INT_JAP_destroyer_screen_desc: Fast escorts protect the battle fleet and give treaty-limited Japan more flexible options.
loc.INT_JAP_carrier_air_groups_desc: Dedicated naval air groups turn carrier experiments into an operational capability.
loc.INT_JAP_long_range_submarines_desc: The submarine arm emphasizes endurance and scouting across the Pacific.
loc.INT_JAP_fleet_bases_desc: New bases and repair facilities support a fleet that must operate far from the home islands.
loc.INT_JAP_aerial_reconnaissance_desc: Naval aircraft extend the fleet's eyes and improve coordination between carriers and surface forces.
loc.INT_JAP_civilian_control_spirit_desc: Civilian ministers make a final attempt to restore cabinet authority over national policy.
loc.INT_JAP_rural_relief_spirit_desc: Support for farmers eases the social strain caused by the collapse in rice prices.
loc.INT_russian_news.1.d: Delegates from communist parties have agreed to establish the Communist International in Moscow. The new organization will coordinate revolutionary movements across borders.
loc.INT_russian_news.2.t: Soviet Russia Declares War on Romania
loc.INT_russian_news.2.d: Soviet forces have declared war on Romania while supporting the Hungarian Soviet Republic. Fighting now links the revolutions in Central Europe to Moscow's intervention.
loc.INT_russian_news.3.d: Soviet Russia has declared war on Finland as it intervenes on the side of Red Finland. The conflict adds a new front to the unsettled Baltic aftermath.
loc.INT_russian_news.4.t: The Far Eastern Republic Is Reintegrated
loc.INT_russian_news.4.d: The Far Eastern Republic has been dissolved and its territory reintegrated into Soviet Russia. Moscow now administers the former buffer state directly.
loc.INT_russian_news.5.d: Moscow and Tokyo have signed the Soviet-Japanese Basic Convention, reopening diplomatic relations after the civil-war intervention in the Far East.
loc.INT_russian_news.6.d: Soviet Russia has declared war on Mongolia in response to Roman von Ungern-Sternberg's invasion. Soviet forces are entering the conflict alongside the Mongolian government.
loc.INT_russian_news.7.t: The New Economic Policy Is Introduced
loc.INT_russian_news.7.d: The Soviet government has introduced the New Economic Policy, allowing limited markets and private trade under state control after the civil war.
loc.INT_russian_news.8.d: Soviet Russia has declared war on Persia while supporting the Persian Socialist Republic. The intervention brings the Red Army into another conflict on the southern frontier.
loc.INT_russian_news.9.t: White Russia Declares War on Poland
loc.INT_russian_news.9.d: White Russia has declared war on Poland as its government seeks to restore the former imperial frontier.
loc.INT_russian_news.10.t: White Russia Declares War on Ukraine
loc.INT_russian_news.10.d: White Russia has declared war on Ukraine, opening another front in its attempt to reassert authority across the former imperial borderlands.
loc.INT_russian_news.11.t: White Russia Declares War in Finland
loc.INT_russian_news.11.d: White Russia has opened a northern campaign against Finland and Red Finland. The surviving governments of the former imperial frontier face a new offensive.
loc.INT_russian_news.12.t: White Russia Moves Against the Baltic States
loc.INT_russian_news.12.d: White Russian forces have opened campaigns against the Baltic states. Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania now face pressure from the government in Petrograd.
loc.INT_russian_news.13.d: White Russia has opened campaigns against the governments of Transcaucasia. The unsettled southern frontier is again under military pressure.
loc.INT_GRE_anatolian_overstretch_desc: The campaign deep inside Anatolia strains Greek supply lines and disperses experienced formations across a vast front. Replacements and ammunition arrive slowly, while support for continuing the war is weakening.
loc.INT_turkey_news.1.d: Delegates at Lausanne have signed a new peace with Turkey. The agreement replaces the unratified settlement of Sèvres and recognizes the sovereignty of the state built by the nationalist movement. Questions over borders and the Straits have dominated months of talks, but the fighting that followed the Great War now has a diplomatic conclusion.
loc.INT_turkey_news.2.d: The Grand National Assembly in Ankara has proclaimed a republic and elected Mustafa Kemal as president. The vote settles a constitutional question left open during the independence struggle: authority now rests with a civilian government answerable to the assembly. Foreign governments are watching how the new state will turn victory into lasting institutions.
loc.INT_turkey_news.3.d: Turkey's parliament has adopted a constitution defining the powers of the assembly, presidency, and cabinet. Its provisions affirm national sovereignty and civil equality after years of imperial collapse and war. The document gives the republic a permanent legal framework, though its promises must still be carried into the provinces and courts.
loc.INT_turkey_news.4.d: The governments in Ankara and Athens have reached an agreement to improve relations. The war and population exchange remain fresh in memory, yet both sides see value in a settled frontier and renewed commerce. Their rapprochement could change the balance of diplomacy around the Aegean.
loc.INT_turkey_news.5.t: Turkey Joins the League of Nations
loc.INT_turkey_news.5.d: Turkey has entered the League of Nations. For Ankara, membership marks international recognition of the republic and gives it a forum for defending the post-Lausanne order. The League gains a member at the crossroads of Europe and the Near East as regional security becomes a growing concern.
loc.INT_turkey_news.6.d: Turkey, Greece, Romania, and Yugoslavia have signed a pact to uphold peace and their existing frontiers in the Balkans. The partners promise consultation as demands for territorial revision grow elsewhere in Europe. The agreement gives their recent rapprochement a wider regional purpose.
loc.INT_turkey_news.7.d: Turkey's assembly has extended the vote and eligibility for parliamentary office to women. Municipal rights have already opened a path into public life; the new law carries that participation to national politics. Supporters see another major reform of the republic, while its practical reach will depend on the next election.
loc.INT_turkey_news.8.d: Ankara has presented a state-led plan for factories making basic goods that the country now imports. Public banks and engineers will direct investment toward textiles, chemicals, and raw materials. The program may strengthen economic independence, but it also demands transport, credit, and skilled labor that remain scarce.
loc.INT_turkey_news.9.d: After an Ottoman victory in the Great War, deputies have reconvened in Istanbul to decide how the empire should be governed in peace. The palace retains its authority, but provincial representatives demand a stronger voice over taxation and reconstruction. Foreign chancelleries are watching whether this constitutional settlement can hold together the victorious empire.
loc.INT_turkey_news.9.a: The empire enters a new session.
loc.INT_turkey_news.10.d: Greek forces have landed at Izmir under Allied authorization. The occupation of the city and its hinterland is provoking protests across Anatolia, where many fear that the armistice is becoming a permanent partition. Istanbul's government is under pressure to defend its claims, while local groups begin organizing resistance.
loc.INT_turkey_news.11.t: A National Movement Gathers in Anatolia
loc.INT_turkey_news.11.d: Mustafa Kemal Pasha has arrived at Samsun as opposition to the occupation spreads. Officers and civic groups are drawing together around the demand that the country's future be decided by its own people. Their organization remains uncertain, but a new center of resistance is taking shape beyond Istanbul.
loc.INT_turkey_news.12.t: A New Assembly Opens in Ankara
loc.INT_turkey_news.12.d: Delegates have convened in Ankara to form a Grand National Assembly. With Istanbul under Allied occupation, the assembly claims authority to direct the national struggle and organize a government of its own. Two rival centers now speak for the Ottoman lands, and their dispute will shape the war ahead.
loc.INT_turkey_news.13.t: Ankara Rejects the Treaty of Sèvres
loc.INT_turkey_news.13.d: The nationalist assembly has rejected the peace terms signed by the Sultan's government at Sèvres. Its delegates refuse the proposed territorial losses and foreign controls, insisting that no settlement is valid without their consent. The treaty deepens the divide between Istanbul and Ankara as fighting continues.
loc.INT_turkey_news.14.d: The Greek advance toward Ankara has been stopped along the Sakarya River. Weeks of fighting have exhausted both armies, but the nationalist government has held its capital and gained time to rebuild. Ankara now hopes to turn a defensive victory into a lasting change in the war.
loc.INT_turkey_news.15.d: Turkish troops have entered Izmir after a rapid offensive drove Greek forces west across Anatolia. The victory ends the occupation that helped ignite the national movement, though the future of Eastern Thrace and the Straits remains to be negotiated. Attention is turning from the battlefield to an armistice.
loc.INT_turkey_news.16.d: The Grand National Assembly has abolished the sultanate, ending the political authority of the Ottoman dynasty. Ankara now claims to be the sole government entitled to negotiate peace, while the position of the caliph remains a separate question. The decision marks a decisive break with the imperial order.
loc.INT_turkey_news.17.d: The Turkish assembly has abolished the caliphate and ended the last institutional office held by the Ottoman dynasty. Supporters describe the decision as necessary for a republic governed by its own laws; opponents fear the loss of a symbol recognized far beyond Turkey. Ankara must now manage the political and religious response.
loc.INT_turkey_news.17.a: A historic office comes to an end.
loc.INT_turkey_news.18.d: Turkey's parliament has approved a Latin-based alphabet for the Turkish language. Schools, newspapers, and public offices are preparing to replace the Ottoman script, while teachers face the vast task of explaining the new letters across the country. The reform is intended to expand literacy and reshape everyday administration.
loc.INT_turkey_news.18.a: A new script enters public life.
loc.INT_turkey_news.19.t: A New Opposition Party Forms in Turkey
loc.INT_turkey_news.19.d: Fethi Okyar has formed the Free Republican Party with the approval of President Mustafa Kemal. Its meetings are drawing citizens frustrated by economic hardship and the pace of reform. The government now faces a public test of whether organized opposition can operate within the young republic.
loc.INT_turkey_news.20.t: Turkey and Iraq Settle the Mosul Question
loc.INT_turkey_news.20.d: Turkey, Britain, and Iraq have reached an agreement on their disputed frontier around Mosul. Ankara accepts the border while the parties arrange compensation tied to the region's oil revenues. The settlement removes a dangerous quarrel left unresolved at Lausanne, though it disappoints those who hoped to retain the province.
loc.INT_turkey_news.21.d: The assembly has required citizens to take hereditary surnames. Officials must now update registers and identity papers throughout the republic, replacing older forms of identification with a common legal standard. The measure is another step in Ankara's effort to remake civil administration.
loc.INT_turkey_news.22.t: Rebellion Breaks Out in Eastern Turkey
loc.INT_turkey_news.22.d: Forces led by Sheikh Said have risen against the government in eastern Turkey. Ankara is sending troops to restore control as the revolt tests the authority of the young republic and exposes deep divisions over its reforms. The fighting threatens to draw resources away from reconstruction.
loc.INT_turkey_news.22.a: The government faces a grave test.
loc.INT_turkey.1.d: The Grand National Assembly has adopted a new constitution. It confirms that sovereignty rests with the nation and gives the president and cabinet defined duties under parliament. Deputies now face the harder work of making these rules govern the courts, provinces, and daily administration.
loc.INT_turkey.2.d: Fethi Okyar's Free Republican Party has attracted supporters far beyond the government's expectations. Shopkeepers, farmers, and professionals bring grievances about taxes, credit, and the pace of reform to its meetings. Ankara must decide how a republic built by one movement will accommodate dissent.
loc.INT_turkey.3.d: The Turkish and Greek governments have agreed to put their recent war behind them. The exchange of populations has left painful memories on both sides of the Aegean, but officials now seek trade and practical cooperation. A quieter western frontier will let both states spend more on rebuilding.
loc.INT_turkey.3.a: Keep the peace across the Aegean.
loc.INT_turkey.4.d: Representatives of Turkey, Greece, Romania, and Yugoslavia have signed a regional pact. They seek to uphold existing borders and settle disputes by consultation as new pressures grow in Europe. The agreement cannot remove every rivalry, but it gives Ankara partners in defending the peace.
loc.INT_turkey.5.d: Deputies assemble for the new parliamentary term. Women now hold seats after the expansion of national suffrage, and the government asks the chamber to supervise its industrial and social programs. The republic enters the next decade with more institutions than it possessed at its birth.
loc.INT_turkey.6.d: The government has set out a coordinated program for factories producing textiles, chemicals, and other basic goods. Public banks and engineers will direct investment where private capital remains scarce. The plan promises jobs and independence from imports, but it will test the treasury and transport network.
loc.INT_turkey.7.d: After the victory, deputies have returned to Istanbul to consider an empire no longer governed on wartime orders alone. Provincial representatives demand a voice in taxation and reconstruction, while the palace wants a dependable ministry. The settlement reached here will decide whether victory can become a durable peace.
loc.INT_turkey.8.t: The Grand National Assembly Abolishes the Sultanate
loc.INT_turkey.8.d: The Grand National Assembly has voted to abolish the Ottoman sultanate. Mehmed VI no longer holds political authority; Ankara alone will represent Turkey at the peace negotiations. Mustafa Kemal now heads the assembly government. The caliphate remains a separate office, leaving the dynasty a religious role while its rule over the state ends.
loc.INT_turkey.9.d: Our delegates have signed a peace treaty at Lausanne. The agreement replaces the unratified Treaty of Sèvres and recognizes the sovereignty of the government in Ankara. The war's last territorial and diplomatic questions can now be settled through the new treaty.
loc.INT_turkey.10.d: The Grand National Assembly has proclaimed the Republic of Turkey and elected Mustafa Kemal its first president. The abolition of the sultanate left sovereignty with the assembly; today's vote gives the state a republican head of government and a settled constitutional direction.
loc.INT_TUR_agricultural_recovery_desc: The end of the tithe gives farmers room to rebuild their holdings.
loc.INT_TUR_industry_incentive_spirit_desc: Private investors receive modest support for domestic manufacturing.
loc.INT_TUR_central_bank_spirit_desc: A national bank steadies credit and currency.
loc.INT_TUR_five_year_plan_desc: The state directs capital into essential industries.
loc.INT_TUR_mining_investment_desc: State financing supports surveys and extraction.
loc.INT_TUR_emergency_order_desc: Temporary security powers have restored order at a political cost.
loc.INT_TUR_civil_service_desc: Trained officials carry reforms into the provinces.
loc.INT_TUR_balkan_security_desc: Regional diplomacy gives Turkey a more secure position.
loc.INT_TUR_defense_preparedness_desc: The armed forces coordinate plans and supplies for a new decade.
loc.INT_TUR_provincial_compromise_spirit_des: Autonomy has eased tension between Istanbul and the provinces.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_budget_spirit_desc: The treasury now matches its commitments to dependable revenue.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_industry_spirit_desc: Railways and technical schools support modest factory growth.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_constitutional_order_des: The dynasty, parliament, and provinces have found a durable balance.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_parliament_desc: Victory has preserved the dynasty, but the wartime cabinet cannot govern indefinitely. Deputies return to debate taxes, provincial demands, and the empire's future.
loc.INT_TUR_provincial_compromise_desc: The provinces seek a greater voice after years of requisition and military rule. Istanbul offers administrative concessions in exchange for renewed loyalty.
loc.INT_TUR_customs_compromise_desc: The treasury needs stable duties and predictable trade. A revised customs settlement helps finance reconstruction without returning to wartime expropriation.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_budget_desc: The ministry compares provincial receipts with the cost of railways, schools, and a standing army. Reform will fail unless the treasury can pay for it.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_schools_desc: New classrooms and teacher training strengthen administration outside the capital. Education also gives young subjects a stake in a reformed empire.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_officers_desc: A victorious wartime army still needs modern staff work, logistics, and peacetime discipline. The officer schools revise their lessons from the Great War.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_industry_desc: Rail connections and technical education support modest factories. The court seeks a broader tax base without putting all industry under direct military control.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_slump_desc: Export earnings and credit fall as the world economy contracts. The ministries protect food supply and public works while seeking fresh revenue.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_recovery_desc: Road, port, and industrial projects put idle labor to work. A smaller but dependable program offers a path out of the slump.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_1935_settlement_desc: By the middle of the decade, the dynasty, parliament, and provinces have reached a workable balance. The empire faces new pressures abroad from a firmer domestic position.
loc.INT_TUR_maintenance_of_order: The Law on Maintenance of Order
loc.INT_TUR_maintenance_of_order_desc: The government claims emergency authority to contain the revolt and other violent challenges. Stability may return, but exceptional powers narrow political life.
loc.INT_TUR_izmir_conspiracy_desc: An alleged plot against the president is uncovered during a planned visit to Izmir. Investigators pursue those involved as the republic tests its new institutions.
loc.INT_TUR_great_speech_desc: Mustafa Kemal recounts the national struggle before the party congress. His account defines the republic's origins and the direction its leaders intend to follow.
loc.INT_TUR_free_republican_party_desc: Fethi Okyar organizes an opposition party with the president's encouragement. Public enthusiasm exposes both economic discontent and the difficulty of managed competition.
loc.INT_TUR_menemen_incident_desc: The killing of an officer during a local uprising shocks the government. Ankara responds with security measures and renews debate over the pace of reform.
loc.INT_TUR_1935_assembly_desc: The new parliament reflects the republic's political settlement and includes women deputies for the first time. Its work will carry the reforms into a more uncertain decade.
loc.INT_TUR_civil_administration_desc: Officials in the provinces need consistent training and clear authority. A professional administration should turn laws passed in Ankara into routine practice.
loc.INT_TUR_soviet_friendship_desc: Ankara and Moscow renew their commitment to peaceful relations. Their wartime cooperation becomes a pragmatic treaty of neutrality and nonaggression.
loc.INT_TUR_mosul_settlement_desc: The frontier with Iraq is settled after difficult talks with Britain. Ankara accepts a fixed boundary and turns its attention to internal development.
loc.INT_TUR_italian_rapprochement_desc: Former adversaries improve their relations through diplomacy. Commercial exchanges and mutual assurances reduce one source of tension across the Mediterranean.
loc.INT_TUR_greek_rapprochement_desc: Venizelos and İnönü seek a practical peace after years of war and population exchange. Cooperation across the Aegean gives both countries room to rebuild.
loc.INT_TUR_league_of_nations_desc: Turkey joins the League of Nations as a recognized sovereign republic. Membership gives Ankara another forum in which to defend the post-Lausanne settlement.
loc.INT_TUR_balkan_entente_desc: Greece, Romania, Yugoslavia, and Turkey coordinate to protect the regional status quo. The pact strengthens diplomacy without binding Ankara to an immediate war.
loc.INT_TUR_eastern_diplomacy_desc: Ankara seeks steadier relations with Iran, Iraq, and Afghanistan. Border security and trade offer common ground for future regional agreements.
loc.INT_TUR_peace_at_home: Peace at Home, Peace in the World
loc.INT_TUR_peace_at_home_desc: The republic aims to secure its borders through diplomacy while directing its resources to reform at home. New regional ties make that policy more credible.
loc.INT_TUR_general_staff_reform_desc: The General Staff becomes an independent military command outside the cabinet. Civilian leaders retain political authority while officers plan national defense.
loc.INT_TUR_officer_schools_desc: A generation of officers trained in the independence struggle must now prepare for peacetime command, logistics, and modern combined arms.
loc.INT_TUR_reserve_system_desc: The army registers, trains, and equips a reserve force. A smaller standing army can meet emergencies only if its mobilization system works.
loc.INT_TUR_border_roads_desc: Roads from the capital to the provinces improve both trade and mobilization. Supply failures from the independence struggle remain a warning.
loc.INT_TUR_air_service_desc: Airfields, maintenance crews, and pilot training give the armed forces a more reliable air arm, though resources remain limited.
loc.INT_TUR_naval_training_desc: The navy rebuilds professional training and maintenance after the long wars. Coastal defense depends on crews that can keep a small fleet at sea.
loc.INT_TUR_defense_review_desc: Army, navy, and air officers review the republic's defenses as Europe becomes more unsettled. Mobility and reliable supply matter more than imperial ambitions.
loc.INT_TUR_abolish_ashar_desc: The tithe weighs heavily on farmers rebuilding after a decade of war. Its abolition sacrifices revenue now in hope of larger harvests and a stronger rural economy.
loc.INT_TUR_agricultural_credit_desc: Credit cooperatives and rural lending help farmers purchase seed, tools, and draft animals. Recovery in the countryside will determine how much the new republic can sustain.
loc.INT_TUR_model_farms_desc: Demonstration farms around Ankara test improved methods and show what organized irrigation and machinery might offer the countryside.
loc.INT_TUR_sugar_industry_desc: Domestic sugar production gives farmers a new market and reduces reliance on imports. Factories in the interior link agricultural reform to industrial policy.
loc.INT_TUR_industry_incentives_desc: Tax concessions and legal protection draw private capital into manufacturing. The republic still relies on imported machinery and a thin domestic investor base.
loc.INT_TUR_central_bank_desc: A national central bank gives Ankara a firmer hand over currency and credit. It must steady the lira while trade and foreign investment weaken.
loc.INT_TUR_depression_response_desc: Falling demand and scarce credit threaten the republic's young factories. Ankara reviews imports, investment, and public works as the wider world economy contracts.
loc.INT_TUR_first_industrial_plan_desc: The state directs scarce capital toward textiles, chemicals, and basic materials. A coordinated plan gives new factories the imports, credit, and power they need.
loc.INT_TUR_textile_mills_desc: New textile works process domestic cotton and wool into goods the country has long imported. State planning turns local harvests into industrial supply.
loc.INT_TUR_etibank_desc: A state mining bank will survey deposits, finance extraction, and supply the planned factories with domestic raw materials.
loc.INT_TUR_industrial_recovery_desc: The first state industries are taking shape, but roads, skilled workers, and finance remain scarce. Ankara consolidates the gains before the next round of investment.
loc.INT_TUR_1924_constitution_desc: The assembly replaces its wartime constitutional framework with a permanent republican charter. Sovereignty remains with parliament while the presidency and cabinet acquire defined responsibilities.
loc.INT_TUR_civil_courts_desc: A single civilian judiciary takes shape as separate religious courts give way to republican institutions. Judges and clerks must learn to administer a new legal order.
loc.INT_TUR_hat_reform_desc: New rules for public dress make reform visible in everyday life. The government presents them as a civic break with imperial custom, while resistance reveals the limits of rapid change.
loc.INT_TUR_close_lodges_desc: Religious lodges and hereditary titles lose their official standing. Ankara seeks a common civic authority, but communities accustomed to local religious leadership may object.
loc.INT_TUR_common_calendar_desc: The administration adopts international calendars, clocks, numerals, and measures. Uniform standards make trade, schools, and the railways easier to coordinate.
loc.INT_TUR_local_womens_vote_desc: Women gain the right to vote and stand in municipal elections. The reform introduces political participation at the local level before a nationwide parliamentary change.
loc.INT_TUR_historical_society_desc: Scholars gather in a new historical society to study Anatolia and the republic's past. Their work reaches schools and helps shape a shared civic narrative.
loc.INT_TUR_language_society_desc: The new language society studies Turkish vocabulary and supports literacy after the alphabet reform. Teachers and officials need common terms for public life.
loc.INT_TUR_peoples_houses_desc: Local cultural houses offer lectures, libraries, theatre, and adult classes. The government uses them to bring the republic's reforms beyond Ankara and Istanbul.
loc.INT_TUR_university_reform_desc: The old Darülfünun is reorganized as Istanbul University. New appointments and curricula aim to strengthen science, medicine, and public administration.
loc.INT_TUR_aftermath_of_mudros_desc: The Ottoman armies lay disarmed and the Allies may occupy strategic ground. Istanbul still has a sultan, but provincial officers and local associations are beginning to contest the settlement.
loc.INT_TUR_italian_landing_desc: Italian forces occupy Antalya as the Allied powers divide their influence in Anatolia. Ankara will have to persuade Rome to withdraw while facing the Greek army in the west.
loc.INT_TUR_occupation_of_izmir_desc: Greek forces land at Izmir with Allied approval. News of the occupation carries resistance committees beyond the western coast and turns Anatolian discontent into a national question.
loc.INT_TUR_samsun_desc: Sent to inspect the Ninth Army district, Mustafa Kemal reaches Samsun on 19 May 1919. He begins coordinating officers and local groups who refuse to accept partition.
loc.INT_TUR_amasya_circular_desc: The circular declares that the nation's independence will be secured by its own determination. It calls representatives together and challenges the passive course of the Istanbul government.
loc.INT_TUR_erzurum_congress_desc: Delegates from eastern Anatolia reject mandates and territorial partition. They insist that the eastern provinces form an indivisible whole and choose a representative committee.
loc.INT_TUR_sivas_congress_desc: Representatives from across Anatolia unite the defense associations under one movement. The congress gives the national struggle a countrywide political organization.
loc.INT_TUR_representative_committee_desc: The committee speaks for the congresses, coordinates provincial resistance, and presses the Istanbul cabinet to recognize the demands of the national movement.
loc.INT_TUR_national_pact_desc: The last Ottoman chamber adopts the Misak-ı Milli, setting out the lands and sovereignty the national movement refuses to surrender.
loc.INT_TUR_occupation_of_istanbul_desc: Allied troops occupy the imperial capital and arrest nationalist deputies. The remaining center of independent political action shifts toward Ankara.
loc.INT_TUR_grand_national_assembly_desc: Deputies meet in Ankara on 23 April 1920. Their assembly claims national sovereignty and provides the political authority needed to direct the struggle on several fronts.
loc.INT_TUR_kuvayi_milliye_desc: Local irregular forces resist occupation where the old army cannot. Their flexibility buys time, though scattered command makes sustained campaigns difficult.
loc.INT_TUR_regular_army_desc: The assembly brings the western front under a centralized command. Regular formations replace independent bands and give Ankara a force capable of meeting Greek offensives.
loc.INT_TUR_western_front_desc: The contest with Greece becomes an open war for western Anatolia. Ankara commits its reorganized army while trying to keep Britain and France out of the fighting.
loc.INT_TUR_first_inonu_desc: The army checks the first Greek thrust toward Eskişehir in January 1921. The defense strengthens the assembly's authority and confidence in its new command.
loc.INT_TUR_second_inonu_desc: Another Greek offensive is turned back in March 1921. Ankara gains time to mobilize, but the larger contest for central Anatolia remains undecided.
loc.INT_TUR_kutahya_eskisehir_desc: The July 1921 battles force a withdrawal toward the Sakarya River. Preserving the army takes priority over holding every town on the western approaches.
loc.INT_TUR_tekalif_i_milliye_desc: Emergency requisitions gather transport, clothing, food, and equipment for the army. The burden falls on a population already exhausted by years of war.
loc.INT_TUR_sakarya_desc: After weeks of fighting east of the Sakarya River, the Greek advance is stopped in September 1921. The victory gives Ankara room to prepare a decisive offensive.
loc.INT_TUR_great_offensive_desc: A carefully prepared attack begins in August 1922. Concentrated forces break the Greek front and pursue the retreating army toward the Aegean.
loc.INT_TUR_liberate_izmir_desc: The nationalist army reaches Izmir in September 1922. The western campaign ends, but a formal settlement is still needed for Thrace and the Straits.
loc.INT_TUR_mudanya_desc: The October 1922 armistice settles the fighting with Greece and arranges the return of eastern Thrace without another campaign across the Straits.
loc.INT_TUR_eastern_front_desc: Kazım Karabekir's forces confront Armenia in the east while Ankara seeks a stable Caucasian frontier.
loc.INT_TUR_alexandropol_desc: Victory in the eastern campaign returns Kars to Ankara's control. A lasting frontier still requires agreement with the Soviet republics.
loc.INT_TUR_moscow_treaty_desc: Ankara and Soviet Russia recognize one another's struggle against the postwar settlement. Their March 1921 agreement lays out the principles of the northeastern border.
loc.INT_TUR_kars_treaty_desc: The October 1921 treaty confirms the frontier with the Caucasian Soviet republics and secures Kars within the national settlement.
loc.INT_TUR_cilician_resistance_desc: Local forces resist French occupation around Adana and the southern towns. Ankara seeks a negotiated withdrawal while keeping its main army on the Greek front.
loc.INT_TUR_italian_withdrawal_desc: Italian forces leave their zone in southwestern Anatolia in 1921, removing one occupation front without a major campaign.
loc.INT_TUR_ankara_accord_desc: The October 1921 agreement ends the southern fighting and returns occupied Cilician territory while leaving Hatay under French administration.
loc.INT_TUR_sevres_desc: The Istanbul government accepts a treaty that would partition Anatolia and place the Straits under international control. Ankara refuses to treat that signature as a mandate from the nation.
loc.INT_TUR_reject_sevres_desc: The Grand National Assembly repudiates Sèvres and insists on the National Pact. No settlement can last without Ankara's consent.
loc.INT_TUR_abolish_sultanate_desc: The assembly ends the Ottoman sultanate on 1 November 1922. Authority rests with Ankara before the formal proclamation of a republic.
loc.INT_TUR_lausanne_desc: Negotiators secure international recognition of the new Turkish state in July 1923. Lausanne supersedes Sèvres and closes the War of Independence.
loc.INT_TUR_republic_desc: The assembly proclaims a republic on 29 October 1923 and elects Mustafa Kemal president. Ankara becomes the undisputed center of government.
loc.INT_TUR_abolish_caliphate_desc: The assembly abolishes the caliphate in March 1924, separating the new republican state from the remaining imperial religious office.
loc.INT_TUR_unify_education_desc: The Law on the Unification of Education puts schools under one national ministry and expands the republic's ability to train a new generation.
loc.INT_TUR_civil_code_desc: A new civil code replaces much of the Ottoman family-law framework and advances the republic's program of secular legal reform.
loc.INT_TUR_alphabet_reform_desc: The Turkish alphabet law of 1928 introduces a Latin-based script and launches a nationwide campaign to teach it.
loc.INT_TUR_surname_law_desc: The 1934 law requires citizens to adopt hereditary surnames. The assembly will soon confer one on the republic's founder.
loc.INT_TUR_ataturk_surname_desc: The assembly grants Mustafa Kemal the surname Atatürk in November 1934. His official name and portrait now follow the later republican era.
loc.INT_TUR_womens_suffrage_desc: Constitutional changes in 1934 extend national voting and candidacy rights to women, broadening participation in the republic's institutions.
loc.INT_TUR_izmir_economic_congress_desc: Delegates debate agriculture, trade, and industrial reconstruction in 1923. The government must rebuild an economy strained by a decade of war.
loc.INT_TUR_railway_nationalization_desc: Ankara expands and nationalizes railways to bind the interior to ports and markets, reducing dependence on foreign-owned lines.
loc.INT_TUR_isbank_desc: The new national bank channels capital to Turkish enterprises and supports a domestic commercial sector.
loc.INT_TUR_early_statism_desc: As private capital proves insufficient for heavy industry, the state takes a larger role in financing and building factories.
loc.INT_TUR_republican_peoples_party_desc: The movement that directed the independence struggle becomes the governing party of the new state.
loc.INT_TUR_progressive_republican_party_des: Former comrades organize the Progressive Republican Party in 1924, testing how far opposition can operate within the new order.
loc.INT_TUR_sheikh_said_rebellion_desc: Rebellion in eastern Anatolia exposes deep tensions over centralization, identity, and secular reform. The government responds with emergency powers.
loc.INT_TUR_six_arrows_desc: The party codifies republicanism, nationalism, populism, statism, secularism, and reformism as guiding principles.
loc.INT_TUR_1936_handoff_desc: The independence struggle and first reform era give way to the challenges represented by Turkey's 1936 focus tree.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_victory_desc: A Central Powers victory averts Mudros and the historical partition crisis. The Ottoman government must still address exhausted provinces and the cost of war.
loc.INT_TUR_constitutional_restoration_desc: The victory government reopens constitutional politics to regain legitimacy beyond the wartime cabinet.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_provincial_reform_desc: Greater administrative capacity and negotiated local authority offer a path to holding together a diverse empire.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_railways_desc: Postwar reconstruction focuses on the Anatolian rail network, whose weakness hampered supply and commerce during the war.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_army_reorganization_desc: Experience from the Great War informs a smaller, more coherent army for the surviving empire.
loc.INT_TUR_occupation_desc: The armistice leaves foreign troops at strategic points and limits the government's authority.
loc.INT_TUR_national_resistance_desc: Local defense associations and officers organize against partition.
loc.INT_TUR_kuvayi_milliye_spirit_desc: Irregular resistance recruits quickly but lacks the cohesion of a regular army.
loc.INT_TUR_regular_army_spirit_desc: The assembly has united its field formations under a central command.
loc.INT_TUR_emergency_requisitions_desc: Emergency requisitions sustain the army while straining civilian life.
loc.INT_TUR_sakarya_victory_desc: The defense of the Sakarya has restored confidence in the army.
loc.INT_TUR_great_offensive_spirit_desc: The army concentrates its strength for a decisive campaign in the west.
loc.INT_TUR_sevres_pressure_desc: Partition threatens the territory claimed by the National Pact.
loc.INT_TUR_republican_institutions_desc: The assembly and presidency form the core of the new state.
loc.INT_TUR_railways_desc: Rail construction and nationalization improve inland connections.
loc.INT_TUR_statism_desc: Public investment fills gaps that private capital cannot yet cover.
loc.INT_TUR_internal_unrest_desc: The rebellion and its suppression strain public confidence.
loc.INT_TUR_ottoman_reconstruction_desc: Victory leaves the empire intact, but rebuilding remains a formidable task.
loc.INT_ENG_settlement_desc: The war has ended, but Britain must demobilise its forces and define its place in a changed world.
loc.INT_ENG_coupon_coalition_desc: Lloyd George governs with Conservative support after the wartime coalition wins the December election.
loc.INT_ENG_irish_negotiations_desc: The war in Ireland has made a political settlement urgent for ministers and Parliament.
loc.INT_ENG_anglo_irish_treaty_desc: Negotiators agree on dominion status for the Irish Free State while Northern Ireland remains in the United Kingdom.
loc.INT_ENG_coalition_collapse_desc: Conservative MPs abandon the coalition and bring Lloyd George’s government to an end.
loc.INT_ENG_election_1922_desc: The Conservatives seek a mandate to govern alone under Bonar Law.
loc.INT_ENG_baldwin_1923_desc: Stanley Baldwin succeeds Bonar Law as prime minister amid debate over tariffs and unemployment.
loc.INT_ENG_labour_1924_desc: Ramsay MacDonald forms Britain’s first Labour ministry with support from the Liberals.
loc.INT_ENG_election_1924_desc: After Labour loses the confidence of the Commons, Baldwin returns with a Conservative majority.
loc.INT_ENG_general_strike_desc: A dispute over coal wages and working hours spreads into a national stoppage.
loc.INT_ENG_strike_settlement_desc: The national stoppage ends, though the miners’ dispute continues for months.
loc.INT_ENG_election_1929_desc: The general election returns Labour as the largest party, and MacDonald again becomes prime minister.
loc.INT_ENG_national_government_desc: A financial crisis leads MacDonald to form a cross-party ministry in August 1931.
loc.INT_ENG_election_1931_desc: The October election gives the National Government a large parliamentary majority.
loc.INT_ENG_baldwin_1935_desc: Stanley Baldwin replaces MacDonald as prime minister and leads the government into the 1935 election.
loc.INT_ENG_demobilization_desc: Millions of servicemen return to civilian life while wartime industry adjusts to peacetime demand.
loc.INT_ENG_homes_for_heroes_desc: Housing policy turns wartime promises into a programme of new homes and local services.
loc.INT_ENG_postwar_recession_desc: Falling demand and industrial disruption deepen unemployment after the short postwar boom.
loc.INT_ENG_trade_recovery_desc: The government seeks export markets and shipping work as industry adapts to peace.
loc.INT_ENG_gold_standard_desc: Churchill restores sterling to the gold standard at the prewar parity.
loc.INT_ENG_coal_industry_desc: Coal owners press for lower wages, deepening the confrontation with the miners’ unions.
loc.INT_ENG_rating_relief_desc: The 1929 reforms change local finance and relieve rates on parts of industry and agriculture.
loc.INT_ENG_depression_desc: The global crisis adds to unemployment and strains the public finances.
loc.INT_ENG_unemployment_relief_desc: Ministers expand relief while searching for work in regions hit hardest by industrial decline.
loc.INT_ENG_leave_gold_desc: Sterling leaves gold after a severe drain on reserves in September 1931.
loc.INT_ENG_sterling_area_desc: Common currency ties help Britain and its partners manage trade after the gold-standard crisis.
loc.INT_ENG_ottawa_desc: Britain and the dominions negotiate a system of imperial tariff preferences.
loc.INT_ENG_special_areas_desc: New powers target persistent unemployment in the worst affected industrial districts.
loc.INT_ENG_recovery_1935_desc: Lower interest rates and housing growth aid recovery, though older industrial regions still struggle.
loc.INT_ENG_imperial_settlement_desc: London must reconcile wartime imperial cooperation with growing demands for self-government.
loc.INT_ENG_cairo_conference_desc: British officials reshape administration in the Middle East after the Ottoman collapse.
loc.INT_ENG_egypt_1922_desc: Britain recognises Egypt as an independent kingdom while retaining reserved powers.
loc.INT_ENG_imperial_conference_1926_desc: The dominions press for an explicit statement of equality within the Commonwealth.
loc.INT_ENG_balfour_declaration_desc: The conference recognises Britain and the dominions as autonomous communities of equal status.
loc.INT_ENG_india_round_table_desc: British and Indian delegates debate constitutional reform and provincial responsibility.
loc.INT_ENG_statute_westminster_desc: Parliament gives legal effect to the constitutional equality of the dominions.
loc.INT_ENG_india_white_paper_desc: The government sets out its proposals for a new constitutional settlement in India.
loc.INT_ENG_india_act_desc: The new act expands provincial autonomy and lays out a federal framework.
loc.INT_ENG_paris_peace_desc: Britain joins the negotiations that will set the terms of the postwar order.
loc.INT_ENG_league_nations_desc: The League of Nations becomes a central forum for Britain’s diplomacy.
loc.INT_ENG_washington_treaty_desc: The major naval powers agree limits on capital ships and new construction.
loc.INT_ENG_locarno_desc: Britain joins the guarantee of the western European frontier.
loc.INT_ENG_kellogg_briand_desc: Britain endorses the international renunciation of war as an instrument of policy.
loc.INT_ENG_london_naval_desc: Naval talks extend limitations to further classes of warships.
loc.INT_ENG_manchuria_desc: Japan’s occupation of Manchuria tests Britain’s commitment to the League.
loc.INT_ENG_disarmament_conference_desc: Delegates debate arms limits while European security becomes less certain.
loc.INT_ENG_stresa_front_desc: Britain, France and Italy condemn German treaty violations and discuss European security.
loc.INT_ENG_abyssinian_crisis_desc: Italy’s attack on Ethiopia forces Britain to weigh League sanctions against European diplomacy.
loc.INT_ENG_ten_year_rule_desc: Treasury and defence planners assume no major war is likely in the next decade.
loc.INT_ENG_raf_independence_desc: The RAF remains a separate service despite postwar pressure to reduce expenditure.
loc.INT_ENG_naval_reductions_desc: The Admiralty adjusts its fleet and dockyards to peacetime budgets.
loc.INT_ENG_air_defence_desc: Air staff examine warning, interception and the defence of the home islands.
loc.INT_ENG_imperial_defence_desc: Britain weighs commitments in Europe, the Mediterranean and Asia against limited resources.
loc.INT_ENG_defence_requirements_desc: The committee reviews threats and recommends priorities for future rearmament.
loc.INT_ENG_raf_expansion_desc: Cabinet approves the first stages of a major expansion of the air force.
loc.INT_ENG_naval_rearmament_desc: The Admiralty presses for ships and modern equipment as the international situation deteriorates.
loc.INT_ENG_army_modernisation_desc: The army studies mechanisation and the requirements of a future European war.
loc.INT_ENG_postwar_burden_spirit_desc: The cost of the war still weighs on the public finances.
loc.INT_ENG_housing_program_spirit_desc: Local authorities are building homes for returning servicemen and their families.
loc.INT_ENG_postwar_slump_spirit_desc: Industry struggles with unemployment and falling export demand.
loc.INT_ENG_trade_recovery_spirit_desc: Commercial networks are being restored after wartime disruption.
loc.INT_ENG_gold_standard_spirit_desc: The pound has returned to the prewar gold parity.
loc.INT_ENG_general_strike_spirit_desc: Work in transport and industry has been interrupted by the national stoppage.
loc.INT_ENG_depression_pressure_spirit_desc: The world economic crisis has worsened unemployment and strained the Treasury.
loc.INT_ENG_unemployment_relief_spirit_desc: Relief measures ease hardship in districts hit by industrial decline.
loc.INT_ENG_sterling_recovery_spirit_desc: A more flexible exchange rate supports exports after gold convertibility ends.
loc.INT_ENG_sterling_area_spirit_desc: Currency ties support trade among Britain and its partners.
loc.INT_ENG_imperial_preference_spirit_desc: The Ottawa agreements give Commonwealth trade a preferential framework.
loc.INT_ENG_special_areas_spirit_desc: Public support is directed to districts with persistent unemployment.
loc.INT_ENG_recovery_spirit_desc: New construction and easier credit are aiding recovery, though it remains uneven.
loc.INT_ENG_national_government_spirit_desc: The cabinet draws support from several parties in a national emergency.
loc.INT_ENG_dominion_equality_spirit_desc: The dominions have been recognised as autonomous communities of equal status.
loc.INT_ENG_westminster_statute_spirit_desc: Parliament has codified the constitutional status of the dominions.
loc.INT_ENG_indian_reform_spirit_desc: The 1935 act expands provincial self-government in British India.
loc.INT_ENG_league_policy_spirit_desc: Britain works through the League of Nations to address international disputes.
loc.INT_ENG_ten_year_rule_spirit_desc: Defence planning assumes a major war is not imminent.
loc.INT_ENG_defence_review_spirit_desc: The government has reconsidered the scale and timing of rearmament.
loc.INT_ENG_raf_expansion_spirit_desc: The air force is receiving increased resources and new aircraft.
loc.INT_ENG_naval_rearmament_spirit_desc: The fleet is beginning a new programme of modernisation.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.1.d: The German delegation has signed the treaty at Versailles. Our ministers return with a settlement that promises security, but the costs of the war and the future of Europe remain unresolved.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.1.a: We must make the peace endure.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.2.d: Our negotiators have agreed to create an Irish Free State with dominion status. The treaty leaves Northern Ireland within the United Kingdom and divides opinion on both sides of the Irish Sea.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.3.d: Conservative MPs have ended the coalition with Lloyd George. Andrew Bonar Law now forms a ministry that seeks a mandate of its own.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.4.d: Ill health has forced Bonar Law from office. Stanley Baldwin takes over the premiership as arguments over tariffs and unemployment dominate the Commons.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.5.d: The Conservatives have lost the confidence of the Commons. Ramsay MacDonald forms a Labour ministry, dependent on Liberal support and watched closely by both the trade unions and the City.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.6.d: A general election has given the Conservatives a majority. Baldwin returns as prime minister after Labour's short first ministry.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.7.d: The Trades Union Congress has called a general strike in support of the miners. Trains, newspapers and many public services are disrupted while the government tries to maintain essential supplies.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.8.d: Labour has emerged as the largest party in the Commons. Ramsay MacDonald returns to Downing Street to form a second ministry amid mounting economic difficulties.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.9.d: The financial crisis has broken the Labour cabinet over spending cuts. MacDonald remains prime minister and forms a National Government supported by Conservatives and Liberals.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.9.a: The coalition must face the crisis.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.10.d: Pressure on sterling and the Bank of England's reserves has forced the government to suspend gold convertibility. Ministers now confront a volatile exchange rate and the need to restore confidence.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.10.a: The pound must find a new footing.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.11.d: Parliament has enacted a statute recognising the legislative independence of the dominions. The Commonwealth now rests more clearly on consent than on Westminster's direct authority.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.12.d: Ramsay MacDonald has stepped aside as leader of the National Government. Stanley Baldwin returns to the premiership as the cabinet faces questions of defence, unemployment and European security.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.13.d: Italy's assault on Ethiopia has put collective security to the test. Our ministers debate sanctions, the Mediterranean fleet and the risk that European cooperation will break apart.
loc.INT_uk_interwar.13.a: Consult our partners in the League.
loc.INT_uk_news.1.t: Britain and Ireland Sign a Treaty
loc.INT_uk_news.1.d: British and Irish negotiators have reached an agreement that provides for an Irish Free State with dominion status. Its implementation and the position of Northern Ireland remain politically contentious.
loc.INT_uk_news.2.t: Labour Forms a Government in Britain
loc.INT_uk_news.2.d: Ramsay MacDonald has formed Britain's first Labour government after the Conservative ministry lost a vote in the Commons. The new cabinet relies on Liberal support.
loc.INT_uk_news.3.t: A General Strike Begins in Britain
loc.INT_uk_news.3.d: British trade unions have begun a general strike in support of the miners. Transport and other essential services face disruption as talks between the unions and government continue.
loc.INT_uk_news.4.d: Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald has formed a cross-party National Government amid Britain's financial crisis. The move has split the Labour Party.
loc.INT_uk_news.5.d: The British government has suspended sterling's convertibility into gold after pressure on the currency and the Bank of England's reserves.
loc.INT_uk_news.6.d: The British Parliament has enacted the Statute of Westminster, defining the legislative independence of the dominions within the Commonwealth.
loc.INT_uk_news.7.d: Italy's invasion of Ethiopia has prompted a British debate over League of Nations sanctions and the security of the Mediterranean.
loc.INT_ENG_civic_reconstruction_desc: The wartime coalition has ended. Parliament must restore ordinary debate while the country adjusts to peace.
loc.INT_ENG_welfare_ministry_desc: Public health administration can turn wartime lessons into more dependable services for civilians.
loc.INT_ENG_electoral_reform_desc: The postwar electorate demands a broader voice in the Commons and a more representative settlement.
loc.INT_ENG_education_act_desc: Longer schooling and better continuation classes will prepare a generation for modern industry.
loc.INT_ENG_wireless_britain_desc: The new wireless service can inform the public and give the country a shared national forum.
loc.INT_ENG_social_compromise_desc: Ministers seek practical agreements between employers, unions and local authorities after years of upheaval.
loc.INT_ENG_broadcast_service_desc: A public broadcaster will provide reliable news and cultural programming across the United Kingdom.
loc.INT_ENG_equal_franchise_desc: The 1928 settlement gives women and men the same voting terms in parliamentary elections.
loc.INT_ENG_parliamentary_stability_desc: A stable ministry can address unemployment and security without another constitutional crisis.
loc.INT_ENG_public_works_desc: Roads, schools and municipal improvements offer useful work while industry recovers from the slump.
loc.INT_ENG_industrial_reconstruction_desc: Factories and mines must be made competitive as wartime contracts and overseas demand fall away.
loc.INT_ENG_electricity_grid_desc: A coordinated supply of power will help modern machinery reach towns and industrial districts alike.
loc.INT_ENG_transport_board_desc: Railways, roads and ports need a common plan if British exports are to reach their markets efficiently.
loc.INT_ENG_research_associations_desc: Government-backed research can spread new techniques beyond the largest firms.
loc.INT_ENG_empire_marketing_desc: Commercial networks across the Empire offer a route for British goods while global trade remains unsettled.
loc.INT_ENG_industrial_modernisation_desc: Investment and research can renew the older industries that still support millions of British workers.
loc.INT_ENG_development_areas_desc: Special assistance is directed toward coal, steel and shipbuilding districts where unemployment is persistent.
loc.INT_ENG_housing_estates_desc: Local authorities expand the housing drive, improving living standards and sustaining construction employment.
loc.INT_ENG_public_works_program_desc: Large civic projects can put idle labour to work and improve the infrastructure needed for recovery.
loc.INT_ENG_recovery_investment_desc: Lower borrowing costs and renewed construction give the economy a cautious path out of depression.
loc.INT_ENG_mandate_system_desc: Britain must organise its League mandates while answering growing demands for responsible government.
loc.INT_ENG_palestine_mandate_desc: The mandate requires a difficult balance between commitments, local communities and security.
loc.INT_ENG_iraq_treaty_desc: A treaty with Baghdad can replace direct occupation with a more durable partnership.
loc.INT_ENG_transjordan_autonomy_desc: Local administration under Emir Abdullah offers a less costly and more flexible imperial arrangement.
loc.INT_ENG_iraq_independence_desc: Britain supports Iraq's entry into the League while preserving close strategic and commercial ties.
loc.INT_ENG_middle_east_command_desc: Airfields, ports and garrisons in the Middle East require a single strategic outlook.
loc.INT_ENG_imperial_shipping_desc: Merchant routes link the Empire, and the Royal Navy must keep those routes dependable in a crisis.
loc.INT_ENG_empire_exhibition_desc: A great exhibition in Wembley presents imperial goods and reinforces economic ties across the Commonwealth.
loc.INT_ENG_dominion_consultation_desc: The dominions expect a voice in decisions that affect the common defence and foreign policy.
loc.INT_ENG_commonwealth_defence_desc: Defence discussions with the dominions can turn constitutional partnership into practical cooperation.
loc.INT_ENG_american_relations_desc: The United States remains an indispensable financial and naval partner in the postwar order.
loc.INT_ENG_anglo_french_entente_desc: Regular consultation with France offers a measure of security on the Channel and the Rhine.
loc.INT_ENG_soviet_recognition_desc: Formal relations with Moscow may open trade while giving diplomats a clearer view of Soviet policy.
loc.INT_ENG_rhine_guarantee_desc: Britain helps uphold the Locarno settlement and the principle of negotiated European security.
loc.INT_ENG_trade_diplomacy_desc: Commercial agreements can ease political tensions and keep Britain engaged with continental markets.
loc.INT_ENG_collective_security_desc: The League will only deter aggression if Britain is prepared to give its promises practical weight.
loc.INT_ENG_arms_control_desc: Britain continues to seek verifiable limits even as the failures of disarmament become harder to ignore.
loc.INT_ENG_french_staff_talks_desc: Military discussions clarify what help Britain could provide if a continental crisis becomes a war.
loc.INT_ENG_mediterranean_entente_desc: The route through the Mediterranean remains vital to India, the dominions and the defence of Europe.
loc.INT_ENG_security_guarantees_desc: Britain must decide which commitments it can honour as treaty violations multiply.
loc.INT_ENG_staff_college_desc: Professional education will prepare officers for the changing demands of mechanised and joint warfare.
loc.INT_ENG_territorial_army_desc: The Territorial Army provides trained reserves without returning to the mass mobilisation of 1914.
loc.INT_ENG_mechanisation_board_desc: The Army studies vehicles, signals and logistics before committing to expensive equipment programmes.
loc.INT_ENG_military_training_desc: Exercises and staff work can restore readiness after years of economy and reduced commitments.
loc.INT_ENG_armoured_experiments_desc: Experimental formations test how tanks might support infantry and exploit a breakthrough.
loc.INT_ENG_home_defence_plans_desc: The defence of ports, factories and communications needs a plan for the first days of a war.
loc.INT_ENG_coastal_defence_plans_desc: Coastal patrols and maritime aircraft plans protect the approaches to the British Isles.
loc.INT_ENG_naval_aviation_coordination_desc: Naval aviation planning must connect reconnaissance, carrier operations and the wider air defence system.
loc.INT_ENG_submarine_defence_desc: The submarine threat demands escorts, training and better coordination between the Admiralty and the merchant fleet.
loc.INT_ENG_joint_planning_desc: Army, Navy and Air Force planners establish common priorities for a limited but credible defence budget.
loc.INT_ENG_aeronautical_research_desc: Universities, laboratories and manufacturers will keep British aircraft design at the forefront of aviation.
loc.INT_ENG_engine_research_desc: Reliable engines are the foundation of every future fighter, bomber and reconnaissance aircraft.
loc.INT_ENG_radar_research_desc: Scientists explore whether radio echoes can give Britain warning of aircraft beyond the horizon.
loc.INT_ENG_bomber_command_desc: A central bomber force gives the Air Staff a clear structure for long-range operations.
loc.INT_ENG_fighter_defence_planning_desc: The Air Staff develops fighter interception plans before a permanent wartime command is required.
