Look no further than across our border to see countrymen having turned on each other in the name of communism, declaring the end of nations. How long until they declare our nation dead as well? Will the [Root.GetRulingParty] protect us from this threat?'\n\nThe growth of the fascist movement in [Root.GetName] has been bolstered by the proximity of the communist revolution. Many moderates who might normally dismiss fascism as another misguided ideological experiment find this to be a very real concern for them as well. Given the choice between the communism of our neighbors and a fascist regime, they would admittedly prefer the latter. They might even be willing to actively support it.
loc.endsieg_political.12.a: We will be the vanguard against the red threat!
loc.endsieg_political.13.d: 'If we silence the voices of the people, how can any of us claim to be the voice of [Root.GetName] ourselves? If we fear dissent, if we fear being publicly denounced or ousted by public vote, what we truly fear is that we are hated and reviled by our own citizens. Does the [Root.GetRulingParty] really have so little confidence in its principles?'\n\nA careful and loosely organized, but passionate faction in the government has begun to push for less repressive policies against enemies of the state. They want the public involved in decision-making through referendums and local party meetings, even if this means risking the future of the current agenda.
loc.endsieg_political.13.a: We can discuss this internally for a start.
loc.endsieg_political.13.a.tt: Increases the chance of internal support for arranging elections.
loc.endsieg_political.13.b: Knowing we're in the right, we can afford allowing our enemies to talk more openly.
loc.endsieg_political.13.b.tt: Increases the chance of people voicing support for democracy and forming an opposition.
loc.endsieg_political.14.d: Surprisingly, the call for more referendums and less repressive measures against opponents of the regime has received some support in internal party discussions. While [Root.GetRulingParty] leadership remains skeptical, several influential members have supported a shift.\n\nPerhaps they have confidence that little will change in practice, or perhaps they are secretly traitors to the party cause, as many of their opponents would have it. Regardless, if the public call for such changes should come, some of the leaders of [Root.GetName] are ready to compromise.
loc.endsieg_political.14.a: The choice may not always stand between liberty and death.
loc.endsieg_political.14.a.tt: The government may arrange elections when the policy has majority support.
loc.endsieg_political.15.d: Relaxing the restrictions on what sort of anti-[Root.GetRulingParty] propaganda can be spread publicly has, predictably, lead to an increase in public expressions of dissent. Organized demonstrations and pamphlets are so far found mostly in academic institutions and some of [Root.GetName]'s more unfortunate areas, but there is little doubt that the movement is spreading.\n\nThe nation's leaders are torn over the issue. [Root.GetLeader], who maintains an iron grip on party leadership, has little desire to diversify public debate. The first steps have already been taken, however, and there may be no turning back.
loc.endsieg_political.15.a: The movement appears to grow naturally in the absence of of repression.
loc.endsieg_political.16.d: The demonstrations of public dissent which were once confined to limited areas are now widespread. While people gather in the streets, the [Root.GetRulingParty] finds itself at a crossroads. If we continue allowing this propaganda to spread, the referendums suggested both from within the party itself as well as the opposition may show that we do not have the support of the public. The unity we have strived for is giving way to a plurality of opinions, united against us.
loc.endsieg_political.16.a: Even if reform is happening, we must show our strength by suppressing this defiance.
loc.endsieg_political.17.d: As freedom of expression and assembly have grown to become increasingly accepted in [Root.GetName], the faction within the [Root.GetRulingParty] calling for holding elections has gone from secret conspirators to publicly supported reformers. Despite [Root.GetLeader]'s protests, the country has been making a slow but steady move towards democracy for the past months and an election now seems like the natural next step.\n\nHowever, far from all [Root.GetAdjective] citizens are in favor of democratic reforms. There is still debate within the party regarding whether to wait holding the election until we can ensure a stable development.
loc.endsieg_political.17.a: Those loyal to the [Root.GetRulingParty] will support the decision now.
loc.endsieg_political.17.b: The reforms need broader support before an election can be held.
loc.endsieg_political.18.d: The rapidly growing [Root.GetAdjective] fascist movement has never claimed that they need majority support before they seize power, counting on uniting the nation under their leadership once their rule is established. However, it seems their public support has grown rapidly. Many fascists are now calling [Root.GetLeader] a hypocrite, claiming to represent the wishes of the people while in reality turning a deaf ear to the masses.\n\nThe call for a referendum has been dismissed as typical attempts at disrupting the system by [Root.GetRulingParty] members so far, but at least it's a political measure. If we do not act now, the fascists may choose the violent struggle as a better path to power.
loc.endsieg_political.18.c: If the people want it, we'll hold the referendum.
loc.endsieg_political.1801.d: The rapidly growing [Root.GetAdjective] national socialist movement has never claimed that they need majority support before they seize power, counting on uniting the nation under their leadership once their rule is established. However, it seems their public support has grown rapidly. Many national socialists are now calling [Root.GetLeader] a hypocrite, claiming to represent the wishes of the people while in reality turning a deaf ear to the masses.\n\nThe call for a referendum has been dismissed as typical attempts at disrupting the system by [Root.GetRulingParty] members so far, but at least it's a political measure. If we do not act now, the national socialists may choose the violent struggle as a better path to power.
loc.endsieg_political.1801.c: If the people want it, we'll hold the referendum.
loc.endsieg_political.1802.d: The rapidly growing [Root.GetAdjective] populist movement has never claimed that they need majority support before they seize power, counting on uniting the nation under their leadership once their rule is established. However, it seems their public support has grown rapidly. Many populists are now calling [Root.GetLeader] a hypocrite, claiming to represent the wishes of the people while in reality turning a deaf ear to the masses.\n\nThe call for a referendum has been dismissed as typical attempts at disrupting the system by [Root.GetRulingParty] members so far, but at least it's a political measure. If we do not act now, the populists may choose the violent struggle as a better path to power.
loc.endsieg_political.1802.c: If the people want it, we'll hold the referendum.
loc.endsieg_political.1803.d: The rapidly growing [Root.GetAdjective] paternal autocrat movement has never claimed that they need majority support before they seize power, counting on uniting the nation under their leadership once their rule is established. However, it seems their public support has grown rapidly. Many paternal autocrats are now calling [Root.GetLeader] a hypocrite, claiming to represent the wishes of the people while in reality turning a deaf ear to the masses.\n\nThe call for a referendum has been dismissed as typical attempts at disrupting the system by [Root.GetRulingParty] members so far, but at least it's a political measure. If we do not act now, the paternal autocrats may choose the violent struggle as a better path to power.
loc.endsieg_political.1803.c: If the people want it, we'll hold the referendum.
loc.endsieg_political.19.d: Marxist ideas took root in [Root.GetName] a long time ago, but have gained much more widespread support lately. The movement has spread outside political theory and into political practice, with disgruntled workers and even some high-profile celebrities voicing support. The communists call this class consciousness. The [Root.GetRulingParty] call it a fast track to riots and treason.\n\nShowing little faith in [Root.GetLeader] being willing to implement the reforms they demand, the more vocal communists have called for an immediate referendum to have the current government removed. While we might be able to reverse the momentum of this mass movement, failure to do so will doubtlessly result in the more popular communist method of removal: Revolution.
loc.endsieg_political.19.b: Ignore them, they're just causing trouble.
loc.endsieg_political.19.c: The referendum is preferable to a bloody revolt.
loc.endsieg_political.20.d: Unsurprisingly, the idea of the people ruling the nation they inhabit can easily grow very popular among the people. The [Root.GetRulingParty], of course, sees the idea of democracy as represented by these movements - freedom of speech, public elections, free press - merely populist rhetoric meant to weaken [Root.GetLeader]'s government.\n\nHowever, there is no denying those ideas have taken hold among the [Root.GetAdjective] population. In true democratic fashion, they call for a public referendum on replacing the current regime. Although currently easy to ignore, these ideas have a way of growing very persistent. What will happen to us if we make peaceful revolution impossible?
loc.endsieg_political.20.c: If we accept the referendum, perhaps we can preserve our legacy.
loc.endsieg_political.21.d: Having been refused their referendum, almost a token attempt at seizing power legally, the fascists have used their significant public support and connections in the [Root.GetAdjective] military to attempt a coup. The [Root.GetRulingParty] government has refused their terms and claims it is going to fight to the end to preserve [Root.GetName] as we know it.
loc.endsieg_political.21.a: We will stop them at any cost!
loc.endsieg_political.21.b: The fascists carry the true spirit of [Root.GetName]!
loc.endsieg_political.22.d: After their request for a referendum was denied, the few reformers of the communist movement in [Root.GetName] rapidly lost influence to the more radical elements. With the [Root.GetRulingParty]'s refusal to acknowledge the public support for the suggested reforms, the romantic view of the revolution gradually grew more widespread and the leaders of the movement become those who could most easily start a riot. Those riots have now erupted into a full-scale civil war, with the future of the nation at stake.
loc.endsieg_political.22.a: We won't allow them to ruin our country!
loc.endsieg_political.22.b: The fire of the revolution must be extinguished with the blood of the oppressors!
loc.endsieg_political.23.d: After their attempt at a public referendum to institute democracy was refused, the people behind the suggestion have dismissed the [Root.GetLeader] regime as incorrigible. A broad coalition of rebel groups, united by their common goal of instituting more representative political systems in [Root.GetName], have taken up arms and announced that they will not rest until the [Root.GetRulingParty] is overthrown.
loc.endsieg_political.23.a: Spare us from this mob rule!
loc.endsieg_political.24.d: The [Root.GetAdjective] people's infatuation with nationalistic pride and attempts to revive the glories of the past appears to have passed. A rude awakening for its ardent supporters, whose uniforms, militaristic posturing and over-the-top speeches are now more commonly the subject of mockery than sympathies.\n\nOnce considered a threat to the [Root.GetRulingParty] power base, [Root.GetAdjective] fascism is now increasingly seen as an absurd, extremist position and an attack on the most fundamental values of our nation, the very nation they claim to hold in such high regard. The word seems more suited as an insult than a political designation.
loc.endsieg_political.25.d: Many communists had predicted that [Root.GetName] was going to be the next nation to fall to the so-called international revolution, but after a few months of strikes and red flags in the streets, the movement seems to have died down. The working class, the supposed driving force of the revolution, has more pressing concerns than overthrowing [Root.GetLeader] and seem decidedly unimpressed with how well these revolutions have played out elsewhere. Meanwhile, the intellectuals who wrote passionate calls for slitting the throats of the oppressors have turned out to be surprisingly reluctant to instigate anything that might actually upset their comfortable lifestyle.\n\nTalk of the revolution will likely continue, whether over cheap beers or expensive wines, but it will likely be talk and nothing more.
loc.endsieg_political.26.d: After a few months of loud opposition against [Root.GetLeader]'s regime, calling for public elections and more liberal laws on freedom of assembly and speech, the movement seems to have fallen apart. People now express more concern about the stability of [Root.GetName] if such reforms were to take place, with those who clamor for democracy being seen more as troublemakers than everything else.\n\nMore mysteriously, many of the leading figures of the movement appear to have gone missing or stopped their work suddenly. Perhaps some of them chose to go into exile when they saw the failure of their efforts. Regardless, the [Root.GetRulingParty] government denies all knowledge and involvement.
loc.endsieg_political.27.d_fascism: After [Root.GetRulingParty]'s recent rise to power, [Root.GetLeader] announced that [Root.GetName] would no longer keep its Neutral Foreign Policy.\n'The world has become tangled and complex. We are no longer safe on our own. We must stand with our fascist partners against our enemies. If we do not choose a side, we will perish alone.'
loc.endsieg_political.27.d_communism: After [Root.GetRulingParty]'s recent rise to power, [Root.GetLeader] announced that [Root.GetName] would no longer keep its Neutral Foreign Policy.\n'The world has become tangled and complex. This country has always stood on it principles and been ready to defend them. We are no longer safe on our own. Neutrality is no longer the safe haven it used to be and those who seek power in this world do not respect it. We must stand with our communist brothers against the powers that seek to oppress us. Against the bourgeois majority who wants nothing more than keep us down. If we do not take a stand, we will perish alone.'
loc.endsieg_political.28.d: The end of the terrible civil war that has devastated our land draws to an end, and we have finally reached a political agreement. We now see eye to eye with our fellow [Root.GetAdjective]s, and together we will rebuild our great nation. The enemies that have sought to capitalize on our infighting must now face a united [Root.GetAdjective] state.\n\nThe new [Root.GetRulingIdeology] [Root.GetName] will never be divided again!

loc.endsieg_no_rations_desc: The national ration stockpile cannot feed all deployed personnel today. Combat readiness suffers until supplies recover.

loc.INT_weimar.1.d: Chancellor Marx asks President Ebert to dissolve the Reichstag before deputies can overturn the government's emergency economic decrees. The cabinet argues that currency stabilization needs time, but its opponents call the move an evasion of parliamentary scrutiny. Voters now decide whether Marx can build a dependable majority.
loc.INT_weimar.1.a: The nation returns to the polls.
loc.INT_weimar.2.d: The parties fail to sustain a governing coalition, and President Ebert dissolves the Reichstag once more. Germany faces another election in the same year while questions of reparations, economic recovery, and the republic's authority divide the chamber. Every party campaigns for a mandate it may struggle to use.
loc.INT_weimar.3.d: A fragile coalition gives way, and President Hindenburg dissolves the Reichstag. The government hopes an election will produce a clearer parliamentary majority, but divisions between democratic parties and the political extremes remain sharp. The republic must ask its voters to settle another cabinet crisis.
loc.INT_weimar.3.a: The coalition must face the voters.
loc.INT_weimar.4.d: The Reichstag votes down Chancellor Brüning's emergency decree, and President Hindenburg responds by dissolving the chamber. Brüning seeks to continue governing through presidential authority while the country heads toward an election amid unemployment and austerity. The balance between parliament and the presidency grows more precarious.
loc.INT_weimar.5.d: Chancellor von Papen governs with President Hindenburg's support but commands almost no votes in the Reichstag. The president dissolves parliament and calls an election in the hope of breaking the impasse. The parties prepare for a bitter contest as street violence and economic hardship unsettle the republic.
loc.INT_weimar.6.t: The Reichstag Dissolved After a Vote of No Confidence
loc.INT_weimar.6.d: The Reichstag delivers an overwhelming vote of no confidence in Chancellor von Papen. Instead of yielding to the chamber, the government presents a dissolution order signed by President Hindenburg. Germany heads to the polls again while the struggle between presidential rule and parliamentary authority intensifies.
loc.INT_weimar.6.a: Parliament has reached another dead end.
loc.INT_weimar.7.t: The Reichstag Dissolved for a March Election
loc.INT_weimar.7.d: President Hindenburg dissolves the Reichstag and calls a new election for March. The collapse of successive cabinets leaves the country facing another campaign, with the political extremes gaining ground. The next chamber will determine whether parliamentary government can regain its footing.
loc.INT_weimar.8.d: The imperial cabinet is leaving office as defeat and revolution end the old political order. Ministers and military advisers associated with the wartime government submit their resignations, while the new authorities face demobilization, shortages, and unrest. A civilian republican cabinet must now take responsibility for the state.
loc.INT_weimar.9.d: A republican cabinet takes office and begins replacing imperial advisers with civilian figures from the new political order. Its president must establish authority over the administration while the country confronts peace negotiations, demobilization, and political violence. Chancellors will rise and fall as parties attempt to govern the republic.
loc.INT_weimar.9.a: Begin the work of the republic.
loc.INT_weimar.10.d: The failed Kapp Putsch has shaken confidence in Defence Minister Gustav Noske. Critics blame his handling of the armed forces and demand a new course; Noske leaves office as the cabinet tries to reassert civilian authority. Carl Severing becomes available to help defend the republic's institutions.
loc.INT_weimar.11.d: Former finance minister Matthias Erzberger has been assassinated. His signature on the armistice and his support for the republic have made him a target of the nationalist right. The government loses an experienced reformer as political murder threatens public life.
loc.INT_weimar.12.d: Walther Rathenau enters the foreign ministry as the republic searches for room to maneuver abroad. An industrialist with broad international contacts, he must navigate reparations, relations with the victorious powers, and Germany's isolation. His appointment offers a diplomatic opening, though critics at home remain fierce.
loc.INT_weimar.13.d: Foreign Minister Walther Rathenau has been murdered by right-wing extremists. His efforts to negotiate with other powers have drawn violent opposition from enemies of the republic. Crowds gather in protest while the government faces the urgent task of protecting its officials and the constitutional order.
loc.INT_weimar.14.d: Reichsbank president Rudolf Havenstein has died while Germany struggles through a devastating currency crisis. Prices change faster than wages can follow, and confidence in the mark is collapsing. The government must find a successor capable of restoring monetary order.
loc.INT_weimar.15.t: Schacht Takes Charge of the Reichsbank
loc.INT_weimar.15.d: Hjalmar Schacht takes charge of the Reichsbank after helping to stabilize the currency. The immediate panic is easing, but the government still needs credit, budget discipline, and a workable approach to foreign obligations. Schacht now becomes a central adviser in the effort to rebuild financial confidence.
loc.INT_weimar.16.d: Paul von Hindenburg wins the presidential election and succeeds the late Friedrich Ebert. The celebrated former field marshal now holds the republic's highest office, even though many of his supporters distrust the system he is sworn to uphold. His use of presidential powers will shape every future cabinet.
loc.INT_weimar.17.d: Hjalmar Schacht resigns from the Reichsbank as disputes over reparations and financial policy deepen. His departure removes a prominent advocate of monetary stability from the government's circle. Ministers must now defend their economic course without the banker who helped end the inflation crisis.
loc.INT_weimar.18.d: Carl Severing is forced from office during the struggle over control of Prussia. The removal of republican officials from Germany's largest state weakens a major institutional safeguard of the Weimar system. The cabinet loses an experienced defender of constitutional government.
loc.INT_weimar.18.a: The cabinet loses an experienced adviser.
loc.INT_weimar.19.d: Wilhelm Groener leaves the cabinet amid mounting pressure from the army and the political right. As a former senior officer and minister, he has tried to keep the armed forces tied to the government. His departure exposes the presidential cabinet to further instability.
loc.INT_weimar.20.d: Philipp Scheidemann forms a cabinet drawn from the parties supporting the new National Assembly. The government must build republican institutions while facing food shortages, demobilization, unrest, and the terms of peace. Its parliamentary majority is broad, but the challenges before it are immediate.
loc.INT_weimar.21.d: Gustav Bauer is asked to form a new cabinet after Philipp Scheidemann resigns over the proposed peace settlement. The government must decide how to respond to Allied demands while preserving enough parliamentary support to survive. Bauer inherits a republic whose first major test cannot be postponed.
loc.INT_weimar.22.d: Hermann Müller takes office in the aftermath of the Kapp Putsch. A general strike has defeated the coup, but the government still faces unrest, distrust of the armed forces, and demands for accountability. Müller must rebuild a workable coalition before the next parliamentary contest.
loc.INT_weimar.23.d: Constantin Fehrenbach forms a cabinet after elections leave the parties of the original republican coalition without their former majority. His Center-led government must seek support across a divided Reichstag. Reparations and domestic recovery remain pressing while every vote becomes harder to secure.
loc.INT_weimar.24.d: Joseph Wirth takes the chancellorship as Germany confronts an Allied reparations ultimatum. He hopes that accepting obligations and demonstrating compliance will create room for later revision. The strategy demands painful compromises and leaves his coalition vulnerable to attacks from both left and right.
loc.INT_weimar.25.d: Non-party businessman Wilhelm Cuno forms a cabinet as foreign pressure and economic instability grow. French and Belgian demands over reparations threaten the Ruhr, the center of German heavy industry. His government must choose how to answer while the mark weakens and public confidence erodes.
loc.INT_weimar.26.d: Gustav Stresemann brings together a grand coalition amid occupation, passive resistance, and runaway inflation. The government needs to end the economic emergency while asking Germans to accept difficult compromises. Its survival depends on holding parties together through a crisis that reaches every household.
loc.INT_weimar.27.d: Wilhelm Marx succeeds Stresemann and attempts to steady the republic after the worst of the currency crisis. His cabinet faces the unfinished questions of reparations, political extremism, and Germany's place in Europe. A dependable parliamentary majority remains elusive.
loc.INT_weimar.28.d: Hans Luther takes office at the head of a new coalition after Marx's cabinet falls. Stabilization has opened a chance for recovery, but the government still faces contested budget choices and foreign-policy obligations. Luther must keep rival parties cooperating long enough to turn short-term calm into lasting order.
loc.INT_weimar.29.d: Wilhelm Marx returns to the chancellorship after Luther resigns. The republic enjoys a measure of economic relief, yet arguments over schools, budgets, and coalition partners continue to unsettle parliament. Marx must assemble support issue by issue to keep the government functioning.
loc.INT_weimar.30.d: Hermann Müller returns to lead a broad coalition that brings together parties with sharply different economic priorities. They agree on defending parliamentary government, but unemployment insurance and the public finances threaten to divide them. Müller must turn electoral support into a durable governing compromise.
loc.INT_weimar.31.d: Heinrich Brüning forms a cabinet as the grand coalition breaks apart during the economic downturn. Without a secure Reichstag majority, he relies increasingly on President Hindenburg's emergency powers. Cuts in spending and rising unemployment test both the cabinet and the republic's constitutional habits.
loc.INT_weimar.32.t: Franz von Papen Appointed Reich Chancellor
loc.INT_weimar.32.d: Franz von Papen becomes chancellor with President Hindenburg's backing despite lacking a parliamentary majority. His small cabinet looks to presidential decrees rather than party negotiation, while the depression continues to deepen. The Reichstag and the streets are unlikely to accept this arrangement quietly.
loc.INT_weimar.33.t: Kurt von Schleicher Appointed Reich Chancellor
loc.INT_weimar.33.d: General Kurt von Schleicher replaces von Papen and tries to build support across the political divide. He hopes to draw unions and parts of the nationalist right into a new governing arrangement, but neither parliament nor the president offers him a secure base. Time is running short for the republic's final presidential cabinet.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.1.t: Send a peace offer to the French?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.1.d: We have taken control of Northern France, and thus the bulk of French industry and resources. We have entered the gates of Paris and Versailes, just as we have in 1871. Shall we end this war, just as our forefathers have, with an honourable peace?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.1.a: Send the offer. We shall ensure that this time, the peace shall remain.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.2.d: We have lost the bulk of our industry, resources, and most importantly our capital city, Paris. Whilst we could resist the dreaded Boche, chances are that the Germans are going to only give us harsher terms if we were to refuse the armistice now.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.2.a: We must end this war, even if we are on the losing side.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.2.b: We shall fight to the bitter end.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.3.d: The French have refused our offer of an armistice! We have no choice but to fight to the bitter end now.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.3.a: If the French wish to continue this senseless slaughter, so be it.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.4.t: France Surrenders! Armistice of Marne Signed!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.4.d: With our successful Spring Offensive, the so-called Kaiserschlacht, as the soldiers are calling it now, and the subsequent capture of Paris, the Third French Republic has officially agreed to an armistice which has been signed at Marne today ending the war between our two countries. France has agreed to demobilize its military and expel British forces from the mainland as soon as possible with a peace treaty to be soon written under our termss. \n\n With the French out of the war, the rest of the Entente shall follow suit with negotiations on an armistice and final treaty soon.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.5.t: The French have accepted the German Armistice
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.5.d: The French have agreed to an armistice with the Germans, and as such, the war on mainland Europe is over. Regardless of victories and defeats in battles, it would seem that the war is sadly lost. With the French out of the war, it will only be a matter of time before the Germans come streaming through the Turks to retake Africa, and our economy and people will never support a never-ending war.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.6.d: With the fall of France and the expulsion of British forces from mainland Europe the United Kingdom has bitterly agreed to an Armistice between our two nations which has been signed today at Calais. While the process of drawing up a final treaty shall start soon between our nations it is unlikely that we will be able to make any drastic decisions as the United Kingdom still has the worlds largest fleet and the best protection from invasion in the form of an island.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.7.d: The British have refused our offers of ceasefire, although whether we will go to war with them again remains to be seen...
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.8.d: Since turning our backs on the Triple Alliance, now the Central Powers, it would seem that the promises that Britain and France made will never come to fruition. As much as we wish for Italy to be unified, it would seem that we should have chosen to reclaim our old posessions in France instead...
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.8.a: Let us hope for a lenient peace.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.8.b: The dream of Italia Irridente, a unified Italy, shall never die!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.9.d: With France gone and the United Kingdom with the Americans shortly following suite the Italians have reluctantly agreed to an Armistice near Vittorio Veneto along with pressure of the people to whom the unpopularity of the war has grown very much over these past few years, the process of drawing up a final treaty shall begin soon.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.10.d: The Italians have chosen to fight on to the bitter end. With diplomacy failing us in this our of need we will have to do this the hard way.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.11.t: The German Empire offers an Armistice!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.11.d: A distant war in Europe, wars that we usually do not care for yet were dragged into this time. The Germans promise lenient terms on us, as well as no reperations of any sort. In essence, we're going off scot-free. What shall we do?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.11.b: We shall fight to the end!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.12.d: The Americans who have just last year joined the war taking a major part only early this year have agreed to an Armistice at Calais with the British following the surrender of France, the peace which stands between our two nations is and will be a white peace with the Americans most likely returning back to their isolationist stature.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.13.d: Despite our lenient peace offer, the Americans have rejected our offers of peace.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.13.a: Then so be it. We shall learn to invade them in time...
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.14.t: A letter from the Emperor of Germany
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.14.d: The Empires of Japan and Germany are distant and share a lack of respect from the international stage. Sakhalin, a prize rightfully won by the Japanese in the 1905 war was denied to you from a lack of respect by the British and Americans. The German Empire is willing to include transfers of French Indochina in the final peace treaty, as well as any islands held by the Japanese Empire that currently belong to the Deutches Kaiserreich. The empire of Germany is willing to treat the Empire of Japan as an equal on the international stage, and foster a future friendship with it.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.14.b: This seems too good to be true..
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.15.t: The Japanese have accepted an armistice!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.15.d: The Japanese have accepted an armistice, with a letter written by Wilhelm II himself appealing to the Emperor of Japan. Although its precise contents are unknown, we will likely have to give up a few concessions in the east to satisfy them.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.15.a: They're just some desolate islands anyway.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.16.d: The Japanese have declined peace, despite a letter by the Wilhelm II supposedly clamoring for peace.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.16.a: Our Emperor can't do diplomacy very well, now can he?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.17.d: Our participation in this distant European war is largely nominal. A formal cessation of hostilities will change very little on the ground, but we could ask for the status of the German concessions.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.17.a: Let's not push it. Ask for peace regardless of the terms.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.17.c: We will continue this war, on paper at least!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.18.t: Chinese armistice - recognition of German Qingdao
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.18.d: The Chinese have oddly allowed our concession at Qingdao to stand, and should the Chinese actually have control over Qingdao, we shall resume our normal administration promptly. However, should another country, such as Japan hold it, they wll not evacuate the treaty port.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.19.d: The Chinese agree to a peace only if we recognize the end of our concessions there. We may not necessarily control them, however...
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.20.d: Germany has confirmed posession of Qingdao/Tsingdao with China, but it is currently in our hands. Shall we recognize the claim?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.20.a: Yes, transfer Qingdao to the Chinese.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.21.d: Even with the de facto cessation of hostilities, the Chinese have oddle decided to keep fighting us on paper.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.22.d: We have lost control over Qingdao, and the Chinese have incorporated it into their state. What shall we do?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.22.a: We are defeated. Sign it off.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.22.b: We shall retake it, and then some.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.23.d: We have lost yet another war to the filthy barbarians, and yet the people are calling for our surrender of territories. What now?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.23.b: We shall drive them off Chinese soil!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.25.d: Our French allies lie defeated, our lands invaded. This means the de facto nullification of the Entente Cordiale, for we now stand alone against the German war machine!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.123.d: Belgium's status in the treaty is currently open, what shall we do with this artificial buffer state?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.123.c: Take lands to the Maas, then puppet them.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.123.dd: Take their Maas lands, puppet them, and take the Congo.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.126.d: You wish to take land to the Meuse (Maas) from Belgium, but NOT THE CONGO.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.127.d: You wish to take the land behind the Meuse and the Congo
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.128.d: You wish to Split up belgium into Flanders and Wallonia, and take the Congo
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.257.t: The Fate of the Colonial Empires
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.257.d: With the Entente defeated, its colonial empires cannot remain as they were. The territories named in the settlement will be transferred to German administration as part of the postwar order.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.258.d: The defeat of the Entente has left its possessions in Southeast Asia exposed. British Malaya will become the centre of a German East Asian administration, joined by any territories in Indochina and the Pacific already held by Germany.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.129.d: Egypt is currently an English de facto protectorate. However, it was part of the Ottoman empire for a very long time beforehand, and briefly an independent state under Muhammad Ali. What demands are to be made here? I suggest that we gain control of the Suez, personally, sir.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.129.a: Transfer the Suez to us, the Germans!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.129.b: Transfer the Suez to the Turks.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.130.d: You wish to leave Belgium as it was pre-war, minus casualties.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.156.d: Gibraltar is an important port for the British for their route to India, being the gateway to the mediterranian by which ships enter and leave the Suez.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.157.d: Gibraltar shall belong to whoever you selected, as displayed on the map!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.163.d: Malta, a chokepoint in the Mediterranean. Whoever controls it controls passage from the east to the west, and it is currently under british Suzerainity. What shall we do with it?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.164.d: Is this the fate of Malta you desire?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.242.t: The Second treaty of Frankfurt - The Franco-German Border
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.242.desc: The French claim on Alsace-Lorraine helped spark this war, and Bismarck was against annexing any land from the French. However, the French are in no position to bargain, and it seems that the German military have already made preperations to annex a strip of Lorraine from Nanzig to Briey-Longwy. Presumably, in the case of yet another war, these forts that the French built will be used against them...
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.242.a: We'll take only the strip of Lorraine.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.242.0: We'll take nothing, have the status quo of 1871 restored!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.242.b: Part of Lorraine and part of French Africa!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.242.d: Take as much as we can!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.244.d: With the defeat of the Greeks and the Serbs, lands once owned by them now lay open to others. The Bulgars in particular are keen on realizing their dream of Greater Bulgaria, and the Turks wish to secure their Aegean coast.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.244.a: At long last, Bulgaria has her place in the sun!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.244.b: Small pickings, but important ones nontheless.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.245.d: With the victory of the Central Powers over the Entente, we can now rein in the Balkans. If the Ottomans are so able, they will help us in maintaining stability.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.245.a: Very well, but what of the Bulgars?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.246.d: Dealing with the Kingdom of Italy, the treaty of Innsbruck dismantled African posessions and recognized the Dervish state as their de facto owner. Signed by all major participants of the recent war, it recognized the independence of the Dervish state, as well as the transfer of some territories such as the return of Rhodes to the Turks, and the transfer of Venice and Friuli to the Austrians.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.247.d: The French hold land that have a stronger association with the Italian peninsula either by history or by language. What shall we do with these territories?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.247.b: Let the French keep these lands.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.247.c: It would be prudent to give the Italians something...
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.248.d: Kuwait in southmost Iraq could be used as a strategic port by us however, it would likely not be as important now with us owning most of Middle Africa, though it wouldn't hurt, on the other hand we could always be fair and just and give it back to the Ottoman Empire whom would surely appreciate the return of this territory from British Imperialism.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.249.d: With the French having capitulated, they will be in no position to manage their colonies in Asia. These are very precarious and found on the other end of the world, and as much as we would like them for their rubber plantations, the Japanese also desire colonial posessions. We can make a long-term ally in the region should war erupt once more against the British by giving the Japanese Asian posessions despite losing the war.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.249.a: How about we seize it instead?
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.249.b: Let us make friends rather than enemies, for once.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.250.t: The fate of the German Pacific posessions
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.250.d: The Japanese have seized our posessions in the Pacific during the war, and are unwilling to return them. There is nothing in these islands anyway, and we absolutely cannot contest the United States' navy. However, Japan has an interest in them, and we could actually make a profit by ratifying a deal with Japan for these Islands.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.251.d: The Germans wish to recognize our posession of their pacific island colonies for a price, a very reasonable one.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.251.b: We already own them, we need no payment.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.252.t: The Germans demand the return of the Islands.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.252.d: The Germans demand the return of their pacific colonies!
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.253.d: It seems like we will have to take these islands by force.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.254.d: After several months of brutal negotiations a final treaty has been agreed upon between our government in an effort to stop further advances by the Germanand Austro-Hungarian forces. According to the treaty, we will default on all of Imperial Russia's commitments ot the Triple Entente alliance. In the treaty we will cede all of the Baltic States to Germany meant to become German vassal states under German princelings, recognize the independence of Ukraine, cede Byelorussia, cede Kars Oblast in the South Caucasus to the Ottoman Turks. The terms are far above harsh and it is even said the German negotiator has been shocked by the harshness.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.255.d: The Swiss were historically neutral, yet they speak a dialect of German that they simply deny is German. We could integrate them slowly, but we could also just leave them to the status quo.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.255.b: The Swiss shall remain neutral, we only wanted to invade the French...
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.256.d: With our participation on the German side of the war, honoring the Triple Alliance, we have also been able to claim some spoils of war! We are to recieve the Tunisian protectorate so wrongfully denied to us, as well as Savoy, Nice, and the Alps in between them. The lands up to the Rhone are to be demilitarized on the French side of the border.
loc.kaiserschlachtvictory.256.a: The dream of Italia Irridenta is unfinished still..

loc.welcome.1.d:
Welcome my friend, how is your day going? You have chosen the 1910 scenario, it is the calm before the storm. Have fun. 

 If you find any bugs and make sure to report it in the bugs discussion so I can fix it. 

 Credits: Sanaa Ripper (OGs:Lev Slav, Misterjay and Knifepony)
loc.welcome.1.a: Lets get this show on the road
loc.welcome.2.d:
Welcome my friend, how is your day going? You have chosen the 1914 scenario, get ready because my insticts (SPOILER ALERT) are telling me something is brewing in Europe and a certain Franz Ferdinand might get assassinated lighting the fuse to the Balkan Powderkeg. 

 If you find an bugs make sure to report it in the bugs discussion so I can fix it 

 Credits: Sanaa Ripper (OGs:Lev Slav, Misterjay and Knifepony)
loc.welcome.2.a: Uh oh! It can't be...not Franz Ferdinand!
loc.welcome.3.d:
Welcome my friend, how is your day going? You have chosen the 1918 scenario, the war has now gone on for four long years, but not all is bad for the Central Powers whom have knocked out Russia, this means they can focus all of their eastern divisions on the western front giving them numerical superiority. This has prompted Erich Ludendorff to plan the 'Kaiserschlacht' otherwise known as the Kaiser's Battle or Spring Offensive. But on the inside the Central Powers are slowly falling apart, desertion, war exhaustion, and the blockade is all taking its toll and they will either win quick or lose quick. 

 If you find any bugs make sure to report them in the bugs discussion, thanks in advance helps everyone out. 

 Credits: Sanaa Ripper (OGs:Lev Slav, Misterjay and Knifepony)
loc.welcome.41.d: Hello and welcome to the new Endsieg scenario. This is the first new scenario done by MisterJay, and will be expanded upon greatly. This scenario is best played in duos, with both a Soviet Union and a Germany! If you are playing this solo, I suggest playing this on hard mode. Good luck and make the Führer proud!
loc.welcome.41.a: So you're saying I can actually win?
loc.welcome.4.d:
Welcome my friend, how is your day going? You have chosen the 1943 scenario, currently Germany has gathered its forces for its (historically) last major offensive on the eastern front at the Kursk Salient, however the Soviets who have learned of this Operation (Citadel) in advance have made efforts to entrench themselves heavily. In Italy, the allies have landed taking most of sicily and the Italians are on the fence between the Allies and the Axis. Japan has reached its zenith in Asia with the U.S. starting to push down hard against them, however they are relatively successful in China. 

 If you find any bugs make sure to report them in the bugs discussion, thanks in advance helps everyone out. 

 Credits: Sanaa Ripper (OGs:Lev Slav, Misterjay and Knifepony) and Matteo Bosso for the new OOB's
loc.welcome.5.d:
Welcome my friend, how is your day going? You have chosen the June 20th, 1944 scenario, currently Germany is under attack from the east and the west. In the west the allies have landed in Normandy bringing in more troops by the day, in the east the Soviets have launched Operation Bagration pushing hard against the Germans in Belarus. In Asia Japan is falling back with the U.S. making signficant success island hopping towards the Japanese mainland and liberating allied territory with Japan still having a strong hold on China. Indeed this is the fate of the gods (Götterdämmerung). 

 If you find any bugs make sure to report them in the bugs discussion, thanks in advance, helps everyone. 

 Credits: Sanaa Ripper (OGs:Lev Slav, Misterjay and Knifepony) and Matteo Bosso for the new OOB's
loc.welcome.5.a: What shall be the fate of the gods?
loc.welcome.6.d:
Welcome my friend, how is your day going? You have chosen the December 16, 1944 scenario, on the Western Front German troops under the cover of a fog (which is thankfully put the Allied Airforce out of action) have started their one last gamble starting a major (surprise) counter offensive with hopes to cut off the Allies by taking Antwerp and destroying four of the allied Armies. In the east the Red Army has just barely entered Germany, "liberating" Romania, Bulgaria, and a chunk of Yugoslavia pushing into Hungary, the time has now come, the final fight for the Fatherland. Is it to late for Germany? In Asia the Americans have just recently landed in the Phillipines and the Japanese navy has been practically wiped out with a few remenants remaining, the hold on China is still strong. 

 If you find any bugs make sure to report them in the bugs discussion, thanks in advance, helps everyone. 

 Credits: Sanaa Ripper (OGs:Lev Slav, Misterjay and Knifepony) and Matteo Bosso for the new OOB's
loc.welcome.6.a: The Axis are on their knees
loc.welcome.7.d:
Welcome my friend, how is your day going? You have daringly (if you play as Germany, what are you going to play the Soviet Union? Seriously if you do...just why?) chosen the 1945 scenario. On both fronts the Germans have been heavily pushed back but Goebbels calls for the Endsieg continue and the Fuhrer none-the-less continues to be filled with hope for a chance at turning the war around. In Asia, the Americans are now fighting a winning battle at Iwo Jima, right next to mainland Japan, which has now been bombed to bits. 

 If you find any bugs make sure to report it in the bugs discussion so I can fix it, thanks in advance. 

 Credits: Sanaa Ripper (OGs:Lev Slav, Misterjay and Knifepony) and Matteo Bosso for the new OOB's
loc.welcome.8.d:
Welcome my friend, how is your day going? You have chosen the 1948, alternate history scenario where Germany has to an extent won the Second World War. Following the decisive German victory at Moscow and then Stalingrad, Germany and the Soviet Union reluctantly agreed to a treaty. In Italy the Allies pushed for a major invasion prompting the Italian King, Vittorio Emanuel to switch sides with the Allies initial success, as a result the Germans quickly beat back the Italian troops occupying Montenegro, Albania, and Greece setting up their own client states before setting up a loyal Italian Social Republic headed by Benito Mussolini and defeating the allied invasion. With no side able to break the dead lock in the next years an armistice, with no treaty, was agreed upon in 1945, a peace without victory. Japan was not included, and thus was defeated that same year. Britain remains in a war economy, ready for any attack, and the allies are seemingly plotting for another major invasion perhaps with the peace being unstable. 

 If you find any bugs make sure to report them in the bugs discussion, thanks in advance, helps everyone. 

 Credits: Sanaa Ripper (OGs:Lev Slav, Misterjay and Knifepony)
loc.welcome.9.d: Choose whether your country uses the ration system. You can disable daily ration consumption and shortage penalties, receive free rations, or use the standard rules. You can change this setting later from the Cheat Menu.
loc.welcome.9.a: Turn off rations for my units.
loc.welcome.9.b: Just give me some free rations already!
loc.welcome.10.d: Hello and fellow player of Endsieg. This mod has always been known as a \"difficult\" mod, and we are here to change that! Endsieg will always keep the same nature, but we wanted to provide something to the more casual player. Hereby our new cheat system!
loc.welcome.11.d: Here you get to choose what difficulty to play with! Note that you can not remove this buff once you start playing so choose wisely.
loc.welcome.11.b: Who do you think I am? Just give me normal difficulty!
loc.welcome.12.d: Endsieg is sometimes a difficult mod in the reinforce rate department. Here you can choose to upgrade that!
loc.welcome.12.dee: Just give me that reinforcement rate
loc.welcome.13.d: For the people that don't like scripted peacedeals. Make sure you click this if you plan to play as (or against) the German Empire. Do note that this is not the way Endsieg was intended, and if you plan to transition into WW2 this will be a big mess. NOTE: This is still a WIP, so do not expect EVERY scripted peacedeal to be fixed. Please leave a comment on the Steam Workshop if you find one that isn't.
loc.welcome.13.a: No scripted peace deals for me.
loc.welcome.13.b: I want the full Endsieg experience.
loc.welcome.131.desc: Endsieg offers a decent arrangement of conveniences. Currently, you can pick from Scripted Peacedeals, improved game speed and difficulty. To select or change your decision simply pick an option. To bring this menu back up, click on the question mark under fuel and press settings.
loc.welcome.131.a: I want to disable scripted peacedeals!
loc.welcome.131.c: I want to change the difficulty!
loc.welcome.14.d: If your PC is not mother's finest, choose this option. This event will annex South American countries and Tibet and Butan into nearby countries to reduce lag. Note that some events will not work properly and some might not happen at all. If you have problems please tell us on the Steam Workshop.
loc.welcome.14.a: I am playing Endsieg on a toaster ;(
loc.welcome.14.b: I have one of those fancy gaming PC's
loc.welcome.28.desc: Welcome to the new §BSecret Corner§! of Endsieg! Today, we have a couple new interesting things for you to enable... Right now, you have the power to...
loc.welcome.28.d: Do nothing, I don't like this one bit...
loc.welcome.29.desc: For a long time, we have had questions about war exhaustion and why it isn't enabled for all countries. For a long time now, we've said its for balance reasons. We stand by that point, but we are also a proponent of player choice, and hereby give you the option to turn on War Exhaustion for certain/all countries. I want to enable War Exhaustion for...
loc.welcome.29.b: All the nations in Germany's faction!
loc.welcome.29.c: All the nations in France's faction!
loc.welcome.29.d: All the nations in the Soviet Union's faction!
loc.welcome.29.e: No one else. I'm tired enough as is.
loc.welcome.32.t: Its WW2 and I have a whole bunch of bugs!
loc.welcome.32.desc: I can't see my units in WW2! If you can't see your units: unpause for a second. This is a result of the whitepeacing system Paradox uses. \n\nI don't have a focus tree in WW2! This is new to Endsieg: We now have WW1 and WW2 focus trees combined, you have to scroll down for the WW2 part. In the future (read: very far away future) we will be adding an Interwar tree to this as well.
loc.welcome.42.d: Hello and welcome to the Stalingrad Scenario. Have fun playing this brand new scenario. It is my first scenario and bugs can occure. I would be thankful for every reported error/bug.                                                                                                                                                                                        Credits: Sanaa Ripper (OGs:Lev Slav, Misterjay and Knifepony)
loc.welcome.43.d: Greetings. Welcome to the 1916 Scenario. This Scenario is in an early stage of development. More Stuff will be added in the Future. \n\n Credits: Sanaa Ripper (OGs:Lev Slav, Misterjay and Knifepony)
